Kunpeng). ### Research - [x] I have searched the [[pandas] tag]( on StackOverflow for similar questions. - [x] I have asked my usage related question on [StackOverflow]( ### Link to question on StackOverflow None ### Question about pandas Hi pandas maintainers, I’m working on improving Python data ecosystem performance on ARM64 servers (Huawei Kunpeng, also Ampere/Neoverse/Graviton-class). I’d like to ask about pandas’ approach to *ongoing ARM64 performance monitoring* and whether the project would welcome additional ARM64 benchmarking coverage. ### Why this matters Performance changes may impact architectures differently. If we only run regular benchmarks on x86, ARM64 regressions or widening gaps can slip in as the codebase evolves—even when changes are well-intentioned. pandas already uses ASV and has runner automation, so adding ARM64 could be a natural extension to help: - catch ARM64 regressions early (nightly/periodic), - understand cross-arch impact (x86 improves, ARM64 regresses, or vice versa), - provide reproducible data for optimization work and PR reviews. ### Questions for maintainers 1) Does pandas currently run ASV benchmarks on ARM64 on a regular schedule? If yes, where are the results published? 2) If not, would you be open to adding an ARM64 runner (or accepting externally-run ARM64 results)? 3) What is the preferred workflow for adding a new benchmark environment? - via existing runner infrastructure (if applicable), - or via a separate community-managed runner that publishes a dashboard? 4) Would maintainers value tracking ARM64 vs x86 ratios (to detect widening gaps), or just per-arch regressions? 5) Are there priority benchmark groups you’d like to ensure are covered on ARM64 (groupby, merge/join, indexing, IO, strings, datetime, etc.)? ### What I can contribute (long-term, bare-metal) - Access to stable **bare-metal** ARM64 machines (Kunpeng), dedicated to benchmarking (not VMs, not shared workloads). - Reproducible environment controls (CPU frequency/power policy, BIOS settings, kernel, pinned toolchain), so results are stable and comparable. - I’m willing to take **long-term ownership of runner operations** (automation, maintenance, upgrades, incident handling), so this won’t become a temporary/unmaintained runner. - Investigation and actionable reports for regressions, with potential fixes upstream. ### Operational commitments (so maintainers can trust sustainability) - **Cadence** - Nightly run on (latest SHA each night). - Weekly run on the latest maintenance/release branch(es) if useful. - Optional: monthly “deep run” (more repetitions / expanded suite) to confirm trends. - **Reproducibility** - Dedicated bare-metal host, minimal background noise. - Pinned OS/kernel/toolchain; documented dependency versions (NumPy/Arrow/optional deps as applicable). - Fixed CPU governor / power mode and recorded machine metadata each run. - **Publishing** - Publish an ASV dashboard (or whichever mechanism pandas prefers) with a clearly named environment (e.g., ). - Keep logs/metadata for debugging (dependency versions, build flags, ASV machine info). - **Retention** - Keep raw results for **≥ 2 years** to support trend analysis across releases. - **Regression policy** - Use a triage threshold (example: >3–5% sustained regression on key groups, confirmed via rerun) to open actionable follow-ups. - Confirm regressions with reruns to reduce noise. - **Failure handling** - Automatic retry on transient failures; alert on repeated failures with an owner/contact. - **Continuity** - If I can’t maintain the runner, I’ll provide advance notice and help transfer scripts/docs to another maintainer/volunteer. Happy to follow whatever process you prefer. If this belongs in a different repo (benchmark infra/runner), please redirect me. Thanks! <Your Name / Org> <Contact / GitHub handle> (ARM64 HW summary: Kunpeng model, cores, memory, OS/kernel; optional)

title: PERF: loc/iloc setitem with list-of-lists unnecessarily round-trips through object array
text: PERF: loc/iloc setitem with list-of-lists unnecessarily round-trips through object array. ### Pandas version checks - [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [x] I have confirmed this issue exists on the [latest version]( of pandas. - [x] I have confirmed this issue exists on the main branch of pandas. ### Reproducible Example When using (or df.iloc) with a 2D list-of-lists on a mixed-dtype DataFrame, two things happen that are unnecessarily slow: 1. np.ndim(value) constructs a temporary array just to check dimensionality 2. round-trips through an object array For a list-of-lists, the full sequence is: - np.array(value, dtype=object) — O(n) element-by-element boxing into Python objects - value[:, i] — slice an object column - is_object_dtype(...) → True - value_col.tolist() — convert right back to a Python list So the data goes list → object array → list for every column, which is pure waste. Reproducible example Expected Output Possible fix - Replace with a cheap helper that uses getattr(value, "ndim", None) for arrays and isinstance(value[0], (list, np.ndarray)) for plain lists — avoids the first temporary array construction. - In , when value is a list, extract columns directly with [row[i] for row in value] instead of converting to an object array and back. This eliminates the entire list → object array → .tolist() round-trip. ### Installed Versions <details> INSTALLED VERSIONS ------------------ commit : 4ce8e340d5b579c11290d855a7e99e646289555d python : 3.12.2 python-bits : 64 OS : Darwin OS-release : 25.3.0 Version : Darwin Kernel Version 25.3.0: Wed Jan 28 20:47:03 PST 2026; root:xnu-12377.81.4~5/RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 machine : arm64 processor : arm byteorder : little LC_ALL : None LANG : C.UTF-8 LOCALE : None.UTF-8 pandas : 3.0.0+29.g4ce8e340d5.dirty numpy : 2.3.5 dateutil : 2.9.0.post0 pip : 25.3 Cython : 3.2.3 sphinx : 8.2.3 IPython : 9.8.0 adbc-driver-postgresql: None adbc-driver-sqlite : None bs4 : 4.14.3 bottleneck : 1.6.0 fastparquet : 2025.12.0 fsspec : 2025.12.0 html5lib : 1.1 hypothesis : 6.148.9 gcsfs : 2025.12.0 jinja2 : 3.1.6 lxml.etree : 6.0.2 matplotlib : 3.10.8 numba : 0.63.1 numexpr : 2.14.1 odfpy : None openpyxl : 3.1.5 psycopg2 : 2.9.11 pymysql : 1.4.6 pyarrow : 22.0.0 pyiceberg : 0.10.0 pyreadstat : 1.3.2 pytest : 9.0.2 python-calamine : None pytz : 2025.2 pyxlsb : 1.0.10 s3fs : 2025.12.0 scipy : 1.16.3 sqlalchemy : 2.0.45 tables : 3.10.2 tabulate : 0.9.0 xarray : 2025.12.0 xlrd : 2.0.2 xlsxwriter : 3.2.9 zstandard : 0.25.0 qtpy : None pyqt5 : None </details> ### Prior Performance _No response_

This would be a win perf-wise, but the downside would be that the result.index.dtype would no longer be commutative, which I think in previous discussions we've considered desirable. \* We could actually improve perf even more in cases with a non-None by short-circuiting in cases with matching freq and matching . ### Expected Behavior N/A. ### Installed Versions <details> Replace this line with the output of pd.show_versions() </details>

title: ENH: Vectorization (e.g. SIMD) in pandas' Hashtable Operations for Performance Improvement
text: ENH: Vectorization (e.g. SIMD) in pandas' Hashtable Operations for Performance Improvement. ### Feature Type - [x] Adding new functionality to pandas - [x] Changing existing functionality in pandas - [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas ### Problem Description I’ve seen related issues around alignment and vectorization (e.g., #3146 ) and understand pandas prioritizes index alignment and general-purpose data structures. However, this question is focused specifically on whether SIMD or other low-level vectorization techniques have been considered or intentionally avoided in the internal hashtable engine. ### Feature Description Hi pandas team, I'm wondering what the current stance is in the community regarding the possibility of introducing vectorized (e.g., SIMD-based) operations into pandas' hashtable infrastructure (e.g., used in groupby, factorize, categorical operations, etc.). Hashtable lookups and insertions are often performance-critical paths, especially when dealing with large, high-cardinality data. With modern CPUs supporting SIMD instructions (e.g., AVX2, AVX-512), has there been any past discussion or interest in exploring: - SIMD acceleration for probing and inserting into hash tables? - Potential trade-offs in code complexity, portability, and maintainability? - Alignment with pandas’ reliance on NumPy, PyArrow, or other external backends for low-level performance? Would love to know the core team’s view — especially if this is considered an area for experimentation, or whether existing architectural decisions rule this out. In we deliberately return a *shallow* copy (a new object with a view on the original buffers) of the backing array. For correctness, this is fine since pyarrow arrays are immutable, so copying should be unnecessary. However, it does mean that after a , you'll still have a reference back to the original buffer. If the output of the is the only one with a reference to the original buffer, then it won't be garbage collected. Consider: Maybe this is fine. We can probably figure out some workaround in dask (in this case we're making an empty dataframe object as a kind of Schema object. We can probably do something other than ). title: PERF: Possible Memory Leak when Importing Parquet File with PyArrow Engine in Pandas
text: PERF: Possible Memory Leak when Importing Parquet File with PyArrow Engine in Pandas. ### Pandas version checks - [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [X] I have confirmed this issue exists on the [latest version]( of pandas. - [ ] I have confirmed this issue exists on the main branch of pandas. ### Reproducible Example **Description** We've identified a memory leak when importing Parquet files into Pandas DataFrames using the PyArrow engine. The issue occurs specifically during the conversion from Arrow to Pandas objects, as memory is not released even after deleting the DataFrame and invoking garbage collection. **Key findings:** - **No leak with PyArrow alone:** When using PyArrow to read Parquet without converting to Pandas (i.e., no _.to_pandas()_), the memory leak does not occur. - **Leak with _.to_pandas()_:** The memory leak appears during the conversion from Arrow to Pandas, suggesting the problem is tied to this process. - **No issue with Fastparquet or Polars:** Fastparquet and Polars (even with PyArrow) do not exhibit this memory issue, reinforcing that the problem is in Pandas’ handling of Arrow data. **Reproduction Code** **Observations:** - **Garbage Collection:** Despite invoking the garbage collector multiple times, memory allocated to the Python process keeps increasing when _.to_pandas()_ is used, indicating improper memory release during the conversion. - **Direct Use of PyArrow:** When we import the data directly using PyArrow (without converting to Pandas), the memory usage remains stable, showing that the problem originates in the Arrow-to-Pandas conversion process. - **Manual Memory Release (ctypes):** The only reliable way we have found to release the memory is by manually calling _malloc_trim(0)_ via ctypes. However, we believe this is not a proper solution and that memory management should be handled internally by Pandas. **OS environment** _Icon name: computer-vm Chassis: vm Virtualization: microsoft Operating System: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.10 (Ootpa) CPE OS Name: cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:8::baseos Kernel: Linux 4.18.0-553.16.1.el8_10.x86_64 Architecture: x86-64_ **Affected Versions** _pandas==2.2.2 pandas==2.2.3 Latest development version (as of writing)_ **Conclusion** The issue seems to occur during the conversion from Arrow to Pandas, rather than being a problem within PyArrow itself. Given that memory is only released by manually invoking _malloc_trim(0)_, we suspect there is a problem with how Pandas handles memory management when working with Arrow data. This issue does not arise when using Fastparquet or Polars, further indicating that it is specific to the Pandas-Arrow interaction. title: QST: Consistently apply Welford Method and Kahan Summation in roll_xxx functions
text: QST: Consistently apply Welford Method and Kahan Summation in roll_xxx functions. ### Research - [X] I have searched the [[pandas] tag]( on StackOverflow for similar questions. - [X] I have asked my usage related question on [StackOverflow]( ### Link to question on StackOverflow ### Question about pandas For the following functions: 1.def nancorr 2.cdef void add_var 3.cdef void add_skew 4.cdef void add_mean It appears that both the Welford method and Kahan summation are taken into account. However, for second-order functions like correlation and variance, only the Welford method is used without Kahan summation for the means (meanx or meany). For third-order functions like skewness, only Kahan summation for the naive one-pass algorithm is employed without using Welford. My question is: How does the Pandas community decide which method to use for stable precision? If our goal is to achieve the highest possible stability, it seems that all these functions should utilize a combination of Welford and Kahan methods. Could you please clarify the rationale behind these choices?

title: API/PERF: when to check for mismatched tzs/awareness in array_to_datetime
text: API/PERF: when to check for mismatched tzs/awareness in array_to_datetime. If we pass mixed-tz datetime objects, we do a tz-match check at each step of the loop inside / (specifically in ). If we pass mixed-tz strings, the analogous check happens outside the loop. (per #55693 we currently dont have mixed-type checks) Eventually these checks should be shared, which means we need to decide on the in-loop or after-loop versions. Three differences for users are 1) the in-loop version adds the f"at position {i}" to the exception message. 2) the in-loop version can be handled differently based on errors=coerce/ignore 3) the in-loop version is in-loop and so presumably incurs a performance penalty The errors=coerce/ignore part is the API part of the issue (though xref #54467 for deprecating ignore). I think it is very likely that the original intent of coerce was to handle invalid individual items, not invalid combinations of items, so would be OK with the API change that would come with moving this outside the loop.

title: ENH: An option to stop appending .0 to strings if null is present in json
text: ENH: An option to stop appending .0 to strings if null is present in json. ### Feature Type - [ ] Adding new functionality to pandas - [X] Changing existing functionality in pandas - [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas ### Problem Description I sometimes deal with data that stores number-id's as integers and not as strings, and they also contain null values in that number-id column. When I load this data into pandas I would like to be able to specify "treat this column as string". Currently, if there is a null value present Pandas seems to interpret that whole column as float and add ".0" to the end of each number before returning it as a string valued column. example how it currently works: I would like it to return 1 and 2 instead of 1.0 and 2.0 ### Feature Description I perhaps missinterpreted the argument "dtype" in df = pd.DataFrame(jdata,dtype=str) So there could be "force_as_dtype" per column, which could stop the conversion into float before converting to string. I tried tracing where the conversion between types is made, and from what I could find: This "force_as_dtype" per column could be passed on through the "_homogenize" function in pandas/core/internals/construction.py ,and through the "fast multiget" function in pandas/_libs/lib, to finally be used to stop the conversion in the "mayby_convert_objects" function in pandas/_libs/lib. ### Alternative Solutions There exist methods to clean the data before entering it into pandas. And it is quite easy to remove the ".0" from the column after it has been created. ### Additional Context _No response_

This is of course related to the enhancement allowing non-ns units to datetimes, see e.g.: - - **Questions** 1. Given the fact that deprecations of types have already begun, it would be useful to understand what the expected roadmap for is. Is it expected that it will be removed as suggested in #54235? Is there a plan for how to move forward on the "sticking points" listed there (especially the missing units: Week-with anchor, quarter, Year-with-anchor)? 2. The current deprecation of business day periods in #53446 now requires bifurcation of code from to in the special case of business days - if you are using s, you can't wholesale switch to s yet (at least if you have e.g. Quarters), but you also can no longer stick with just s. **Tentative request** To me, it would make sense to revert the deprecation of the BDay dtype until there is a more comprehensive roadmap for types and a path to make a more wholesale switch. But my apologies if I missed something fundamental here about why that deprecation is important in itself.

But instead it is: "'Good Faith' Renewal Price Adjustment's", which is not valid for what I need because field values surrounded by double quotes are invalid for insert statements. It's fine if it was a column name, but this is not that. I am new to pandas and I've looked around and haven't found anything about this. Is there a parameter or a different way of doing this that will properly escape and quote this string? Thanks!

text: BUG: segfault when using read_csv and repeatedly accessing / renaming DataFrame.columns. ### Pandas version checks - [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version]( of pandas. - [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas. ### Reproducible Example ### Issue Description Crash always happens on method of df.columns repeated calls with column name reassignments. When this happens, simply calling df.columns enough times will cause the segfault. All variations of engine types for read_csv (c, python, and python-fwf) are reproducible with no observable difference between any engine type when using the outer for loop forcing thousands of iterations. _Without_ the outer for loop, the python engine performs the best with the lowest chance of reproducing the crash. python-fwf and c perform significantly worse, with python-fwf marginally less likely to crash. Initially found on python 3.6 pandas 1.1.5, also reproduced on python 3.8 and latest version of pandas 1.4.1 The file contents of the CSV seem to be irrelevant. In my case, it had four columns with one row of data. In this example, the columns will initially be changed to something else (on first iteration of outer loop), but subsequent loop executions will rename it to the same values. The outer loop is not necessary to reproduce the crash, but it makes it guaranteed to happen. Note, replacing the inner for loop with the commented out lines will cause the issue to become unreproducible, even with the outer loop. On the other hand, simply commenting out the three column value assignments at the start of the outer loop will make the issue much harder to reproduce, but still possible (it can survive 10000 iterations about 80% of the time). When it does segfault in this case, it does so on the final line of the example. title: ENH: sorted numpy array of datetime64 as pandas.DataFrame.index without copy-conversion
text: ENH: sorted numpy array of datetime64 as pandas.DataFrame.index without copy-conversion. #### Is your feature request related to a problem? Presently, using any array as a index results in copy-conversion to an array of . In my particular use case, I would like to construct a from existing arrays as a view using an existing sorted array as index view, with no copy-conversion. That works for arrays which don't get copied, but my array gets copy-converted to an array of when used as an index. I would like to use a sorted array as a index as is, with no copy-conversion. #### Describe the solution you'd like One solution can be a new index type that uses an array of sorted as is, instead of converting it to an index type with elements. Another solution is a new index type that uses any sorted array as index as is, when . These indexes can use binary search for sub-linear complexity index lookup. Binary search lookup may not be as fast as a hashtable lookup, but the former doesn't require constructing any extra data structures. Any sorted array should be usable as an index with binary lookup and no copy-conversion. #### API breaking implications No breaking of existing APIs should be necessary. These can be new index types implementing existing index APIs, which requires no changes to any existing API user code. title: QST: Is Series in pandas size mutable?
text: QST: Is Series in pandas size mutable?. ### - [X] I have searched the [[pandas] tag]( on StackOverflow for similar questions. - [X] I have asked my usage related question on [StackOverflow]( ### Link to question on StackOverflow ### Question about pandas >>>s a 4.0 b 4.0 c 8.0 d 9.0 f NaN dtype: float64`>>>s a 4.0 b 4.0 c 8.0 d 9.0 f NaN dtype: float64 >>>s.shape (5,) s.drop('f',inplace=True) >>> s a 4.0 b 4.0 c 8.0 d 9.0 dtype: float64 >>> s.size 4 >>> s['f']=9 >>> s a 4.0 b 4.0 c 8.0 d 9.0 f 9.0 dtype: float64 >>> s['b']=100 >>> s a 4.0 b 100.0 c 8.0 d 9.0 f 9.0 dtype: float64 >>> s['g']=200 >>> s.size 6 Please go through the above Python commands that imply that Pandas Series are also size mutable. The size of given series is initially 5 Then I delete one element s.drop('f',inplace=True), so the size of the Series will be 4. Then I again assign a new variable s['f']=9 and s['g']=200, then the size of the Series is 6 now. It means Series is also size mutable.

title: BUG: inconsistent behaviour when grouping DataFrame by week and month, as compared to minutes, hours and days??
text: BUG: inconsistent behaviour when grouping DataFrame by week and month, as compared to minutes, hours and days??. In computer science, we always try to design algorithms and procedures in a logically consistent manner so that other people can follow easily without making wrong assumptions. For example, when we group dates into intervals, for every group we can choose to use either the left or the right boundary to label that group. So if you decide to choose the left timestamp to label every interval, then you should do it for all types of intervals. However, this is not so in Pandas. As you can see above, when grouping into seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks and months respectively: - for seconds, minutes, hours and days, the group time label lies to the left of the sample - but for weeks, months and years, the group time label lies to the right the sample, what is even worse is that the boundary does not align to the beginning of the next interval, rather, it aligns to the beginning of the last day in the interval, which is even more weird (does it mean the last day of a month/year belongs to the next month/year??? absolutely non-sense) In general, we can group dates by arbitrary interval, e.g., 10.5 days or 1.5 weeks (some astronomical events monitoring can leads to such use case). This inconsistency is going to cause errors in applications based on human assumption because who the hell will know that for weeks, months, and years, the library decide to do it differently from the rest??

title: BUG: Dataframe structure is incompatible across minor versions 1.0.5 -> 1.1.0+, violating semver rules
text: BUG: Dataframe structure is incompatible across minor versions 1.0.5 -> 1.1.0+, violating semver rules. - [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas. - [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas. --- 1. Create a DF in Pandas 1.1.0+ ![image]( 2. Load in a different computer/system/subsystem with a different Pandas version like 1.0.5 ![image]( #### Problem description A core objects structure should be compatible across minor versions; which [via the semver standard]( > Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, increment the: > > MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes, > ***MINOR version when you add functionality in a backwards compatible manner, and*** \[emphasis added\] > PATCH version when you make backwards compatible bug fixes. > Additional labels for pre-release and build metadata are available as extensions to the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format. #### Expected Output A serialized dataframe should be compatible across versions. - Serialization to basic objects should be backwards compatible, in such a way that all reasonable serializations should "just work" (eg, joblib, pickle, hdf5 ...) - If it cannot be in all cases, native write functions like should handle the backwards-compatibility work, at least via flag. - If it cannot be at all, the _major_ version should be incremented as per semver, since this breaks backwards compatibility. - If the major version cannot be incremented, Pandas shouldn't pretend to follow semantic versioning and should use a version number that is plainly and obviously not semantic versioning, like Ubuntu's whimsical named versions. #### Output of pd.show_versions() <details> Writer system: Reader system: </details>

text: Pandas strftime function prints unix epoch time in local TZ instead of UTC. I'm trying to convert a given date and time to unix epoch time using Pandas. However, when pulling my code onto my Mac laptop and running locally has resulted in what was unexpected to me at first: that the above code prints off a unix epoch time 7 hours in advance, or a string reading "1609484400". Running the date command on my Mac OS terminal gives me the time in MST, which is where I live, instead of UTC like the remote linux machine I pulled my code from. MST is 7 hours behind UTC so I assume that Pandas is trying to account for the MST time recorded on my laptop and doing some kind of internal conversion. I figure that I need to specify that the time I'm inputing is UTC, so I tried that both with "utc=True" for as well as "tz='UTC'" for . No dice though, as I still get a return value of "1609484400". I want to support customers that use the GitHub Copilot service, or host their own model locally, or pay for a cloud service, but all through the same UI. Right now, if you want to use your own models, you need a new extension (like Continue) which adds a new UI and has unique standards compared to the Chat UI. What I would really like to see is those vendors, instead of creating a new webview to create their own chat window, I'd love to be able to re-use the VS Code Chat UI/UX with other services/providers that can be registered through my extension. Similar to the language APIs, which allow extensions to implement language-server interfaces so the UI is the same across multiple languages, I would love that for the AI UI (Chat window, asking questions in code, etc) also. Something like or , which would then have callbacks. Then, after your provider has been registered, I might see it show up in the family selection list in the Chat window. ![Image]( I really don't want to see multiple extensions re-implementing their own chat webviews. I would like for it to be standardized in the UI for extensions to be able to add to. Under '[Should I use a webview?]( in the VS Code docs, it says: > they should also be used sparingly and only when VS Code's native API is inadequate This is an area where the API is inadequate and as more vendors are building extensions, it'd be better if we all standardized (like the language server APIs).

title: Explorer refresh does not show latest data of the file system provider
text: Explorer refresh does not show latest data of the file system provider. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> ### Define Type ### Use ### Why ![image]( When I click the refresh button, it will only trigger the of and will not re-request the data of the file tree. My understanding of is that it does not pay attention to the source of the data it uses and when the data is requested. It only pays attention to the implementation of its own readFile, watch and other functions. When the FileSystemService of vscode executes related functions, it will call provider corresponding functions. This is true for most scenarios, but for refresh operations (especially for Web scenarios), just re-reading the folder (without re-requesting the data) after the refresh operation has no effect. Therefore, it is best to provide a refresh function that allows the provider to re-perform its own fetching operation, wait for the end, then let the file system re-read the data of the file tree, and then re-render the file tree. is not a good example because it installs the git extension by default and has button to get the latest data. title: Show Windows taskbar icon overlay for the currently opened directory/project/solution
text: Show Windows taskbar icon overlay for the currently opened directory/project/solution. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> When working with multiple directories/projects/solutions in parallel, there are multiple VSCode windows open. When trying to activate the correct window from another app in the foreground, it's hard to pick the right window. The Windows taskbar defaults to combining/grouping those app icons into a single button for all windows, which is the first thing in my way. Luckily this can be disabled so I have two or more VSCode icons on my taskbar. Still, all of them look exactly the same. It's impossible to tell them apart and pick the right window from there. (When hovering an icon with the mouse cursor, a window preview appears after some delay. While its thumbnail content is useless as always because indistinguishable, it does have the title there. But it's annoyingly slow to wait for these thumbnails and then again for them to disappear.) In ancient versions, the taskbar still included the window title but somehow all platforms have moved away from that long ago. Sad story. There exists an [extension for Visual Studio up to 2019]( and a [Windhawk mod for current versions]( that looks for an .editoricon.ico or .png file in the current solution directory and adds that as an overlay icon to the corresponding taskbar icon. The links above contain screenshots of that. This has proven to be super helpful in Visual Studio. After reading up how extensions work in VSCode (I avoid spelling it out in full because it's confusing for all search engines and most users) I believe that this is impossible to achieve with the limited extensibility API in VSCode. Extensions are hosted in a separate process (which can be overcome) but I couldn't manage to install the ffi package to an extension (or anywhere). Native Windows API functions are required for this feature. Easy to use from C# but extremely hard from JavaScript. My theoretical plan how to implement this is as an extension: 1. Create a VSCode extension that is notified when a directory is loaded that contains a file like 2. Call native Win32 API functions through [ffi]( 1. Determine the current process ID 2. Find parent processes as long as they're from the same program file (code.exe) 3. Get the main window handle of that top parent process (Process Hacker can do this, not sure about how easily it's implemented right now) 4. Call the functions to set the taskbar overlay icon from what we've loaded from the directory (not sure if this works from foreign/child processes; also, this seems to use some COM features actually, couldn't find out right now) Is there any chance such an extension could be built? Or better yet, that this feature could be integrated in VSCode itself? I'm not sure about other platforms than Windows but they might also have such features for overlay icons.

As #147746 points out, commands run in different contexts can have different meanings. E.g. when a 'Delete' command is applied to a tree node via a context menu, the context is a single item and the command is usually spelled 'Delete' or 'Delete {singular form}'. When that same command is run from the command palette, it might provide a pick list and support multiple items and so the command is spelled 'Delete {plural form}'. Example: In this example, a right-click on a node in the view shows 'Delete Samples' rather than 'Delete'. It's possible to create multiple commands as a work-around, but this is quite a bit more complexity as the additional commands must be removed from the command palette, in addition to the additional configuration. And this just to modify the title shown in a particular context. I'm not sure if the current behavior is intentional or not so I'm opening this as a feature request.

title: How to get the target process pid when using debugger to run a program in Git Bash terminal
text: How to get the target process pid when using debugger to run a program in Git Bash terminal. - VS Code Version: 1.67.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 In Java debugger extension, we use terminal to launch Java application by default. Now we have a feature requirement to get the Java process pid running in terminal. Since the RunInTerminal DAP just returns the current shellProcessId, we try to use the shellProcessId as parent pid and get the target Java process under its process tree. This approach works well on Windows PowerShell and cmd, where the launched Java process is a descendant of the shell process. However, this approach fails when using Git Bash as the default terminal, because the launched Java process is no longer a descendant process of the shell process. In fact, the parent of java process is a process of "/user/bin/env.exe", and the parent of "env.exe" is a process that's no longer alive. In addition, we can see that the terminal command line returned by VS Code always has a env.exe command before the actual Java command. ![image]( Any suggestion on how we can get the running Java process in Git Bash? Thanks.

text: VS Code Insiders doesn't load an extension's modified package.json on disk after Reload if another version of the extension was previously installed. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version:Version: 1.60.0-insider (user setup) Commit: c08913337cb8b95493be8e99d62e0b3241563f6b Date: 2021-08-19T05:15:46.693Z Electron: 13.1.8 Chrome: 91.0.4472.164 Node.js: 14.16.0 V8: 9.1.269.39-electron.0 OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19043 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Use VS Code Insiders (it also repros with VS Code 1.59.0 if we use a [modified vsix]( that modifies updateChannel for non-Insiders VS Code). 1.5: You may want to set extensions.autoUpdate to "None" or else you may hit additional issues caused by this bug. 2. Open some folder with a .cpp file open so our extension can correctly activate. 3. Make sure the C/C++ extension is uninstalled and is not cached on disk (i.e. close/reopen VS Code Insiders). 4. Open the settings UI and type "updateChannel" to view the value (when it's available later). 5. Install the C/C++ extension (latest 1.5.1 is fine). 6. You should see the updateChannel be Default (assuming you haven't explicitly set it). 7. Open the extension's package.json on disk and search for updateChannel. Bug#1 (minor bug): The package.json on disk has the default updateChannel setting changed to "Insiders" but there was no prompt to reload window from the change (it's supposed to show a message "Extensions have been modified on disk. Please reload the window."). This is a minor issue and doesn't matter, but it could be related to the main bug below. 8. Do a reload window. You should see the updateChannel correctly show "Insiders" now (i.e. bug#2 below doesn't not occur unless you had another version of the extension on disk). 9. Install any other C/C++ vsix version, e.g. 1.5.0 via Install Another Version or manually install a vsix such as from . 10. Reload window to use the new version -- you should see bug#1 again. 11. Reload window again (to use the modified package.json). Bug#2 (main bug): The updateChannel is incorrectly "Default" -- the package.json on disk is not used. It seems to use some cached package.json that doesn't have the modified values on disk. This can cause our extension to enter an upgrade/downgrade "loop" if extensions.autoUpdate is not "None". However, you'll finally see "Extensions have been modified on disk. Please reload the window.", so it will then start using the correct package.json (until you install a new vsix version).

title: Provide API to change Notebook cell language
text: Provide API to change Notebook cell language. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> Currently the only way to update the notebook cell language is to replace the cell. In Jupyter we have things call cell magics. 1. Create a cell with the following text 2. Run this cell with a python kernel and HTML will be displayed. Similarly there are other magics, HTML, Bash, SVG, JavaScript, ruby, etc... Basically its an easy way to write code in another langauge and get that script executed and results displayed in the output. I would like Jupyter users with cell magics to get the benefits of VS Code. * Syntax highlighting * Code completion & the like Today the user will have to manually change the language of the cell to or other. A better experience would be (my suggestion) is for Jupyter to automatically detect such cell magics & change the language as the user is typing the code in the cell. I.e. as soon as the use types in we could change the cell langauge to & voila user now has syntax highlighting & the like for HTML in this cell. Unfortunately this can only be done via API today, & I feel that's a very destructive & heavy API. If while the user is typing in the text editor we change the cell language, then the focus changes. I was hoping for a simpler API where we could just change the language. FYI - Today we use this same API to change the cell language when users select different kernels and there's a single empty cell (we change the langauge of the cell to reflect the language of the kernel). Realted to /cc

title: Extension API: Allow to have hidden unsaved documents
text: Extension API: Allow to have hidden unsaved documents. # Context If you open a text document with It is hidden - no editor will be spawned. However, as soon as an edit is applied to it, a visible editor is spawned by VS Code: # Request It would be really useful if an extension could open a text document in a way that API edits don't open a visible editor! # Reason If that was possible, generic language embedding could be implemented by extensions. Lets say we have a markdown document like this: typescript import { baz } from "foo"; baz({ someParam: 10 }); ` An extension could create a document for the code block and save it to a temporary folder. The extension could keep the document in sync by projecting changes to the code block to the document. Since VS Code already exposes an API to query for autocompletion, the extension could project many language-service features available in the virtual document back to the markdown document. Currently, changes cannot really be projected to documents without VS Code spawning an editor for them. This would be a very annoying user experience. Writing directly to the file system and waiting for VS Code to reload the document is too slow for meaningful language service projection. # Problems 1) If the extension does not dispose the hidden document, it would allocate resources forever. 2) It is unclear what happens if the user opens the very same document. Maybe it should then turn into a normal document, but the lifetime should still be managed by the extension.

title: Completion-option: specify how often to query completion providers
text: Completion-option: specify how often to query completion providers. # Completion scenario 1. I type in "g" 2. A completion provider returns a bunch of completion items all starting with "g" 3. I type in an "m" (so I have typed in the word "gm") 4. Result: VS Code will take the suggestions returned by the completion provider in step 2 and filter them (rather than query the completion provider again with the query "gm") As far as I can see (from manual testing) VS Code will keep doing step 4 above until it has filtered off all items returned by the initial query (step 2), at which point it will query the completion provider again for a fresh list of completion items. # Feature request I'm looking for a VS Code option that controls the extent to which VS Code will re-query the completion provider when the user types in additional letters. In other words, I want to control the extent to which VS Code prefers **a)** doing client side filtering on completion items returned by an earlier query, and **b)** re-querying the completion provider with the new input text. # Notes Re-querying the completion provider only really makes sense when it returns the maximum number of results it can return. I.e. if my completion provider will return, at most, 50 items (let's call this setting ), then re-querying makes sense only when it returns this maximum number of results (since it means there might be more relevant results that were not included). Conversely, if the completion provider returns only, say, 12 results from a query (with ), then client-side filtering of previous results is fine, as the new query would just reduce the number of results from 12 to less. So, in other words, the above "Feature request"-setting is only relevant when a query is not specific enough to return fewer items than the completion provider's setting. So, perhaps, it's necessary to: 1. Change the VS Code API to (optionally) allow specifying the maximum number of results returned ( ) 2. Add a VS Code completion option that controls whether a completion provider is re-queried when the number of results returned by a previous query equals ### VS Code version info Version: 1.43.0 Commit: 78a4c91400152c0f27ba4d363eb56d2835f9903a

title: FileSystemProvider: Issues with asynchronous FileChangeEvent handling
text: FileSystemProvider: Issues with asynchronous FileChangeEvent handling. Issue Type: Bug I'm implementing a FileSystemProvider extension that communicates with another process to provide the file system contents. I was having issues with the 'Unsaved' decorations not going away and/or 'File Save' actions not resulting in writes of changes. After a bunch of experimentation, I got something working, but either the documentation needs some updates, or this is a bug. The sequence of events boiled down to: * The provider sends writeFile to the remote process, and returns immediately. All FileSystemProvider methods return Promises, btw. * Analogs to FileChangeEvents are created by the remote process in response to the writeFile requests and enqueued for delivery later. * The FileChangeEvent-analogs are translated into FileChangeEvents as they are received, and emitted on the onDidReceiveChange event. The communication is via vscode-jsonrpc MessageConnection, and the FileChangeEvent-analogs mentioned in the last line above are sent as Notication messages through the MessageConnection, in case that helps. What I was seeing: * When writing a file, I would see a sequence of 3 stat calls to the file, followed by a writeFile, and the FileChangeEvents seemed to be ignored. After some comparison with MemFS, and some experimentation, I got things working by returning the FileChangeEvent[] directly from the JSON-RPC call that need them, instead of enqueuing them for delivery as Notications, and then delivering the events before returning from the FileSystemProvider methods. What I think is happening is that at least one of the stat calls received before the writeFile call are intended to occur after the writeFile action really completes (i.e. when the Changed FileChangeEvent is emitted), but is instead is triggering after the writeFile call returns. The stat call then completes and returns before the writeFile change events are process, vscode thinks nothing has changed with the file, and leaves the editor marked as dirty. Given that the writeFile/createDirectory/delete/rename methods don't just return the FileChangeEvent[] values directly, I don't think the observed behavior is desired. In case it is, the documentation should be updated to reflect the true ordering requirements. VS Code version: Code 1.42.1 (c47d83b293181d9be64f27ff093689e8e7aed054, 2020-02-11T14:45:59.656Z) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.16299

text: Improve testing experience for VSIXes when Webpack is in play. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> VS Code now supports bundling extensions, and the documentation guides extension devs towards Webpack. I have an extension which imports a lot of dependencies, and the biggest benefit to me is to be able to bundle my into a single file with my own code. However, not all my dependencies play nicely with Webpack. I can work around this using Webpack's option to continue loading them from . The documentation recommends that I exclude from packaging in , which is where I get most of my speed boost from, but then I need to add patterns _not_ to exclude the packages I externalised (and the packages _they_ depend on... which can itself be a bit laborious). Example: However, if I do this, then what I get in the debug environment (F5) does not necessarily match what I get in the packaged environment ( ). If I forget to unignore something, then it seems that the _debug_ extension will work (because it maps the source directory which includes ) but the _packaged_ extension will fail - with no useful diagnostic as to _why_ it failed. And the only way I've found to determine what's wrong in the package is to: * Build the VSIX for the real extension (call it R). * Install the VSIX for R. * Load a folder containing the source of another (dummy) extension (call it D). * Debug D to launch the Extension Development Host. * In the Extension Development Host, trigger one of R's activation event. * If activation of R fails, e.g. due to a missing external dependency, the error is dumped to the debug console where I am editing D. I can now inspect the error and relate it back to a location in R. Is there a more streamlined way? Can we have a way to have the extension packaged, and its VSIX loaded into the Extension Development Host, e.g. via a debug launch configuration?

title: VS Code does not handle a high amount of code completions well
text:
VS Code does not handle a high amount of code completions well. Issue Type: Performance Issue When there is a very high amount of code completions available, vscode will take a long time to show them to the user. Although, this is redundant because the user will likely only scroll through a low percentage of them. Steps to reproduce: - Create a new extension with . - In package.json, add the activation event. - Replace the contents of with this: - Run the extension and create a new file. - Ask for completions ( ) and notice how there is a delay before the completions are provided, but the actual providing of completions take an insignificant amount of time. - Try multiplying the amount of iterations by 10 in case you are not noticing it on your system. Note: this might seem like an insignificant problem that never happens, but this amount of completions can be easily reached when for example an extension adds in all of the available namespaces of a project. Secondly, the delays are actually quite annoying and there is no way to deal with them on the extension's side. One way to optimize it might be to only show the top 100 or so completions, and update that list whenever the user types (in case there are completions that have not been filtered other than the top 100 being shown currently). If the user wishes to scroll pass these 100 then the next 100 will be loaded as well (this happens a very low percentage of the time though). title: Allow extensions to provide language servers for the use of other extensions via LanguageClient. Provide native language servers by default.
text: Allow extensions to provide language servers for the use of other extensions via LanguageClient. Provide native language servers by default.. The extension development utilities in VS Code are great, but may require extension authors to build up their own language server from scratch. At least in regards to generic information about one's code base such as definitions, references, and nav trees, it would be much easier if an extension author could talk to a language server provided by another extension or native to VS Code itself (e.g. Typescript). Here's how it could work: - When an extension author creates their own language server (implementing the LSP), they "provide" that server to VS Code in the form of a LanguageClient. - Another extension author can check the provided LanguageClient's within VS Code, and if the desired client exists (either natively or thanks to another extension they've installed), inject it into their extension and begin making requests. (If it is not provided, they could initialize their own LanguageClient in the usual way.) In order for this to really be useful first and foremost the native language servers in VS Code would need to be available. Then contributors could create extensions that exclusively provide a language client and server. Then extensions that wish to leverage these language servers can focus on their own extension specific functionality. I think this would change the approach to language tooling a bit, but ultimately for the better. Right now my own team is developing an extension that needs definition and reference info for Typescript and there doesn't seem to be any way to piggy back off of the native Typescript server. As a result we spin up _another_ Typescript server within our extension. This feels unnecessary and computationally wasteful (not to mention cumbersome).

title: Azure DevOps Git Clone Fails in Visual Studio – “Unable to Resume Suspended Process During Process Creation”
text: Azure DevOps Git Clone Fails in Visual Studio – “Unable to Resume Suspended Process During Process Creation”. ## Title Azure DevOps Git Clone Fails in Visual Studio – “Unable to Resume Suspended Process During Process Creation” **Visual Studio Version:** Visual Studio 2022 and Visual Studio 2026 (version 18) **OS Version:** Windows 11 (exact build to be confirmed) ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open Microsoft Visual Studio. 2. Navigate to the Azure DevOps repository cloning workflow. 3. Attempt to clone a Git repository from Azure DevOps. 4. Observe the following error: ### Expected Behavior Visual Studio should successfully launch its bundled Git process and clone the Azure DevOps repository without errors. ### Actual Behavior Visual Studio fails to start or resume the Git process, preventing the repository from being cloned or the affected Git operation from completing. ### Troubleshooting Performed - Confirmed that Git operations work through Command Prompt, Git Bash, and Visual Studio Code. - Confirmed that the issue occurs specifically within Visual Studio. - Reviewed Microsoft Defender exclusions for the Visual Studio installation directories and bundled Git binaries. - Reviewed the relevant directories and Visual Studio installation paths. - Collected Visual Studio diagnostic logs and a Process Monitor (ProcMon) trace for Microsoft Support analysis. - Reviewed Microsoft Defender events, including Exploit Guard events recorded in Audit mode. No confirmed Defender block has been identified as the root cause. - The issue is affecting approximately 20 Visual Studio users. ### Existing Exclusion Paths Reviewed The Visual Studio installation directories are already excluded. Additional exclusions for specific executables, such as or , require validation and should only be implemented if Microsoft confirms they are necessary. ### Request for Investigation Please investigate why Visual Studio fails to create or resume its bundled Git process when performing Azure DevOps repository operations, even though Git works correctly through Command Prompt, Git Bash, and Visual Studio Code. Please confirm: 1. Whether this is a known issue affecting Visual Studio 2022 or Visual Studio 2026. 2. Whether additional directory or executable exclusions are required when the existing Visual Studio paths are already excluded. 3. Whether Defender, attack surface reduction rules, application control, or another process-creation restriction could be responsible. 4. What additional diagnostic information or targeted tests are required to identify the root cause. The issue remains unresolved despite the troubleshooting completed so far. We request Microsoft's direct feedback and recommended next steps.

title: Latest Update Causes Compilers To Not Detect Changes In Code!
text: Latest Update Causes Compilers To Not Detect Changes In Code!. VSCode auto-updated, and I've noticed a behaviour where replacing files in the file explorer (let's say I have a zip with an older copy, or an alternative branch) no longer results in the compiler noticing the changes, and thus skips re-compiling them. The git tab will still note that the files changed, but unless I manually type something in and save the file inside VSC, the code will instead compile from cache or something, resulting in stale data. The last 24 hours have been hell for me as I could not understand why an older copy of code that I had, which I knew worked, suddenly had the exact same bugs as my latest code. I'm not happy to find out that for one, it really was my tools that were to blame and not me. Steps to reproduce: 1. Have code you've already compiled (I'm doing C#) 2. In file explorer, replace the files 3. Compile, do not edit and save the files, just compile 4. Run the code, notice the compiler preserved the old code OS: W10, Latest. X86 Intel. VSCode version: 1.118.1 "user setup" (as if I had willingly updated) For now I am: 1. Adding pointless // to every file that has changes to force the IDE to notice them 2. title: NOT Following critical instructions in the copilot instruction file
text: NOT Following critical instructions in the copilot instruction file. Type: Bug The user is asking why I sent ^C (SIGINT) to the terminal, and pointing out that the copilot instructions explicitly warn against this kind of behavior. Let me re-read the relevant section from the instructions. From the copilot-instructions.md: ### 🚨 Terminal Command Rules — CRITICAL **🚨 CRITICAL: The VS Code agent terminal has known limitations with complex shell quoting. These rules prevent terminal corruption that wastes time and requires manual recovery. Violating these rules WILL corrupt the terminal session and require manual recovery.** The user is right - I should NOT have been sending commands to a terminal while another command was still running. That's what caused the ^C. The instructions don't explicitly mention ^C, but the principle is clear: don't corrupt terminal sessions. I see what happened now—I sent a new command while ./restart_all.sh was still executing, which forced the terminal to interrupt the running process with SIGINT before accepting the new input. The user is understandably frustrated because I violated the terminal rules, caused their services to go down, and wasted their time and tokens. I should have either run the restart in the background or waited with a proper timeout instead of sending commands to an active terminal. title: Bug: documents opened by EH: vscode.workspace.openTextDocument() are not disposed correctly
text: Bug: documents opened by EH: vscode.workspace.openTextDocument() are not disposed correctly. - VS Code Version: 1.108.2 - OS Version: Windows 11 This was noticed by the fact that diagnostic entries of the file being closed doesn't get removed from Problems View, if a file was opened from extension by , which differs from opening files from Explorer panel, in which case diagnostic entries are removed on file close. Reproduction steps: 1. Open a file which contains problems, using call from extension 2. Ensure that problems appear in Problems View 3. Close file 4. Observe that diagnostics remains in Problems View 5. Additionally, if you give VS Code several minutes to idle, at some point it triggers resource cleanup, removing giagnostics from Problems View unexpectedly Also, when using a watcher task with problems matcher, diagnostics does not get replaced by task's diagnostics outputs when file is closed. Not necessarily, you can check the video I have posted in to demonstrate diagnostics vanishing (ignore that there I blame for this, since now it is clear that the source is different). Another place I mention this issue is I tried to fix it and found something, but I'm not sure how to complete it. Here are my results 1. First, I have found that for the file opened from EH, [ModelService.onModelRemoved]( is not fired on close 2. The reason for this turned out to be that the of model equals when the [dispose]( is called on close, and that differs for the files opened from Explorer panel, which is in that case 3. Found that, what adds additional reference, is [ExtHostDocuments._proxy.$tryOpenDocument]( which end up here [const ref = await this._textModelResolverService.createModelReference(uri);]( and is seems that it doesn't get disposed on close 4. I have tested what if I reduce counter by 1 manually for the file opened from EH. It gets disposed then, and diagnostics removed from Problems View as it should, but diagnostics does not get replaced by running task's problem matcher outputs

title: What happens when editing a GitHub Copilot prompt after conversation summarization?
text: What happens when editing a GitHub Copilot prompt after conversation summarization?. Is conversation summarization irreversible? Is the un-summarized conversation lost forever, or do previous prompts keep the full conversation before the summarization? This is critical to know when editing previous prompts: 1. Submit a prompt such as "Change to ". 2. The dreaded "Summarizing conversation ..." appears; it finished with "Conversation summarized". 3. Edit the previous prompt to "Change to ". **Expected:** GitHub Copilot summarizes the conversation again. **Actual:** Often GitHub Copilot _does not_ summarize the conversation again. You might wonder, if I dread the conversation summarization so much (e.g. #283446), why I seem to be _wanting_ it to appear. That's not the issue. This strange behavior makes me worried whether a _later conversation summarization_ might be irrevocably losing the conversation, thus preventing the ability to resubmit prompts. This happens often. I noted it in #286822: > I edited the previous prompt a third time to switch back to "Design" mode again. I asked the LLM to evaluate risk. Again it did _not_ summarize. But here's the worrying part: after switching back to Agent mode to request the implementation a third time, even with a much larger prompt, _no summarization occurred_!! In fact the entire implementation proceeded with no summarization! … Knowing what happens is important for many scenarios: * Let's say I accidentally submit a prompt with Claude Haiku 4.5, but realize that I wanted to submit the problem with Claude Opus 4.5, because the problem is so complex that only Claude Opus 4.5 could handle it. If the conversation is summarized in that round and I resubmit the prompt with Claude Opus 4.5, does the conversation get restored so that Claude Opus 4.5 can see the full conversation? Or is Claude Opus 4.5 presented the pitiful summarization that happened during the first submission to Claude Haiku 4.5? * Or let's say that the LLM summarizes in the middle of a huge implementation, and the summarization throws the LLM off-track. So I edit the previous prompt in order to force summarization so it won't happen in the middle of the implementation. (See #284474.) But at this point, has summarization already happened irreversibly? * Sometimes editing the previous prompt still causes summarization to occur again. (See e.g. #286822.) What does that mean? Did it reset the conversation, and then summarize the full version? Or did it immediately summarize a summarization, because restoring to a checkpoint didn't undo the first summarization? From the current GitHub behavior, it's hard to know what is actually going on with summarization. One more reason why I'm really just [wanting to turn the durned thing off]( but still don't know what that means either. ☹️

title: Feature Request: Add delay setting for terminal command execution by Copilot/AI agents
text: Feature Request: Add delay setting for terminal command execution by Copilot/AI agents. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> # Feature Request: Add delay setting for terminal command execution by GitHub Copilot > **Target Repository**: (VS Code Terminal API) > > **Related Issue**: #11383 (2016) - "delay sendText until terminal is ready?" > > _Issue generated by AI copilot and adjusted by a human_ ## Summary Add **configurable delay setting** for Chat Tools API terminal commands to solve the terminal initialization race condition. While #11383 requested automatic waiting, this proposes a user-configurable delay for modern autonomous workflows. **Problem**: executes immediately after , before shells like Git Bash finish initializing, causing command truncation in GitHub Copilot agent mode. ## Motivation **Historical Context**: Issue #11383 (2016) identified this problem: "it would be nice if sendText waits for bash to be ready before sending because now the stuff I have send shows up twice". Nine years later, with GitHub Copilot's autonomous agent mode, this is now **critical**. **Modern Impact**: With enabled, first commands fail because: 1. returns immediately 2. Shell loads environment (Git Bash, WSL take 300-500ms) 3. No wait for shell integration signals ( ) 4. executes before prompt ready 5. Command truncated → **entire autonomous workflow breaks** **Why configurable over automatic**: While #11383 proposed automatic waiting, autonomous agents need **predictable, configurable delays** to: - Balance speed vs reliability (different shells have different init times) - Allow power users to optimize their workflows - Provide graceful degradation when shell integration unavailable - Match the precedent of ## Proposed Solutions ### Option 1: Simple Delay (Preferred) Insert configurable delay between and . ### Option 2: Granular Delays ### Option 3: Shell Integration Wait (Most Robust) Wait for sequence before sending commands. title: Option to Remove/ Disable 'Hidden Terminals'
text: Option to Remove/ Disable 'Hidden Terminals'. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.107.0-insider (Universal) - OS Version: macOS Tahoe 26.2 Description: While using using the Copilot agent, and it needs to use the terminal for whatever reason, instead of just using the last open terminal or listing a new terminal, it creates a 'hidden terminal', and sometimes multiple hidden terminals. If there's an issue within the running terminal commands, you cannot see the issue and have to rely on the chat to debug which can be time consuming, or the chat 'hangs' because the terminal doesn't complete for whatever reason, or it would simply be faster/ easier to run commands yourself. As such, you have to click 'hidden terminal' and then select the terminal from the command palette, just to open the new terminal view. I do not want to debug the terminal from the chat. A more fluid workflow would just have the chat agent open a new terminal and run the new commands in the already visible terminal panel. It would be nice to have an option to disable hidden terminals. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a project in VS Code Insiders. 2. Use Copilot Agent to run code / compile / test / or otherwise execute a command that triggers a terminal. 3. Observe that the terminal does not appear as a visible tab or panel. Instead, a “hidden” terminal is created. 4. You must now select the hidden terminal, select from the command palette, to view the running commands. I don't mind the agent using the terminal as a tool, or running commands, it's that I can't see the Agent's output in the terminal to determine if it's working or correct. I'd like to be able to disable the 'hidden terminal' feature so the experience is more transparent. Or by default re-use the last active visible terminal rather than spawning hidden ones.

title: First line of less output overwritten by command line
text:
First line of less output overwritten by command line. Type: Bug This bites me worst when using things like , but can be reproduced using . What happens is that shows the first N-1 lines of the output (where N is the terminal height) plus a line with a single as the prompt. When I quit out of less by typing the is overwritten by the shell prompt. Nice. But in recent (last few months) VS Code releases there's a feature that limits the output to the *last* N-2 lines (e.g. ) where you can scroll inside this N-2-sized region to see earlier output. The two separate "paging" mechanisms together result in the *first* line of the output being overwritten by the command whose output it was. In the case this drops the HEAD revision from sight, which is confusing. Maybe it's not so important to show the command without scrolling back? (I can usually remember the last command I typed. :-) That would give a much better user experience IMO. title: Wrong file extension
text: Wrong file extension. This might be seen as a dup of "Save As: Default file type should be *.*", but it's really more of a rebuttal (with proposed solution). *(Sorry about not linking to original, but I assume that a bot would see that it is closed, which might prevent a human from ever reading this...)* In the interest of respecting your time, I'll lead with the solution: ## Solution Stop specifying a content-type to the upstream save action. Note that the OS already defaults to selecting 'All Files', which is far more likely to be the desired behavior. Note that this solution could also be considered a win for your devs who no longer have to maintain the code responsible for such. ### Problem The answer in the original issue was that the behavior is caused by "upstream" (presumably referring to Electron). But (not to be rude, and I could always be wrong) that seems like a cop-out. Because, whether intentional or not, VSCode must be supplying what it believes the current file's content-type is when it calls the upstream save action. How else would the (often incorrect) extension be getting set? - The file extension filter inside the dialog always corresponds to whatever VSCode believes the of the content being saved is. > For example: > An unsaved file containing ERB is always mis-detected as HTML by VSCode. > When saving, the default file extension filter is set to HTML. > This causes the dialog to hide any existing ERB files unless the user clicks on and scrolls to the bottom of the giant list of possible extensions and selects 'All Files' (which would otherwise already be selected unless configured otherwise at the OS level). - And even when the syntax of the content is guessed correctly, the concept of automatically setting the file extension is, itself, bad UX. > For example: > It is common to name related files with a shared prefix ( , ). > The automatic filtering behavior prevents what is often the fastest method, which is to simply click on an existing file with that prefix and adjust the extension. > This bug not only forces users to type out the full filename, but does so while preventing them from having a visual reference to existing files—each of which could be considered problematic in their own right. - If no effort is going to be made to provide configurability for this behavior in VSCode, then please just remove this behavior altogether. ### Conclusion The root problem is the concept of specifying a content type / file extension to begin with. Doing so is not required, and the trade-offs—some of which described above—far outweigh whatever the imagined benefits are supposed to be.

title: VS Code does not display Vietnamese text correctly with TCVN3 (ABC) encoding
text: VS Code does not display Vietnamese text correctly with TCVN3 (ABC) encoding. When opening files encoded in TCVN3 (ABC) – a legacy Vietnamese encoding – VS Code displays garbled or incorrect characters instead of proper Vietnamese text. This makes it impossible to read or edit legacy Vietnamese scripts that require TCVN3 encoding. Steps to Reproduce: Create or obtain a text file encoded in TCVN3 (ABC) with Vietnamese content. Open the file in VS Code. Observe that Vietnamese characters are not displayed correctly. Expected Behavior: VS Code should provide an option to view and edit files using TCVN3 (ABC) encoding, displaying Vietnamese text properly. Actual Behavior: Characters appear as gibberish or with incorrect diacritics. However, even with .VnArial installed and selected, VS Code still cannot render Vietnamese text correctly in TCVN3 encoding. Request: Please add support for TCVN3 (ABC) encoding in VS Code, or provide an extension/setting to view and edit files with this encoding.

title: Terminal auto-approve backend does not reliably apply regex/wildcard rules, requiring excessive literal command line approvals
text: Terminal auto-approve backend does not reliably apply regex/wildcard rules, requiring excessive literal command line approvals. Observed behavior: When using the VS Code 'chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove' setting, even with a global regex rule (e.g. '/.*/': true), many terminal commands only get auto-approved if their full literal command line is explicitly listed. This results in a proliferation of literal command line approvals, despite having comprehensive regex and wildcard rules. Expected behavior: Regex and wildcard rules should reliably match and auto-approve all relevant terminal commands, minimizing the need for literal command line approvals. Impact: - Reduces maintainability and clarity of settings - Indicates a bug or limitation in the backend matching logic for terminal command approval - Hinders full agent autonomy and automation Steps to reproduce: 1. Set 'chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove' to { '/.*/': true } in settings.json (see attached context). 2. Attempt to run a variety of terminal commands via agent/extension automation. 3. Observe that some commands are only auto-approved if their full literal command line is added, not via regex/wildcard. Recommendation: Investigate and fix the backend matching logic so that regex and wildcard rules are reliably applied to all terminal commands, eliminating the need for literal command line approvals. This will improve maintainability and enable full agent autonomy. Context: See settings.json and recent agent/user discussion for details.

[Expandable hovers for JavaScript and TypeScript]( When you hover over a symbol in JavaScript or TypeScript, VS Code tries to show the most useful IntelliSense type information about that symbol. Types can be very complex, so one challenge for us has been trying to find the right balance between showing enough details to be useful, while not showing so much info that it becomes overwhelming. It's hard to come up with a good one size fits all approach, and also the level of type detail you want might change depending on what you are working on. That's why this iteration, we've added new UI that gives you more control over how types are shown in hovers. When you hover over a symbol, now you can select the little + icon on the left side of the hover control to expand the interfaces and complex types in the hover into their components. For example, you can use this to see the properties of an interface directly in the hover: Hovers can be expanded multiple times, which recursively expands types from the previous expansion. If you ever expand too much, just select the - icon to go back to the previous level. Also keep in mind that not every type is expandable and that we still need some limits on just how much expansion we can support. title: Allow snippet nesting
text: Allow snippet nesting. Currently, VS Code does not allow expanding a snippet when the cursor is inside a tab stop of an active snippet. In other editors (Sublime Text, Neovim with UltiSnips/LuaSnip), this is possible: the snippet engine permits invoking another snippet inside a placeholder, and the outer snippet continues functioning normally. This feature would greatly improve workflows in domains where repetitive, structured text is common, such as LaTeX, Typst, and other typesetting languages. In these cases, users often need to insert smaller “component” snippets (integrals, fractions) into math environments. At present, doing so in VS Code requires manually exiting the placeholder or invoking Trigger Suggest ( ) each time, which interrupts typing flow.

The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.103.0 - OS Version: MacOS Sequoia 15.6 When working with GitHub Codespaces from your local environment (so not the browser based Codespaces editor), VSCode attempts to connect to the Codespaces environment for MCP connections instead of your local machine environment. This causes problems with self hosted MCPs that cannot be added within the Codespaces env (like [the Figma MCP]( The problem occurs with remote MCP connections (SSE or HTTP) that are behind a VPN for security reasons, as the VPN connection is not being picked up by VSCode, as it still uses the Codespaces environment. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Install [the Figma MCP]( locally and try to connect to it from a Codespace. Ideally, when using the desktop version of VSCode + Codespaces, there should either be an option to pick which env to be used for MCP connections (local / Codespaces) and maybe default it to local.
