title: Claude Desktop MCP Configuration Conflict Breaks Github Copilot Chat
text: Claude Desktop MCP Configuration Conflict Breaks Github Copilot Chat. Type: Bug # GitHub Copilot - Claude Desktop MCP Configuration Conflict Bug Report ## 🐛 **Issue Summary** GitHub Copilot Chat (Ctrl+I) stops working when Claude Desktop has ANY MCP server configured ## 🚀 **Reproduction Script** Because VS Code automatically discovers MCP servers from Claude Desktop's configuration file and attempts to start them, creating a conflict that prevents Copilot Chat from functioning across ALL VS Code projects. **Confirmed Issue Timeline**: Weekend of July 26-27, 2025 on Windows 11 Enterprise system. ## 📋 **Bug Details** ### **Environment Information** - **OS**: Windows 11 Enterprise (Build 26100.1.amd64fre.ge_release.240331-1435) - **VS Code Version**: 1.102.2 (c306e94f98122556ca081f527b466015e1bc37b0, x64) - **GitHub Copilot Extension Version**: 1.346.0 - **GitHub Copilot Chat Extension Version**: 0.29.1 - **Azure GitHub Copilot Extension Version**: 1.0.58 - **Claude Desktop Version**: 0.12.55 - **User Profile**: [userprofile] - **Report Date**: July 28, 2025 (Issue occurred weekend of July 26-27, 2025) ### **Configuration Details** - **Claude Desktop Config**: - **MCP Server**: CIPP-MCP Proxy (FastMCP stdio-to-http bridge for Claude Desktop) - **Script Path**: ## 🎯 **Root Cause Analysis** **The core issue appears to be:** 1. **Claude Desktop configuration** defines MCP servers for Claude's use 2. **VS Code/GitHub Copilot automatically discovers** MCP servers from Claude's config file 3. **VS Code attempts to start** the MCP server (FastMCP based MCP Proxy) for its own use 4. **Backend MCP server is not running** because it was only intended for Claude Desktop 5. **Conflict occurs** when GitHub Copilot tries to use a partially functional MCP setup **Key observation**: VS Code shows the MCP server as "running" even when the backend service isn't available, and attempts to automatically restart the MCP process when stopped. Current behavior shows MCP icon in Copilot Chat endlessly "discovering tools" rather than complete failure. **Architecture Problem**: The FastMCP Proxy is designed as a stdio-to-http bridge for Claude Desktop, but VS Code treats it as a standalone MCP server, creating a broken state where: - Proxy process starts successfully (appears "running" to VS Code) - Backend MCP endpoint is not running - Proxy cannot fulfill MCP requests, causing Copilot Chat to malfunction or enter infinite discovery loop - **VS Code automatically restarts the proxy** when manually stopped, creating persistent conflict ## 🔄 **Reproduction Steps** ### **Prerequisites** 1. Install VS Code with GitHub Copilot extension 2. Install Claude Desktop application 3. Have a MCP server configured for Claude Desktop **Note**: The specific MCP server doesn't matter - ANY MCP configuration in Claude Desktop triggers this conflict but it is especially apparent if the MCP server is not functioning or in development. ### **Exact Configuration That Caused the Issue** The problematic Claude Desktop configuration that causes the endless discovering tools loop is below. Another variation breaks copilot chat completely: **Note**: The original problematic configuration may have used a command instead of / . This one prevented copilot chat from responding at all. That chat interface was available but it would simply ignore any converstatons. As soon as I would stop the CIPP-MCP copilot chat would immediately respond to whatever I asked it last and keep working for a few minutes until VS Code restarted CIPP-MCP. The current configuration still causes MCP discovery issues in VS Code, demonstrating that any Claude Desktop MCP configuration triggers the conflict. ### **Steps to Reproduce** 1. **Verify Copilot Working**: Open VS Code, test GitHub Copilot chat (Ctrl+I) and inline suggestions 2. **Add Claude Desktop MCP Config**: Edit the config file above with the problematic configuration 4. **Test Copilot**: Return to VS Code and observe Copilot Chat malfunction ### **Expected Behavior** - GitHub Copilot should ignore Claude Desktop MCP configurations or have the ability to toggle them on/off - VS Code should not attempt to start MCP servers from Claude Desktop's config unless explitly requested by the user - Both tools should operate independently without cross-contamination of configurations ### **Actual Behavior** *(Confirmed on July 26-27, 2025)* - VS Code/GitHub Copilot discovers MCP server from Claude Desktop config immediately upon VS Code startup - **Current behavior**: MCP icon appears in Copilot Chat but shows "discovering tools" indefinitely - **Previous severe behavior**: GitHub Copilot Chat would accept input but would not respond at all until I 'stopped' CIPP-MCP Proxy from VS Code - **Configuration dependency**: Removing Claude Desktop config immediately restores Copilot functionality - **Restart cycle**: Restoring the config breaks Copilot again, confirming direct correlation - **Automatic restart issue**: Even when manually stopping the CIPP-MCP Proxy process, VS Code automatically restarts it within minutes - **Persistent conflict**: VS Code continues attempting to manage the MCP server, creating an ongoing conflict state - The conflict persists until Claude Desktop config is completely removed ## 🔍 **Diagnostic Information** ### **Files to Check During Reproduction** - (Claude config) - VS Code settings: - VS Code extension logs: - GitHub Copilot extension logs: Check VS Code Developer Tools > Console - Windows Event Viewer: Application and System logs for any MCP or Python process errors - Task Manager: Check for python.exe processes related to Claude MCP servers/proxies ### **Potential Conflict Areas** 1. **Configuration Cross-Contamination**: VS Code reading Claude Desktop's MCP config 2. **Process Management**: VS Code trying to manage MCP servers intended for Claude 3. **Architecture Mismatch**: FastMCP Proxy designed for Claude's stdio ↔ HTTP bridge, not direct VS Code usage 4. **Resource Conflicts**: Proxy processes started without proper backend connections (real MCP server unavailable) 5. **Automatic Restart Logic**: VS Code persistently restarts stopped MCP processes, preventing manual resolution 6. **State Management**: Partial MCP initialization causing Copilot to enter infinite discovery loops 7. **IPC/Communication**: Interference between Copilot and improperly initialized MCP servers ## 🔍 **CIPP MCP Proxy Code** *(The Python script VS Code incorrectly tries to execute)* The proxy script that VS Code attempts to start is a FastMCP bridge designed only for Claude Desktop: **Architecture Issue**: This proxy is designed to: 1. Accept stdio input from Claude Desktop 2. Bridge to a streamable-http MCP server at ` or the real MCP endpoint 3. The backend MCP server ( ) is NOT running when VS Code starts the proxy 4. This creates a "zombie" proxy process that VS Code shows as "running" but is non-functional ## 📊 **Impact Assessment** ### **Severity**: High - **Reason**: Completely breaks GitHub Copilot functionality - **Workaround**: Remove Claude Desktop MCP configuration ### **User Impact** *(Real-World Impact)* - Developers cannot use both GitHub Copilot and Claude Desktop with MCP servers simultaneously - Forces choice between AI tools instead of allowing complementary usage - Significant impact on development productivity, especially for users relying on Copilot Chat - Issue occurs silently - users may not realize Claude Desktop MCP config is the cause - Affects enterprise users who may have both tools configured for different purposes ## 🔧 **Workaround** **Only complete removal of Claude Desktop MCP configuration provides permanent resolution:** 1. title: Show the cursor's offset from the beginning of the line
text: Show the cursor's offset from the beginning of the line. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> Many languages/environments show the exact location of an error in a line of code. In Javascript for example, typing will log . The last number, 14, is a reference to the second since it's the 14th character in the line. This is useful because, in this example, it tells me which of the three identifiers is the problem. Previous IDEs I've used show the cursor's position in the document with the same scheme, displaying a line number and character number in that line, which makes it easy to locate exactly where the issue is. I was surprised to learn that VSCode does not do this; it only shows the line number. Perhaps I'm missing a setting somewhere, but I've looked around and cannot find any way to enable seeing the cursor's offset from the beginning of the line. There is a workaround, which is that VSCode will show me a count of the number of characters currently _highlighted_, so I can put the cursor at the beginning of the line, hold shift, and then move the cursor around to see the character offset. This is honestly not that bad, but I have to remember that it's the method, and I really think that something this basic should be displayed by default. Or at least offer a setting to enable it.

title: Entry Breakpoints
text: Entry Breakpoints. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> It would be really great if there were two types of breakpoints: Let's call them Entry-Breakpoint and Dependent-Breakpoint. It often happens that you need to debug certain parts of the code, but only for a specific type of entity or a specific entity. Currently you have to deactivate the breakpoints in the code, until execution reaches the entity in question (you usually use a breakpoint that is inside an if statement that recognizes the entity). Then you would reactivate your breakpoints and hit play so that execution will stop at the relevant code. It would be very nice if you had Dependent-Breakpoints, that would not stop execution until an entry breakpoint has been reached. I.e. they would only activate once the Entry-Breakpoint they are dependent on has been reached. This is somewhat like conditional breakpoints, but not quite like them (for conditional breakpoints are too complicated for debugging purposes). In the UI, dependent breakpoints could have big blue dots (in contrast to normal breakpoints that have red dots). Normal breakpoints would then all become Entry-Breakpoints, but without any Dependent-Breakpoints below them. One could also implement it such that in general Dependent-Breakpoints are only activated after at least one Entry-Breakpoint has been reached (or only after execution has been halted at least once). But I don't think it would be too complicated to have a double-layered tree of breakpoints in the view (top level would be Entry-Breakpoints, second level below would be Dependent-Breakpoints). One would be able to configure the dependency relation by simply dragging and dropping Dependent-Breakpoints.

title: Feature Request: Confirmation Dialog for Closing VS Code with Active Background Processes
text: Feature Request: Confirmation Dialog for Closing VS Code with Active Background Processes. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> ## Summary Add a confirmation dialog when closing VS Code while background processes (such as terminal tasks) are still running, requiring explicit user confirmation to terminate these processes. ## Problem Statement Currently, when VS Code is closed accidentally while processes are running in the terminal or other background tasks are active, these processes are terminated without warning. This can lead to data loss, incomplete operations, or corrupted states in development workflows. ## Proposed Solution Implement a popup confirmation dialog that appears when attempting to close VS Code while background processes are active. The dialog should: - Display which processes are currently running - Provide options to: - Close VS Code and terminate all processes - Cancel the close operation - Optionally, allow processes to continue running in the background ## Use Cases - Preventing accidental termination of long-running builds - Avoiding interruption of active file operations - Ensuring proper completion of git operations - Protecting against data loss during installations ## Technical Details The feature should: 1. Detect active processes in integrated terminals 2. Monitor background tasks initiated through VS Code 3. Present a clear, non-intrusive dialog with process information 4. Remember user preferences if they choose "Don't ask again" option ## Similar Features in Other Products This functionality is similar to how many IDEs and text editors (such as Visual Studio) handle closing with active processes, providing users with information and choice before terminating operations. ## Additional Context This feature would significantly improve the user experience by preventing accidental termination of important tasks and aligning with users' expectations of application behavior when closing with active processes. I believe this feature would benefit many developers who regularly run background processes in VS Code and occasionally close the editor without thinking about what might be running.

Missing/Inconsistent Data for SQL Exercis Version: 1.98.2 Commit: ddc367ed5c8936efe395cffeec279b04ffd7db78 User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/134.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/134.0.0.0 Embedder: codespaces <!-- generated by web issue reporter --> Hello -- I'm teaching an MIS course for which our textbook is a Cengage book, augmented by the MindTap courseware. MindTap includes a module, "SQL Labs: Exercises for the Real World", which opens a GitHub interface that describes SQL exercises and serves as a platform for running student solutions to those exercises. One exercise, in the "Math with SQL" section starts with the prompt "Using the software.plans table, . . . ", but the "software" database has no "plans" table, only a "subscriptions" table, which has none of the columns supposedly in the "plans" table. However, I worked through all the exercises on my own last week and had no trouble with the data, as all databases and tables were as expected. It seems the databases and data are moving targets, here today and gone tomorrow; the student must experiment with different browsers, computers, etc. for things to work as they should! Even right now, I could not get the Cengage/GitHub platform to work on my standard browser (Chrome), and all I get is a 404 error page from GitHub. Please look into this and help me solve it, so my students will be able to learn and apply these SQL concepts, rathen than hating anything to do with computer coder whether SQL or 3rd generation languages such as Python! -- JS

title: GitHub Copilot instructions implementation inadequate for deciding which to use for new files.
text: GitHub Copilot instructions implementation inadequate for deciding which to use for new files.. In #272199 we had a long discussion and discovered that there can be user-wide instructions, but they have to use to be picked up for general Ask mode if there is no file context to indicate a file type. microsoft/vscode-docs#9006 was opened to clarify the docs. The assertion in #272199 is that if you are working on an actual Java file, then you can use for the instructions. However it turns out in practice that this is inadequate because of a design flaw; it will only work sometimes, specifically if you are editing an existing file, not creating a new one. If I ask the LLM to _create_ a Java file, GitHub Copilot will not know until _after my prompt is processed_ what file will be created. However GitHub Copilot makes the decision about which instruction files to add _before submitting the prompt_. Therefore even if I use at the top of my instruction file, that instruction file will never be picked up when _creating new Java files_. Obviously I don't want edited Java files to be one way and new Java files to be another way. Asking the LLM "now update the new Java file you just created, based upon the instructions you suddenly see because the file type is now known" would be a kludge; I might as well manually include instructions. In short, the scheme is not really useful. I'll need to just if I want the instructions to work even for new files, which means the instruction file will suddenly be bloated with instructions for Java, for TypeScript, for Rust, etc. I propose that the GitHub Copilot team redesign the instruction association logic so that it becomes similar to another tool that the LLM can request. The LLM could then choose the correct instruction file to be inserted _at the time the LLM decides to edit or create a file_. With this approach would work for editing existing file, creating new files, and even for adding new code snippets within the chat in Ask mode.

title: Reconsider the whole 60 day upvote process for feature requests
text: Reconsider the whole 60 day upvote process for feature requests. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> I completely understand that there are tons and tons of issues opened up due to the size of this project, but unfortunately it seems that the current process skews towards prioritizing certain types of features over others. I see so many of certain types of features that are implemented based on an open issue that happened to received the upvotes within the timeframe, while there may also be a topic that has NUMEROUS closed tickets for the same topic, where if you counted the upvotes, they have significantly more interest. I.e. there are cases with an open issue with 50 votes, and 50 closed cases that each have 15 votes, so the sum of these demonstrates a much higher overall level of interest. The current process also seems to be causing numerous duplicate issues, because the 60 day window expires and it forces another issue to be generated (unnecessarily). And to me, the fact that despite being discouraged that their issue had been closed already, someone took the time to re-create and post the issue AGAIN, shows a level of passion not frequently found in many of these open issues which are actively being worked. I pretty religiously look at the release notes, and over the past year I haven't been excited for a single feature that I can recall (further evidence that features that are being produced seem really niche and not representative of what is desired by the most/the average user. Any possibility of refining these parameters? 250 votes in 180days? 100 votes in 90 days? To be clear, I'm not suggesting EVERY issue that's closed warrants consideration. I'm simply suggesting that the methodology may not be capturing what you're trying to capture and skews towards certain types of tickets being mistakenly prioritized as "popular". By allowing ticket to remain open LONGER (even if they require more upvotes to be considered) at least this gives them a chance to build momentum / stir up a buzz (ex. a discussion on reddit may direct users to a certain topic). Or maybe a panel of moderators reviews these with some alternative criteria than upvotes. Ex. Subjectively helps to prioritize ideas that seem innovative or that may be "low hanging fruit" (really quick/easy fixes).

title: Auto save trims the cursor line of a custom text editor in a side-by-side diff or with different path casing
text: Auto save trims the cursor line of a custom text editor in a side-by-side diff or with different path casing. Follow-up to which was fixed in That fix makes auto save leave the cursor line alone when trimming trailing whitespace and final newlines in custom text editors such as the Markdown editor: the trim save participants use the selection that the editor reports through the proposed API. Two cases still trim the line being typed on: - **Side-by-side custom diff:** when a custom editor is shown as one side of a side-by-side diff, the visible editor pane is the diff, whose input has no resource of its own when the two sides differ. The participants skip it, so the editable side's cursor line is trimmed on auto save. - **Path casing:** on a case-insensitive file system, a custom editor input can keep different path casing from the text model's URI. The case-sensitive comparison then misses the editor, and its cursor line is trimmed. title: Restored chat editor tabs show "Chat" instead of their session title until revealed
text: Restored chat editor tabs show "Chat" instead of their session title until revealed. After reloading the window, chat editor tabs that are not in the foreground show the generic title "Chat" instead of their session title. The real title only appears once a tab is revealed and its chat model is resolved. This affects tabs for agent host and other contributed chat session types (for example Copilot CLI sessions). Local chat sessions are not affected because their title is read from persisted session data. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Open several agent host chat sessions as editor tabs and send a message in each, so they get titles. 2. Reload the window. 3. Look at the tabs that are not active: they are labeled "Chat". Clicking one shows its real title. **Expected:** each restored chat tab shows its last known title immediately. **Cause:** falls back to "Chat" when there is no resolved model and does not know the session. That method only handles local sessions.

title: Agent host: chat created while the remote host connection is down cannot be restored (Session identity was not advertised)
text: Agent host: chat created while the remote host connection is down cannot be restored (Session identity was not advertised). When the connection to a remote agent host is down and VS Code has stopped reconnecting, sending the first message in a new chat for that host still creates a chat session on the client only. The host never creates it. After a reload, that chat's editor can't be restored and shows *"The editor could not be opened due to an unexpected error"*. **Try Again** keeps failing, and the prompt is lost. Version: 1.145.0-insider (commit c5f99e81a5d0ce82a55615da27c322bbe48ad00e), Windows, remote agent host over WebSocket ( provider). ## What happened (reconstructed from the renderer log) 1. The WebSocket connection to the remote agent host closed. retried in rounds ( , followed by and another round). After about 20 minutes, the rounds stopped. The window then stayed disconnected from that host for about 12 hours, with no further reconnect attempts in the log. 2. In that state, I opened a new chat for that host and sent a message: The request failed immediately, but the editor kept the materialized resource . The same failure had already happened once with an earlier new chat. 3. Later, the window reconnected to the host and was reloaded. Restoring that chat editor fails, and so does every **Try Again**: The error comes from in [agentHostSessionHandler.ts]( It refreshes identities through , and the ID isn't listed. I confirmed with an AHP call directly against the host: neither a session nor a chat with that ID exists. The host never received the session. ## Problems 1. **No recovery after reconnect gives up.** Once automatic reconnect stops, the host connection stays dead indefinitely, but the UI still lets you start chats and send messages to that host. The failure only appears after sending. 2. **The untitled session is materialized before the host confirms it.** If creating the session or sending the first message fails, the editor keeps a resource that will never exist on the host. That leaves an editor that can't be restored, and the user's prompt is lost. ## Expected - Keep reconnecting periodically (or on window focus or network change), or clearly show that the host is disconnected and block sending until it is reachable again. - If the first request fails before the host creates the session, keep or revert the chat as untitled and keep the prompt, so the user can resend it once the host is back. - When a restored chat refers to a session the host doesn't know, show a specific message instead of the generic "editor could not be opened" error.

title: Session nested under another can't be moved back out: "has no recorded conversation of its own"
text: Session nested under another can't be moved back out: "has no recorded conversation of its own". In today's Insiders, a session that was nested under another session can't be moved back out. **Steps** 1. Have an older session that isn't open in the Agents window (in my case a 4-month-old worktree session). 2. Drag it onto another session to nest it. The nest succeeds. 3. On the nested chat, run **Move to New Session** (or click **Undo** in the move notice). **Expected:** the chat becomes its own session again. **Actual:** the move fails every time. The agent host refuses it with: > Chat ahp-chat://default/… has no recorded conversation of its own to take into a new session. ( , from in .) The session's data is intact, but it stays stuck under the other session. Undo fails the same way, because Undo of a nest also moves the chat to a new session. **Cause (from the logs and the agent-host database):** after the nest, the moved session's main chat has no provider data in , i.e. no link to its own conversation. The destination session's own main chat does have it. The nest didn't record that link for the moved chat. Nests of sessions that were already loaded keep working; the one that failed here was an older session that wasn't loaded at the time of the nest.

title: Agents window: drag and drop onto a workspace revealed by "+N more workspaces" does nothing
text: Agents window: drag and drop onto a workspace revealed by "+N more workspaces" does nothing. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (core Agents window sessions list) - VS Code Version: 1.145.0 ( @ d7658021df8; root cause verified in code) - OS Version: macOS (not OS-specific) In the Agents window sessions list, workspaces can be reordered with drag and drop. When the capped workspaces are expanded with "+N more workspaces", there is an implicit line between the always-visible workspaces and the revealed ones. Any drop onto a revealed workspace fails: a drop indicator is shown, but the dragged item doesn't move there. It doesn't matter what is dragged: a workspace from above the line, another revealed workspace or a custom group. Steps to Reproduce: 1. In the Agents window, group sessions by Workspace, Repository or Environment, with Show > Recent (the default). 2. Have at least one workspace with a session updated in the last 4 days and at least two workspaces whose sessions are all older than that, so a "+N more workspaces" row appears. 3. Click "+N more workspaces" to reveal the capped workspaces. 4. Drag any workspace, from above the line or from the revealed ones, and drop it before or after one of the revealed workspaces. 5. 🐛 The drop indicator is shown, but nothing moves. For comparison, dropping onto a workspace above the line works, including when a revealed workspace is dragged there: it moves up and stays visible after collapsing. <details> <summary>Root cause</summary> - puts only custom groups and primary (uncapped) workspaces in the user-managed . Revealed "+N more" workspaces are appended after that block in their default order and aren't part of it ([sessionsList.ts#L5725-L5776]( - returns a drop for any top-level grouping section, including revealed ones, so the drop feedback looks valid ([sessionsList.ts#L7089-L7101]( - calls ([sessionsList.ts#L7154-L7164]( requires only the drop target, not the dragged item, to be in that order. When the target isn't there, it returns and silently returns ([sessionSectionOrderService.ts#L129-L133]( [#L262-L275]( - Before that, moves the dragged header to the top level, so a header dragged out of a custom group leaves its group but doesn't land where it was dropped. Drops onto headers above the line work because the target is in . A revealed workspace dragged there is also promoted so it escapes capping, by design (#322916). The tool already rejects revealed workspaces as targets explicitly ([sessionsList.ts#L7413-L7415]( </details> ### Expected behavior Dropping onto a revealed workspace should move the dragged item there, the same as dropping onto a workspace above the line. A workspace moved below the line should land where it's dropped and be hidden behind "+N more workspaces" when collapsed, until it's dragged back up. Only promotion exists today (there's no demotion state), so this leaves some design questions: - Capping is criteria-based, not a fixed count. A workspace stays above the line if it has a comparison group, a session updated in the last 4 days, the open window's folder or the onboarding session, if it has been promoted, or if it's the most-recent fallback ([sessionsList.ts#L5455-L5498]( If the visible block had a fixed size, the first workspace below the line might need to move up when one is moved down. - Should a moved-down workspace stay below the line when it gets new activity, or return above it? - Reordering revealed workspaces among themselves needs a persisted order for the revealed area. Today any successful drag also promotes the dragged workspace, which would move it above the line instead of where it was dropped. - What should happen when a custom group, which is never capped, is dropped below the line? *🤖 Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of .*

title: Local Hooks list stays empty for a hooks-only plugin until another plugin refreshes discovery
text: Local Hooks list stays empty for a hooks-only plugin until another plugin refreshes discovery. Testing #343747 ## Summary With only an enabled SDK-installed hooks-only plugin, **Customizations (Local) > Hooks** initially shows no hooks. Installing a mixed-contribution plugin from the same marketplace makes both plugins' hooks appear. Removing the mixed plugin leaves the original hooks-only plugin's two hooks visible. The observed Local inventory transition is **0 -> 4 -> 2**, without changing hook settings. ## Environment - Code OSS Dev 1.145.0, Windows 11 x64, main - Node.js 24.22.1 - Fresh isolated authenticated profile, empty workspace outside the fixture repository, and aligned disposable , , and - Fixture repository: at - Installation through the **Copilot** harness's SDK marketplace; the failing inventory surface is the **Local** harness, not a remote Agent Host ## Repro steps 1. Start the build above with a fresh profile and no installed test plugins. Use a separate, trusted disposable workspace. Keep the normal user/Copilot home untouched. 2. Verify **Chat: Use Hooks** ( ) is enabled. In the controlled run it was checked in both User and Workspace settings, editable, and unchanged throughout. was at its default ; these fixtures use Copilot-format . 3. Select the **Copilot** harness. Open **Customizations > Plugins > Configure Marketplaces**, add , and browse catalog . 4. Install **only **. 5. Select the **Local** harness by its visible picker label. Open **Customizations > Plugins** and verify is **Enabled**, its profile switch is checked, and its details report **2 hooks**. 6. Open **Hooks**. Leave the search empty. The page shows **User 0 / Workspace 0**, with no plugin hook rows. The recorded view was still empty approximately **40 seconds** after opening it. 7. Return to Copilot's marketplace and additionally install ** ** from the same catalog. Do not change settings or disable the hooks-only plugin. 8. Return to **Customizations (Local) > Hooks**. Now all **four** rows appear: and for each plugin. 9. Uninstall **only ** through Copilot Browse, then return to Local Hooks. The two ** ** rows remain visible. ## Expected The enabled hooks-only plugin's two hooks appear at step 6, without installing another plugin to refresh the inventory. ## Actual The initial list is empty. Adding the mixed plugin makes the previously missing hooks-only entries visible, and they remain visible after the mixed plugin is removed. ## Controls and scope - The modal title explicitly showed **Local** for each inventory observation; this was not inferred from an attempted harness switch. - The hooks-only plugin was enabled before the empty view. Both plugins were enabled in the positive control. - **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** showed an inactive account gate, zero managed-setting keys, and **0 applied policies**. The managed-hooks-only and strict-plugin-only policies were not applied. No policy was changed or bypassed. - The controlled workspace was trusted via the process-scoped launch flag. - The private profile had only the launcher's title/simple-dialog settings; there were no workspace settings, and the settings hash did not change. - No model-backed Local runtime was tested: **zero SDK user messages/tool executions**, no fixture hook marker file, and no manual MCP Start. This report is about **Local UI inventory/refresh**, not a claim that Local hooks failed to execute. - The sequence is consistent with initialization/refresh behavior, but the code cause and whether other actions can trigger recovery have not been established. Related but distinct: #343572 and #330114 concern Copilot Agent Host hook publication. This report concerns the controlled **Local** inventory transition above.

title: Markdown editor: custom code block editor iframe stays in place when lines are inserted above it
text: Markdown editor: custom code block editor iframe stays in place when lines are inserted above it. In the Markdown editor, code blocks with a custom code block editor (for example a Mermaid diagram) render the editor in an iframe that floats over the block. Inserting a new line above such a block moves the block down, but the iframe stays at its old position and covers the wrong content. Steps: 1. Open a Markdown file containing a mermaid block in the Markdown editor. 2. Place the caret on the line above the block and press Enter. 3. The diagram iframe does not move with the block. The editor view asks the embedded editor factory to reposition its iframes after each render ( ), but the extension's lazily loading factory wrapper does not forward that call. The iframe is then only repositioned on scroll or resize, not on edits that move the block without resizing the editor.

title: MCP authentication spinner stops animating while sign-in is in progress
text: MCP authentication spinner stops animating while sign-in is in progress. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured - VS Code Version: Insiders; exact reporting build not captured - OS Version: macOS; exact version not captured - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host chat, MCP authentication - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not captured - Logs: Not collected; source-level investigation below Steps to Reproduce: 1. With persistent chat progress enabled (the current default), start a chat that requires MCP server authentication. 2. Select **Authenticate** and observe the inline “Authenticating ...” indicator while sign-in is running. **Actual:** The spinner stops animating while the authentication message remains visible, making it look as though sign-in has stalled. **Expected:** The indicator should communicate that authentication is still running, rather than appear frozen (unless reduced motion is enabled). ### Source-level RCA The [MCP authentication component explicitly requests a spinning loading icon]( and [awaits authentication before clearing its active state]( However, the [persistent-progress CSS rule]( applies to descendant elements. Terminal and subagent indicators are exempted, but the MCP authentication indicator is not. This suppresses the animation without cancelling authentication. The rule originated in #336087. This explains the frozen indicator in source; it has not been independently reproduced in a live window. The actual authentication outcome was not established. Duplicate check: #340546 concerns a rejected-token retry loop and a persistent Authenticating state in Customizations, rather than this inline spinner's animation being suppressed. No matching animation report found. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: Agent Host BYOK custom endpoint (DeepSeek v4-pro): multi-turn tool-call history loses reasoning_content → 400 "reasoning_text in the thinking mode must be passed back"
text: Agent Host BYOK custom endpoint (DeepSeek v4-pro): multi-turn tool-call history loses reasoning_content → 400 "reasoning_text in the thinking mode must be passed back". Summary Using the Agent Host chat (provider copilotcli) with a BYOK custom endpoint pointed at the official DeepSeek API (deepseek-v4-pro, thinking enabled), a multi-turn tool-call conversation eventually fails with a 400 claiming the reasoning text must be passed back. Short conversations and non-tool turns succeed; the failure appears only after several tool-call rounds (e.g. starting multiple background shells and then reading terminal output). The error names reasoning_text (Copilot/CAPI dialect), while DeepSeek officially expects reasoning_content. Since the endpoint URL is (no proxy), the reasoning_text wording appears to be produced by the Agent Host/CLI layer, not DeepSeek. Environment VS Code: 1.143.1 (macOS) /copilot: 1.0.100-1 /copilot-sdk: 1.0.23-preview.5 OS: Darwin arm64 24.6.0 Chat surface: Agent Host ("智能体主机"), provider copilotcli Model: customendpoint/ds/deepseek-v4-pro, apiType: chat-completions, thinking: true Endpoint: (official, no proxy/reverse proxy) Steps to reproduce Configure a BYOK custom endpoint for DeepSeek deepseek-v4-pro with thinking enabled. Open the Agent Host chat. Have the agent start several background shells and then call the terminal-read tool, across multiple turns. At some later turn the request fails. Expected The request succeeds. Every assistant message that carries tool_calls also carries the model's reasoning_content, as DeepSeek requires for thinking-mode tool-call conversations. Actual The request is retried 5 times (same payload) and then surfaced as an error. ### Notes / pointers - — only carries / ; there is no . - — maps a reasoning item to a chat part and consecutive assistant messages are merged (L236-L240). Long histories / pruning can leave a tool-call assistant message without the thinking part. - — only writes when is true. - — renames ↔ depending on / mode and strips / , which looks lossy for providers that require the full reasoning chain on every tool-call turn. - — and the server-error retry path. ### Workaround Disabling thinking for this model (non-thinking mode), or using a short conversation without repeated tool calls, avoids the failure. ### Additional context The failure correlates with history length rather than with any single tool: non-tool turns and short tool-call sequences succeed; only longer multi-turn tool-call histories (background shells + terminal reads) trigger it. This suggests the reasoning is lost/pruned from one assistant tool-call message during replay, rather than the field name being wrong from the start.

title: [Agent Host] Freeform-only question answers leave cloud sessions waiting
text: [Agent Host] Freeform-only question answers leave cloud sessions waiting. # Freeform-only question answers leave cloud Agent Host sessions waiting ## Summary In the VS Code Agents Window, entering a custom response to a single-select question can leave a cloud Agent Host session waiting indefinitely after submission. The question explicitly allows free-form input, but VS Code encodes the response as a text answer instead of a selection answer. The cloud host rejects the incompatible answer kind, so the pending call never completes. Selecting a listed option succeeds. This is an answer-encoding mismatch, not a connection failure or slow model response. ## Environment - VS Code Agents Window. - Cloud Agent Host backed by copilotd. - A single-select question with . ## Reproduction 1. In a cloud Agent Host session, have the agent ask a single-select question with two options, such as "Red" and "Blue", and allow a custom response. 2. Do not select either option. 3. Enter a free-form response, such as "Green". 4. Submit the response. These are illustrative reproduction values, not captured conversation content. ## Expected behavior The custom response is accepted and delivered to the agent. The question completes and the session continues. The answer retains the protocol's kind, with the custom response carried in . ## Actual behavior VS Code submits a answer for the single-select question. The cloud host rejects the answer-kind mismatch and leaves the input request unresolved. The session appears hung on the question tool. The diagnosis identified two occurrences of this failure and a successful listed-option submission. Transport remained responsive after the failures. ## Root cause [convertCarouselAnswers in agentHostSessionHandler.ts]( handles an answer with as a selection. However, its [freeform-only fallback]( unconditionally emits when only is present. The function already receives question metadata, but the fallback does not use the question kind to distinguish a free-form selection from a genuine text question. The cloud host's [check_answer_kind validator]( requires for a question. Its [input bridge]( already supports custom selection responses through . Allowing free-form input does not make the correct selection answer kind. ## Suggested fix - Make freeform-only answer conversion question-kind-aware. - For a single-select question, preserve and populate . - Cover the analogous multi-select case using . - Preserve existing conversion for genuine text questions, listed selections, combined selection/custom responses, and boolean questions. - Surface rejected input submissions clearly and keep the question retryable instead of leaving the user with an apparent hang. ## Regression coverage The existing [freeform-only conversion test]( expects a text answer without supplying question metadata. It does not cover the failing single-select case with metadata. Add coverage for: 1. Single-select plus freeform-only input: produces with . 2. Multi-select plus freeform-only input: produces with . 3. Genuine text input: continues to produce . 4. Listed-option and option-plus-freeform input: preserve existing behavior. 5. Cloud round trip: custom response is accepted, the pending question tool completes, and the agent continues. 6. Rejected submission: a visible error and a usable retry path. ## Workaround Stop the pending turn and send the intended answer as a normal chat message, asking the agent to continue without another question. Selecting a listed option also works when an offered option accurately represents the intended answer. ## Scope and privacy This report documents diagnosis only, not an implemented fix. Source references were inspected read-only; the exact deployed VS Code commit was not established. No implementation tests were run. No logs, log excerpts, diagnostic archives, captured answer payloads, session identifiers, or private conversation content are included or attached. *🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of .*

title: Built-in GitHub MCP authentication stalls when a connector-scoped token needs repo access
text: Built-in GitHub MCP authentication stalls when a connector-scoped token needs repo access. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not provided. - VS Code Version: Not provided. - OS Version: Not provided. - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host, built-in GitHub MCP server authentication and Customizations view. - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not provided. - Logs: An Agent Host debug export ( ) was shared in the original discussion. The archive is not attached here. ## Summary The built-in GitHub MCP server requests authentication, but clicking **Authenticate** does not unblock the tool call. The reporter also tried **Start** in the Customizations view, with no visible effect. The investigation reported by points to GitHub MCP being mistaken for a Copilot Connector because an inherited OAuth scope contains . The connector authentication path then reuses a token without the newly required scope, and restarting the server waits on the turn that is itself blocked on authentication. ## Steps to Reproduce The following preconditions and sequence are reconstructed from the reported investigation; this issue was not independently reproduced while filing. 1. Have multiple GitHub authentication sessions, including: - - - - , created when authorizing a connector and lacking . 2. Start an agent session using the built-in GitHub MCP server. The agent host selects the least-permission session satisfying , resulting in the three-scope connector session rather than either four-scope session with . 3. Invoke a GitHub MCP tool requiring , such as against a repository requiring that scope. 4. When authentication is requested, click **Authenticate**. 5. Also try **Start** for the built-in GitHub MCP server in the Customizations view. **Actual:** Neither action unblocks the operation; the tool call remains waiting for authentication. **Expected:** Authentication obtains a credential covering the required GitHub MCP scopes, passes it to the correct consumer, and resumes the blocked operation. A scope inherited from an existing token must not, by itself, classify the built-in GitHub MCP server as a Connector. Required authentication/restart work must not wait for the blocked turn to finish. ## Reported Authentication Sequence 1. The built-in GitHub MCP server reuses the agent host's token. Initial connection succeeds with , despite the token lacking . 2. is rejected and GitHub MCP requests . 3. The runtime merges the requested scope with the existing token scopes, so VS Code receives . 4. VS Code treats a request containing as a Connector request and routes it through connector authentication instead of normal GitHub MCP token acquisition. 5. Connector authentication finds the existing connector-scoped session, considers authorization satisfied, and resends the same token without . 6. The server restart waits for the current turn to finish, while that turn is waiting for authentication, leaving the operation stuck. ## Suggested Regression Coverage - A connector-scoped GitHub session without coexists with broader GitHub sessions, and the built-in GitHub MCP server subsequently requests . - Both the in-turn **Authenticate** action and the Customizations **Start** action acquire/forward a credential covering the requested scopes and unblock the operation. - Real Connector authentication continues to work, without treating any MCP request containing the connector scope as a Connector request. - Authentication recovery does not depend on completion of the turn blocked on that authentication. ## Related Related but distinct from #341123 (closed), which tracked WorkIQ/Kusto Connector Sign In continuing to forward an insufficiently scoped token. This issue concerns the built-in GitHub MCP server being routed through Connector authentication because of an inherited connector scope.

title: Markdown Editor: typing lag grows with document size (full re-parse and re-measure on every keystroke)
text: Markdown Editor: typing lag grows with document size (full re-parse and re-measure on every keystroke). Typing in the Markdown Editor ( ) lags noticeably on larger files. On a ~96 KB Markdown file (≈2,600 lines of headings, paragraphs, lists, blockquotes and tables), each keystroke keeps the editor webview busy for ~600–800 ms, so typed text appears seconds later. The plain Text Editor has no noticeable lag on the same file. Reported in (problem 2). Problem 1 of that issue (auto save scrambling typed text) has a separate fix. ### Where the time goes A CPU profile of the webview while typing 10 characters at the end of the first heading (Code OSS, local build) shows two costs that both scale with document size and run on every keystroke: - **~300 ms: full re-parse.** in always parses the whole text with micromark, then reconciles the fresh tree against the previous one. Reconciliation preserves node identity, but parsing itself is not incremental. - **~300 ms: full re-measurement.** in re-measures every block's ( over every text leaf, plus per block), even for blocks whose view node and size are unchanged. When frames are this long, key events can also appear reordered: for example followed quickly by a typed character inserted the character before the caret moved. ### Expected Typing cost should depend mostly on the edited block, not on the document size: e.g. reuse measurements of unchanged blocks (translated when blocks above change height) and re-parse only the affected top-level block range. ### Repro 1. Open a ~100 KB Markdown file with the Markdown Editor. 2. Switch to editing mode and type a sentence at normal speed. 3. Observe that text appears with a multi-second delay.

title: Agent host: copilot-runtime grows to 46 GB RSS and is OOM-killed, wedging the host
text: Agent host: copilot-runtime grows to 46 GB RSS and is OOM-killed, wedging the host. ## Summary On a remote Linux agent host, the child grew to **45.9 GB anonymous RSS** over 7 days. The kernel OOM killer then killed it, and the agent host wedged the same way as #342774. This confirms the OOM/SIGKILL theory in root cause 4 of that issue. The runtime held far more memory than the session history it had loaded: - The 5 sessions it held locks on at the kill had **2.4 GB** of on disk, about **19×** less than its RSS. - All 19 sessions it attached during its 7-day lifetime total **4.9 GB** on disk, about **9×** less. - It reached **13.5 GB within 2 minutes of starting**, after resuming 4 sessions. See the [earlier comment]( on #342774; that measurement was this same process. ## Environment - VS Code Insiders , commit (2026-10-19) - / - Remote agent host over SSH: Ubuntu, kernel , aarch64 (NVIDIA GB10), 128 GB RAM, no swap - Client: Agents window on macOS ## Kernel evidence At 01:55:13Z the agent host hit the same in as #342774. This host has now wedged that way three times: 2026-10-13, 2026-10-19, and 2026-10-27. ## Memory at the time of the kill The kernel's process dump, grouped by process name, totals 116 GB: | Process | Count | RSS | |---|---|---| | | 1 | 45.9 GB | | (agent-launched test workers) | 34 | 22.5 GB | | VS Code server ( ), including the agent host file watcher at 15.6 GB | 9 | 19.9 GB | | Rust test binaries (agent-launched) | 6 | 12.2 GB | | Everything else | — | ~15.5 GB | The agent host, the runtime, and every process the agents spawn share one cgroup ( , ). That cgroup has recorded 409 OOM kills this boot. The runtime is by far the largest process in it, so it is the OOM killer's first choice whenever agent-launched builds or tests push the machine over. That kills the process that coordinates every session, instead of the test worker that caused the spike. ## Runtime lifetime (PID 3851385) | Time (UTC) | Event | |---|---| | 2026-10-20 01:36:06 | Runtime starts and resumes 4 sessions | | ~01:38 | 13.5 GB RSS, still growing about 0.9 GB per 30 s at ~40% CPU | | 10-20 → 10-26 | 19 distinct sessions attached (38 events). Nothing in the runtime log shows a session being unloaded or evicted. | | 2026-10-27 01:55:06 | OOM-killed at 45.9 GB anon RSS, with tool calls in flight in 2 sessions | Neither the runtime log nor records any memory telemetry, so the growth between the first and last points is unknown. ## What the history contains This is the largest session open at the time of the kill: a 555 MB with 151,596 events. | Event type | Count | Size on disk | Largest | |---|---|---|---| | | 17,291 | 231.5 MB | 207 KB | | | 378 | 116.1 MB | 4.0 MB | | | 16,590 | 77.3 MB | 134 KB | | | 30,383 | 52.0 MB | 66 KB | | | 12,995 | 27.7 MB | 3 KB | | | 16,590 | 20.0 MB | 65 KB | Other sessions open at the kill had 1.38 GB, 337 MB, 139 MB, and 8 MB of history. ## Expected - Runtime memory should stay bounded relative to the history it serves. For example, don't keep full histories, especially binary assets, resident for idle or resumed sessions, and evict sessions that are no longer active. - The runtime should not be the OOM killer's first choice over the processes it spawns. For example, give spawned tool and shell processes a higher than the runtime, or run them in their own cgroup. - The agent host should log the runtime's exit signal and recover, as described in #342774. title: run_in_terminal: clearing pending PowerShell input depends on the PSReadLine edit mode, not the OS
text: run_in_terminal: clearing pending PowerShell input depends on the PSReadLine edit mode, not the OS. Follow-up from When falls back to the basic or no-shell-integration execute strategies, it decides whether to send Ctrl+U to clear pending prompt input from the OS: PowerShell on Windows never gets Ctrl+U, PowerShell elsewhere does. Whether Ctrl+U clears the line actually depends on the PSReadLine edit mode: - **Windows edit mode** (default on Windows): Ctrl+U has no binding and is inserted into the command line. - **Emacs edit mode** (default on macOS and Linux): Ctrl+U is and clears the line. That leaves two cases: 1. **Windows with Emacs or Vi edit mode:** pending input is no longer cleared, so the agent's command is appended to it. For example, pending plus runs . 2. **macOS or Linux with :** Ctrl+U is still sent and inserted into the command line, the same failure fixed on Windows. Steps to reproduce (case 2, from reading the code, not yet run): 1. On macOS, make pwsh the default profile, add to , and set . 2. Ask the agent to run . 3. In the agent's terminal, type at the prompt without pressing Enter. 4. Ask the agent to run again. Expected: the pending text is cleared and runs. Actual: Ctrl+U ends up in the command line and the command fails. Possible direction: the pwsh shell integration script already reports PSReadLine-derived properties through (for example ). It could also report the edit mode so the clearing key is picked from that, falling back to the current OS default when shell integration isn't active. Authored by Copilot on behalf of anthonykim1

title: Markdown editor: render Mermaid diagrams like the Markdown preview
text: Markdown editor: render Mermaid diagrams like the Markdown preview. In the experimental Markdown editor, Mermaid code blocks look different from the same diagram in the Markdown preview: - **Theme:** the editor uses Mermaid's default (purple, light) theme instead of the VS Code theme mapping the preview uses. text: remote.portsAttributes: requireLocalPort is ignored for port ranges. ## Summary accepts port ranges, but a matching range rule with does not show the documented warning when forwarding uses a different local port. An exact numeric port rule with the same flag correctly shows the warning. The range still applies its , so the failure is not that the rule fails to match. is dropped while resolving the attributes. ## Environment and verification scope - VS Code: **1.119.0-insider**, commit , arm64. - OS: **macOS 26.2**, build . - Installed user extensions disabled; a local extension development host supplied the reproduction fixture. - VS Code product code was unmodified. - Source analysis used upstream at . **Reproduced in the running VS Code desktop app:** range rule with , exact-port rule with , and exact-port rule with . **Checked only in an isolated source-class harness:** host-and-port and process-command regex rules also lose . Their missing-dialog behavior was **not** reproduced in the desktop app. The desktop reproduction uses a controlled local tunnel provider, not a Remote SSH or Dev Containers connection. The fixture creates real loopback TCP forwarding through , exercising VS Code's forwarding model, configuration resolution, Ports view, and native dialog service. It does not replace those VS Code components. ## Reproduction steps [Download the self-contained source fixture]( It contains the extension source, initial workspace settings, and README; no dependency installation is needed. 1. Extract the archive. Ensure loopback ports **45321** and **45322** are free. From the extracted directory, launch: On macOS, if the CLI is not on PATH, use the installed application's . 2. Wait **more than ten seconds** after startup. VS Code's mismatch-dialog cooldown otherwise suppresses even the positive control. 3. Run **Repro: Range Rule** from the Command Palette. It configures: The fixture opens remote port 45321, requesting local port 45322. A fixture server already occupies 45322. The provider attempts it, receives , chooses another local port, and forwards to the HTTP application. 4. Open the Ports view. The row has label **Repro range**, confirming the range matched. The local port differs from 45322, but **no mismatch warning appears**. 5. Run **Repro: Exact Port Rule**. It closes the previous tunnel and replaces the range with the exact key , keeping . The same conflict now produces the expected mismatch warning. 6. Dismiss the warning, wait more than ten seconds, then run **Repro: Exact Port False Control**. It uses exact key with ; forwarding succeeds without a warning, as expected. 7. Close the development host to stop the fixture servers and tunnels. The fixture also includes optional host-and-port and fallback commands; those were **not completed in the recorded desktop run**. ## Expected and actual results A matched range with should show the same warning as a matched exact-port rule when the requested local port cannot be used. This setting requests a warning; it does not prohibit forwarding to another port. | Case | Actual local port in recorded run | Mismatch warning | Verification | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Range, | 61303 instead of 45322 | **Missing** | VS Code desktop | | Exact port, | 61380 instead of 45322 | **Shown** | VS Code desktop | | Exact port, | 61452 instead of 45322 | Absent, as expected | VS Code desktop | | Host-and-port, | Not tested in desktop | Resolved flag was | Source-class harness only | | Process regex, | Not tested in desktop | Resolved flag was | Source-class harness only | All three desktop forwards returned HTTP 200 with the expected fixture response. title: Terminal sticky scroll stays a white bar after its WebGL context is lost
text: Terminal sticky scroll stays a white bar after its WebGL context is lost. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.144.0-insider (7cc5e7382b284f2156375fcedc388b44a07c0487) - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (Apple silicon) When the sticky scroll overlay's WebGL context is lost and not restored, the overlay keeps the lost canvas: a white bar with Chromium's sad-face placeholder where the command should be. The terminal itself falls back to the DOM renderer in the same situation after 3 seconds. The overlay never does, so it stays broken until the window is reloaded or is toggled. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Set , open a terminal with shell integration (the default), and run so sticky scroll shows . 2. Run **Developer: Toggle Developer Tools** and evaluate: 3. Wait more than 3 seconds, then run . **Expected:** like the terminal, the overlay falls back to the DOM renderer and shows . **Actual:** 13 seconds later, after new commands, the overlay is still a white bar (screenshot). ![Terminal panel whose sticky scroll row is a white bar instead of the seq 1 100 command]( A real GPU process loss gives the same result when Chromium doesn't restore WebGL contexts, which happened after repeated GPU process restarts. Both terminals fell back to the DOM renderer and rendered correctly, while both sticky scroll overlays kept the sad face (screenshot). ![Two split terminals rendering text normally, each with a white sticky scroll bar showing a sad-face icon]( ### Cause ([terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L510-L526]( loads a but never subscribes to . does subscribe, and disposes the addon ([xtermTerminal.ts#L956-L961]( History: WebGL for sticky scroll was added in the terminal's DOM fallback is from ### Possible fix Subscribe to in and clear . calls again on every terminal resize, configuration change and theme change ([terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts#L478-L487]( so it would recreate the addon immediately. Loading the addon throws while WebGL2 is unavailable. Before re-enabling, either remember the loss or follow the terminal's own renderer. --- (Authored by Copilot on behalf of anthonykim1)

In my logs that happened on all 18 refreshes between the promotion at 09:32Z and 12:22Z, 8 of them in the last 80 minutes. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Set . 2. In the Agents window, open a Copilot CLI session and add a second chat to it, so it shows as a nested chat in the sessions list. 3. Send a prompt in that nested chat and wait for the turn to finish while it is open, so the chat is read. Promotion requires a started turn. 4. In the sessions list, right-click the nested chat and choose **Promote to Session**. 5. The new session opens and appears read. 6. Wait for the next sessions-list refresh (usually a few minutes apart in my logs). **Expected:** the promoted session stays read. **Actual:** the promoted session shows as unread again after every refresh. Opening it, or **Mark as Read** (Shift+I), clears the indicator only until the next refresh. ### Evidence Excerpt from the client's AHP transport log ( and ). I removed titles, prompts and paths. Status bits: , , . - Promoted chat (now the new session's default chat): - New session: | Time (UTC) | Dir | Message | Session | Chat | |---|---|---|---|---| | 09:32:51.659 | c2s | → | | | | 09:32:51.929 | s2c | | ** ** (Idle, unread) | ** ** (Idle, IsRead) | | 09:32:51.930 | c2s | on | | | | 09:32:52.433 | s2c | echo of . **No follows.** | | | | 09:42:50 → 12:22:50 | s2c | 18 results | every time | every time | | 09:46:13, 10:24:29, 10:46:13, 12:06:43 | c2s | Session opened again → . Echoed each time; still no . | | | | 12:13:36.364 | s2c | next after the 12:06:43 open, **7 minutes later**: unread again | | | The session starts out unread while its only chat is read, and it never leaves that state. The renderer applies each result ([ ]( which flips the session back to unread. The wrong flag exists only in the host's in-memory summary from the promotion: overlays it via , while the persisted read state is correct. That's why a host restart clears it (see Workarounds). ### Root cause 1. **Promotion creates the session as unread.** [ ]( passes with no bit. [ ]( keeps the chat's summary, including its own bit. [ ]( then keeps the session's unset flag. Everywhere else, a session with a single chat has the same read state as that chat. The catalog resolver, , and restore all keep them in sync; promotion is the only path that doesn't. 2. **Nothing repairs it.** Since #339732, the Agents window marks a session read only through its main chat ([ ]( → [ ]( → ) and relies on the host to update the session. The host only does that when the chat goes from unread to read ([loaded session]( [unloaded session]( This chat is already read, so the read is a no-op and the session stays unread. Introduced by the combination of #339732 (session read state synced from chats) and #341788 (promote a chat to its own session). Both are in the Insiders build above. ### Workarounds (verified) I verified these against the unfixed host code with a probe that reproduces this exact state: reports session and chat . - **Right-click the session's section header → Mark All as Read.** This sends , which marks the session read, and it stays read whether or not the host has the session loaded. Opening the session or using **Mark as Read** (Shift+I) doesn't help, because both send only . Note: this marks every unread session in that section read. - **Developer: Restart Local Agent Host** (or quit and reopen). After a restart the session is listed read with no other action. The wrong flag exists only in the host's in-memory summary created at promotion; the persisted read state is correct. Restarting interrupts any running turns.

title: Agents window: Akusto #kusto tool in a background session opens Kusto Explorer in the focused session
text: Agents window: Akusto #kusto tool in a background session opens Kusto Explorer in the focused session. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No. It requires Akusto Explorer ( 0.5.2026092201). Any extension tool that opens an editor would behave the same way. - VS Code Version: 1.144.0-insider (7cc5e7382b284f2156375fcedc388b44a07c0487) - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (arm64) Steps to Reproduce: 1. In the Agents window, start session **A** and ask the agent to run Kusto queries ( ). 2. While A is working, switch focus to session **B**. 3. 🐛 When A runs its first or , a **Kusto Explorer** editor tab opens in **B's** editor area and stays in B's editor tabs. ## Why this happens **Akusto:** - The tools call on their first invocation in the extension host ( ). - In the Agents window, is hidden ( ). As a result, falls back to , which calls . - There is only one Explorer per window, and queries use . Results from any session can therefore replace what another session is showing. **Agents window:** - All sessions share one extension host and one editor part. The editor tabs and active editor belong to the **focused** chat ( , sections 1 and 5). - An editor opened by an extension does not record which session caused it, so resolves to the focused session, not the one that invoked the tool. - A tool can identify the session that invoked it only through the opaque or the private proposed . Extensions have no API to: - open an editor or webview panel for a specific chat session, or - find out whether that session is the focused one. So even a well-behaved extension cannot place its UI correctly. ## Possible fixes **Akusto (short term):** When running in the Agents window, don't open the editor fallback from tool calls. Keep it for explicit commands such as . The tool result could tell the model and user that results are available in Kusto Explorer and include a command link to open it. **Platform:** 1. Let tools target editor opens at the session that invoked them. For example, accept the or a session resource in and in the show options. The editor would join that session's editor tabs, and the focused session would be unchanged. 2. Alternatively, provide the focused chat session to extensions so tools can avoid revealing UI when their session is not focused.

title: New remote (Codespace) installs synced extensions even when Extensions is unchecked in Settings Sync
text:
New remote (Codespace) installs synced extensions even when Extensions is unchecked in Settings Sync. Type: Bug - VS Code Version: 1.143.1 (commit e646868227c3e3a9e3f24277c8c7220be42c0be7) - OS Version: Windows x64 (desktop client); remote is a GitHub Codespace (Debian 12) - Settings Sync: on, signed in with GitHub; **Extensions** and **MCP Servers** unchecked in "Settings Sync: Configure" ## Steps to reproduce 1. At some point, sync extensions with Settings Sync (GitHub account), so the cloud store has an Extensions resource. 2. Later, run "Settings Sync: Configure" and uncheck **Extensions**. Leave Settings Sync on for settings, keybindings, etc. 3. From desktop VS Code, create and connect to a new Codespace whose lists only under . **Expected:** The Codespace has only the extensions from (plus image and Codespaces defaults). I excluded extensions from sync, and the Settings Sync docs say extensions aren't synced to remote windows. **Actual:** About 40 extensions from the old synced list (for me, the extensions I had installed: Python, Jupyter, C#, PowerShell, other AI coding agents, etc.) are installed into the Codespace about 3 seconds after the server starts. The same repository opened in VS Code for the Web gets only the extensions. ## Cause in [src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/electron-browser/remoteExtensionsInit.ts]( checks only that Settings Sync as a whole is enabled. It then reads the Extensions resource from the sync store: It never checks whether the Extensions resource is enabled. Unchecking Extensions stops future uploads but leaves the last uploaded list in the store, so every new remote gets that stale list. Suggested fix: also skip when the Extensions resource is disabled (e.g., ). ## Why it matters People use dev containers and Codespaces to isolate untrusted or project-specific environments, and carefully list the extensions that should run there. These installs bypass that, and they pass , so publishers the user never trusted in that remote are installed without a prompt. Unchecking Extensions is the documented way to keep extensions out of sync, so users reasonably believe they're protected. Workarounds: "Settings Sync: Show Synced Data" → "Reset Synced Data" (deletes the stale list), turn Settings Sync off entirely, or add extensions to (honored by ). ## Log evidence Remote server arguments (only two extensions requested, sync disabled on the server): Client-initiated installs, matching the options in ( , ): (41 installs with these options between 20:37:01 and 20:37:06.) title: Flaky Windows build: Node.js compile cache generation leaves an interrupted shared-process cache entry
text: Flaky Windows build: Node.js compile cache generation leaves an interrupted shared-process cache entry. **Signature:** Windows x64 fails during Node.js compile cache generation ( ): - **Latest hit:** main CI [488834]( on Oct 23, , Electron 43.8.3 / node 24.22.1. The next run is expected to pass. - **Rate:** 1 in 170 failed or partial def 111 builds since Oct 16. It's rare, but official builds run the same step on Windows, so it can also fail an insider or stable build. Recovery is "Rerun failed jobs". - **Cause:** the leftover entry is Node.js's interrupted temp write, left when a utility process (here, the shared process) exits in the middle of a cache write during generation. That matches the investigation in #343049. You reproduced it there on Oct 21 and mentioned a generator lifetime fix. The label does not distinguish scheduled/running removal, a safety-related deferral (for example, another session still using the worktree), a reported removal error, or an unknown previous outcome. ### Expected behavior - Allow a safe cleanup retry for leftover worktrees belonging to sessions already marked as done, without restoring the session or deleting its history. - Keep scheduled/running removal non-selectable to avoid duplicate requests. - Show authoritative cleanup status when available. When removal reports an error, expose its reason accessibly and offer retry. - Do not infer failure merely because a worktree remains after a timeout. Preserve safety checks for shared worktrees and uncommitted changes. ### Investigation The cleanup service classifies every archived session as , while the editor’s manual-selection predicate only allows , , and . Archiving requests asynchronous host-owned worktree removal, so an archived session does not imply its worktree was removed. Simply enabling the checkbox is insufficient: retry must explicitly reschedule worktree removal rather than relying on another archive state change. Implementation and regression tests are in progress in a draft pull request.

title: Relaunched terminals ignore windowsReparentConsoleWindow being turned off
text: Relaunched terminals ignore windowsReparentConsoleWindow being turned off. Found while reviewing by reading the code at fb04e9e3d8e4bc56375e4795d7fdc8ff4293f2b3. The Windows steps below haven't been run yet. Turning off stops new terminals from making VS Code the owner of their console window. An existing terminal that relaunches still makes VS Code the owner. ### Steps to reproduce On Windows, with a local terminal and on: 1. With on (the default), open a terminal. 2. Set to . 3. Run **Terminal: Relaunch Active Terminal**. 4. In the relaunched shell, check who owns the console window: **Expected:** is the same as , because nothing owns the console window. **Actual (from the code):** is the VS Code window. The relaunched process is sent the window handle that was saved before the setting was turned off. The same happens for the other relaunches that go through the terminal's existing process manager: the seamless relaunch after environment variable changes, the relaunch with shell integration disabled, and the relaunch after a pty host restart. ### Cause - returns early when the setting is off, but it doesn't clear the saved and ([terminalProcessManager.ts#L781-L792]( Nothing else clears them. - Relaunching reuses the same manager ([terminalInstance.ts#L1936]( and calls ([terminalProcessManager.ts#L459-L474]( looks up the saved window ([#L373-L375]( and sends the saved handle before ([#L388-L389]( doesn't check the setting either ([#L819-L828]( - The "does nothing when the setting is disabled" test ([terminalProcessManager.test.ts#L464-L469]( turns the setting off before any window is saved, so it doesn't cover this. Two related cases have the same cause: - If a terminal was created while the setting was off, turning it on and relaunching doesn't set an owner. - Moving a terminal to another window while the setting is off leaves the old window saved, so a later relaunch uses the old window. ### Why it matters This setting is how to turn the behavior off if it causes problems, such as the VS Code window staying disabled when a dialog's process dies ( It has ([terminalConfiguration.ts#L501-L510]( so an experiment can turn it off in the middle of a session. Until the window reloads, terminals that relaunch keep getting VS Code as their owner. A reload creates new process managers, so relaunches after it honor the setting. Terminals that reconnect after the reload keep their existing owner until their shell exits, because nothing removes an owner from a running console. ### Suggested fix - Check the setting every time a process is created, in or , not only in . - Keep saving the terminal's current window while the setting is off, so turning it back on works for relaunches and moves. - Clear the saved handle when the window changes, so a failed lookup for the new window can't send the old window's handle. - Add tests to the suite: - Setting on, , , setting off, : the relaunched process's calls should be . - Setting off, , , setting on, : the relaunched process's calls should be . - Window 4's lookup succeeds, then with a lookup that fails, then : the relaunched process shouldn't be sent window 4's handle.
