title: Agent-host chats ignore chat.agentSkillsLocations, so personal skills in ~/.claude/skills are no longer loaded
text: Agent-host chats ignore chat.agentSkillsLocations, so personal skills in ~/.claude/skills are no longer loaded. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> ## Description Since chats run on the Copilot CLI agent host by default, VS Code's skill-location setting chat.agentSkillsLocations is no longer applied. Personal skills in ~/.claude/skills still appear in VS Code's default skill locations, but agent-host chat sessions never load them. I did not opt into the agent host. It is the default, and I see no obvious way to start a chat on VS Code's own agent instead. In practice, the setting has no effect. ## Steps to reproduce Create a personal skill at ~/.claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md with valid frontmatter (name, description). Make sure neither ~/.copilot/skills nor ~/.agents/skills exists. Start a new chat in VS Code with default settings, so it runs on the agent host. Ask the agent which skills it has, or trigger the skill by its description. ### Expected The skill is loaded. ~/.claude/skills is one of the default entries of chat.agentSkillsLocations (source claude-personal), and Claude Code loads it too. ### Actual The skill is missing from the session's skill list. Project skills (<repo>/.claude/skills, .github/skills) and plugin skills load, but no personal skills from ~/.claude/skills do. ## Analysis The agent host creates sessions with enableConfigDiscovery: true. It passes skillDirectories only for skills from plugins and extensions, not from the chat.agentSkillsLocations setting. The CLI runtime only scans ~/.copilot/skills and ~/.agents/skills for personal skills. ~/.claude/skills is only scanned at the project level (<repo>/.claude/skills). Older bundled CLI versions even list ~/.claude/skills as a personal folder in their "No skills found" help text, without scanning it. As a result, VS Code's default skill locations and what agent-host sessions actually load don't match. Any custom path added to chat.agentSkillsLocations is presumably ignored as well. Suggested fix Either pass the folders from chat.agentSkillsLocations to agent-host sessions via skillDirectories, or align the CLI's personal skill folders with VS Code's defaults by adding ~/.claude/skills. If the setting no longer applies, VS Code should at least say so instead of ignoring it silently. ## Workaround ln -s ~/.claude/skills ~/.agents/skills, then start a new chat. ## Environment - VS Code 1.143.0 (stable, commit 2d0b7506a36c1d6db9a466440131a8e01eab2289) - Remote – WSL (Ubuntu 24.04), Windows host - Agent host: /copilot-sdk-linux-x64 1.0.23-preview.5, runtime reports Copilot 1.0.100-1 - No custom chat.agentSkillsLocations value (defaults)

title: Extension-contributed MCP servers are never activated in Agent Host (Copilot CLI) chat sessions
text: Extension-contributed MCP servers are never activated in Agent Host (Copilot CLI) chat sessions. Type: Bug Extension-contributed MCP servers are never activated in Agent Host (Copilot CLI) chat sessions, because the lazy collection that loads them is only triggered by the *local* chat autostart path. ## Environment - Version: 1.143.1 (user setup) - Commit: - Date: 2026-10-22T17:23:22Z - Electron: 43.7.7 - ElectronBuildId: 15743441 - Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 - Node.js: 24.21.0 - V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0 - /copilot: 1.0.100-1 - /copilot-sdk: 1.0.23-preview.5 - OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.28000 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install an extension that contributes an MCP server through and registers it in via — e.g. (id ). 2. Reload the window. Do **not** send a chat message in the native/local Copilot Chat (sidebar). 3. Start a chat in Agent Host mode (the Copilot / CLI-backed agent) and ask for something that requires the extension's MCP tools. ## Actual The extension is never activated in that window, so its MCP server is never contributed and is invisible to the Agent Host session: This line only appears in *after* a native/local chat request has been sent in the same window. Before that, the extension id does not appear in the extension host log at all, and the server is absent from the MCP server inventory. The Extensions view additionally shows the extension as "Not yet activated" with an empty **Activation Events** list, even though an implicit activation event does exist for it. ## Expected An extension that contributes an MCP server should be activated as soon as a chat/agent session may need it, regardless of whether that session is a native/local chat or an Agent Host (Copilot CLI) session. The server should be visible in and in the Agent Host session's tool list without requiring a local chat first. ## Root cause The activation event itself is fine — already has an implicit generator, so the extension is *not* required to declare itself: - — - — yields for each contribution. The problem is *when* that event is fired. Extension-provided collections are registered lazily, and the lazy load is what performs the activation: - — the collection is registered with . - — calls . is only ever invoked from collection discovery, which filters on *not yet cached*: - — picks and calls . - — / is the only caller of . And there are only three ways to reach it: 1. — is called from the request path, guarded by the comment *"MCP autostart: only run for native VS Code sessions (sidebar, new editors) but not for extension contributed sessions that have inputType set."* This is the local-chat-only path, and it is what makes the extension appear to "suddenly" activate after a local chat. 2. — the command. 3. — the refresh action on the chat input MCP state indicator. The Agent Host path never calls any of these. It reads the already-collected server list directly: - — calls . Because is only populated for collections that have been loaded, and extension collections are lazy, an extension-provided server is simply absent from the list that gets forwarded to the Agent Host. Note the asymmetry: extension-provided MCP servers are the *only* MCP source that is lazy. Servers from , the gallery, and plugins are registered eagerly and are therefore present in Agent Host sessions. This is why the issue looks like "extension MCP servers don't work in Copilot CLI mode" while every other MCP source works. ### Secondary observation: the Extensions view cannot show implicit activation events The Extensions view renders only the manifest-declared list, so the generated event is invisible: - The feature renderer uses and renders . An extension that relies on an implicit activation event therefore shows an empty **Activation Events** section, which makes it look like the extension has no way to be activated at all. ## Proposal ### 1. Activate MCP provider extensions when Copilot Chat is enabled The most direct fix is to make collection discovery part of enabling the chat/agent surface, rather than a side effect of sending a native chat message. Concretely, should be invoked when the Copilot Chat integration becomes available/active, so that extension-provided MCP servers are discovered and their providers activated up front. The Agent Host delivery path in should not depend on the collection having been loaded as a side effect of an unrelated code path — it should ensure discovery has happened before reading . ### 2. Generalize to every extension that contributes agent functionality to Copilot Chat The same lazy-vs-eager inconsistency applies to all extension points that contribute agent functionality to Copilot Chat, and it is worth fixing them as one class of problem rather than one extension point at a time: - MCP servers — (has an implicit activation event, but is activated too late) - Chat participants / agents — (implicit ) - Chat sessions — (implicit ) - Chat context providers — (implicit ) - Language model chat providers — (implicit ) - Language model tools — (implicit ) - Chat plugins — (no implicit activation event) - Tool sets — (no implicit activation event) - Remote coding agents — (no implicit activation event) The general principle would be: **if an extension contributes something to Copilot Chat's agent surface, it should be activated when that surface is enabled** — not when a particular mode of it happens to be used, and not only after the user has already sent a message that happened to reach the relevant code path. Two concrete sub-items follow from this: a. **Activation should be driven by "the agent surface is enabled", not by "a native chat was sent".** Extensions contributing to the agent surface should be activated when Copilot Chat is enabled, so their contributions are present and discoverable in *all* session modes (native, Agent Host, Agents window) and in the / Customizations UI. b. **Extension points that contribute to the agent surface but have no implicit activation event should get one** (e.g. , , ), so that a declaration alone is enough to make the extension activate — consistent with how , , etc. already behave. c. **The Extensions view should surface implicitly generated activation events**, so an extension whose activation is driven by a generated event ( , , ...) does not appear to have no activation events at all. ## Workaround Running (or clicking the refresh action on the chat input MCP state indicator) calls , which discovers the extension collection and activates the provider. After that the server is available for the Agent Host session in the same window.

title: Reject tsgo builds when a completion callback throws synchronously
text: Reject tsgo builds when a completion callback throws synchronously. spawnTsgo accepts a completion callback that can return void or a promise. After a successful compiler exit, a synchronous exception from that callback currently escapes the child-process exit handler instead of rejecting the build promise. Callers cannot handle the failure through the returned promise or createTsgoStream error event. Invoke the completion callback inside the promise chain so synchronous exceptions and asynchronous rejections propagate consistently. Add regression coverage using successful compiler invocations, including callback failure and successful completion. This is an error-handling contract fix; no current source-map callback failure is required to reproduce it.

text: Agents Window resets This Computer to Cloud after reloading the new session composer. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable , , and in the Agents Window. 2. Reload the window while the local provider is still registering. **Expected:** The composer restores This Computer for the local workspace. **Actual:** The environment can become stuck on Cloud, including for a workspace Cloud cannot serve. ### Cause Automatic workspace restoration can run before the local provider registers. Add a deterministic Cloud-first/local-later registration regression test. Explicit environment changes and provider-targeted draft restoration should continue to work.

title: OAuth MCP server calls fail with 401 after adding a workspace folder replaces the extension host; Reload Window restores access
text:
OAuth MCP server calls fail with 401 after adding a workspace folder replaces the extension host; Reload Window restores access. Type: Bug Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. Reproduces with no user-installed extensions (fresh --extensions-dir). Built-in extensions remained active, including Copilot Chat, which is required to invoke MCP tools, so I couldn't test with everything off. - VS Code Version: 1.144.0-insider, commit 5170ebe909381b6990cd686dc47da9c854bc5946 (arm64) - Also reproduced on Stable 1.142.0, commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1 - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), arm64 - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.72.2026102104 (built in) Reproduced in a fresh instance ( and pointing at empty temp directories), with the server configured only in the workspace : { "servers": { "datadog": { "type": "http", "url": " } } } Datadog MCP is used here because it is publicly reachable (a Datadog account is needed to sign in). ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a window with a single folder ( ) containing the above. 2. Start the server and complete the OAuth sign-in. 3. In Copilot Chat (Agent mode), run a read-only call, e.g. "Only run the Datadog MCP search_datadog_monitors tool with status:alert. Reply if it succeeded or not." It succeeds. 4. File > Add Folder to Workspace and add a second folder ( ). The logs show the extension host is replaced. 5. Repeat the same prompt. ## Expected The call succeeds, or VS Code re-creates the authentication provider and refreshes or re-prompts for sign-in. This does not look like ordinary token expiry: the failing call happens about one minute after the successful one (14:01:00 to 14:02:04 in the logs), right after the extension host is replaced (14:01:50), and Reload Window restores access without my having to sign in again. The authentication state should survive an extension host replacement. ## Actual The call fails: "MCP server could not be started: 401 status sending message to {"errors":["Unauthorized"]}". Chat reports "It did not succeed (failed with a 401 Unauthorized error)." Developer: Reload Window fixes it. Video (redacted): ## Logs (local time, 2026-10-21) Extension host log: 14:01:50.097 [info] Extension host terminating: received terminate message from renderer 14:01:50.638 [info] Extension host with pid 73460 started Renderer log: 14:01:50.325 [info] ChatSessionStore: Workspace transition from 4a4b8c1f... to 1b181f93... 14:02:04.959 [error] [LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Error from tool mcp_datadog-mcp_search_datadog_monitors ... MCP server could not be started: 401 status sending message to ... MCP server log: 14:01:01.918 [info] Discovered 37 tools (before the folder add) 14:01:50.146 [warning] Extension host shut down, server will stop. 14:02:04.487 [info] Starting server datadog 14:02:04.490 [info] Starting server from LocalProcess extension host 14:02:04.885 [info] Discovered resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp 14:02:04.954 [info] Discovered authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/v1/mcp 14:02:04.955 [warning] Error getting token from server metadata: Canceled: Canceled 14:02:04.956 [info] Connection state: Error 401 status sending message to {"errors":["Unauthorized"]} After Reload Window (new host pid 74019 at 14:02:17): 14:02:36.346 [info] Starting server datadog 14:02:37.425 [info] Discovered 37 tools (no Canceled warning, no 401) ## Possible cause (from reading source, not confirmed at runtime) Read at commit 6d62b1d (Stable 1.142.0), not at the Insiders commit: - MainThreadAuthenticationProvider keeps the RPC proxy of the extension host that created it. - Disposing the host delegate in AuthenticationService does not unregister the providers that host registered. - getOrActivateProviderIdForServer() reuses the matching old provider. - Calls on a disposed RPC reject immediately with Canceled. - McpHTTPHandle._fetchWithAuthRetry() only takes its forceNewRegistration branch when an Authorization header already exists, so with no token it ends in a 401. I have not captured the provider's RPC state in a debugger. Related: #341484 (similar symptom, Agent Host path), #313493 (auth not reacquired after a network transition). title: Windows extension development watcher ignores source edits
text: Windows extension development watcher ignores source edits. When developing built-in extensions on Windows, the extension watch task completes its initial compilation but ignores subsequent source edits. It supplies an absolute Windows glob to the native watcher, whose file filter matches paths relative to the watched repository root. Reproduction: run a built-in extension watch task on Windows, wait for its initial compilation, edit a TypeScript source, and observe that the output is not rebuilt. The watcher should recompile edits, report compiler errors, and resume compiling after the errors are corrected. Use a repository-relative forward-slash glob and exercise the real watch/compiler pipeline in a regression test. This issue is scoped to source matching, not build lifecycle reporting or workspace launch tooling. Parent story:

title: Main process policy watchers permanently hold 2 of 4 libuv threads on macOS. Slow open() stalls file access in all windows
text: Main process policy watchers permanently hold 2 of 4 libuv threads on macOS. Slow open() stalls file access in all windows. <!-- Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes <!-- If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.142.0 - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 ## Summary On macOS the main process runs with the default libuv threadpool of 4 threads. 2 of them are held for the whole process lifetime by ( waiting on a semaphore). All work the main process does on behalf of every window shares the remaining 2 threads. When 2 calls are slow, the pool is exhausted and every window stalls: - no window can open or save files, or expand folders in the Explorer, until the slow opens return - closing any window shows "Discarding backups is taking a bit longer..." and the renderer logs - everything recovers at the same moment once the slow opens return That can be the case when file access is slow e.g. on a slow filesystem or also due to security scanners like Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. It also happens with , because opening a window still reads the of every installed extension through the main process. ## Steps to Reproduce: Either Open VS Code where e.g. the Extension files are on a slow filesystem Or 1. In Terminal.app (not the VS Code terminal, which sets ), start a separate instance with a threadpool of 2: 2. The window never finishes loading. stops after . 3. : both threads sit in ( ). 4. With the same command starts normally. ## Expected A slow for one window's request delays only that request. Other windows keep working, and closing a window does not wait on unrelated file I/O. ## Actual One slow per free thread blocks file access for all windows, because the shared pool has only 2 usable threads. ## Maybe Related - #321902 - #327479 - #337272 ## Possible fixes - Run the policy watchers on a dedicated thread instead of a libuv pool worker ( occupies a pool thread for its whole lifetime). - Set a larger for the main process. - Avoid re-reading every installed extension's through the main process on each window open. ## Workaround Start VS Code with ENV

title: Multi-diff file tree skips files while scrolling when a later active diff remains visible
text: Multi-diff file tree skips files while scrolling when a later active diff remains visible. ## Description The multi-diff editor's right-hand Changed Files tree can skip a file entirely while scrolling because another, previously active file remains partially visible. Reproduced in an existing VS Code Insiders window on Windows (build commit prefix ) using dbgjs wheel scrolling. No source changes or restart were needed. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open a multi-diff editor with the Changed Files tree visible and several consecutive files, for example , , , , and . 2. Activate , then scroll back to the beginning without activating another diff. 3. Use a viewport tall enough to show multiple diffs simultaneously. In the observed case, the viewport was approximately 1579 CSS px tall and the preceding diff was 838 px tall. 4. Scroll down through and into the subsequent files. **Expected:** The tree follows the file being read as scrolling advances through the diffs, including . **Actual:** Selection progresses , skipping . Across 65 downward wheel-scroll samples, was never selected. ## Runtime evidence and investigation At scrollTop 650, the visible file models were , but both the active model and selected tree entry were . Later, the visible models were . The test diff occupied the upper part of the viewport (entry bounds approximately y=-19..819), while began at y=819. The tree still selected . The installed workbench bundle and live model inspection confirm the cause: - , around line 210: prefers whenever it occurs anywhere in , falling back to the first visible item only otherwise. - , around line 38: the active item retains its previous value when focus does not select another item. Scrolling does not replace it. Visibility tracking correctly includes the skipped file; the active-item preference overrides scroll-follow selection. With a tall viewport, the later active file becomes visible before the preceding file reaches the top, so that preceding file never becomes selected. ## Suggested fix and regression coverage Distinguish explicit file navigation from subsequent scrolling: retain appropriate clicked/revealed-file selection near the end of the document, but do not let a stale active item elsewhere in the viewport indefinitely override scroll-follow selection. Add coverage with multiple simultaneously visible diffs and an active item below the topmost one. The existing interaction test in (around line 112) covers file clicks, but does not scroll through this scenario.

title: Uninstall All can remove a remote dependent but fail to uninstall its local dependency
text:
Uninstall All can remove a remote dependent but fail to uninstall its local dependency. can partially fail when an extension is installed locally and an extension that depends on it is installed on the remote. The remote dependent can be removed, while the local extension remains installed and the operation reports that the same dependent prevents its removal. This came up while investigating extension uninstall behavior in a WSL window. It is a separate backend issue from the incorrect installation state reported in #343155. ### Minimal case Consider two user extensions: installed locally with , and installed remotely. The remote extension declares and . The workbench's uninstall flow can include both extensions in one request after the user chooses in the dependents dialog. At the service boundary, the request is equivalent to: If the local dependency check reads the remote installed list before the remote dependent has been removed, it rejects the local uninstall. The remote removal nevertheless proceeds. The result is an error such as , with the dependency still installed locally and the dependent gone remotely. I would expect both extensions to be removed successfully when both are in the requested batch and no other dependents prevent removal. A dependent already included in that request should not by itself cause this partial failure. ### Relevant code The references below are pinned to commit . The workbench [adds dependent extensions to the uninstall request]( then [offers and submits the combined request]( [ ]( groups that request by server. It then [starts each server's uninstall concurrently and waits with ]( For the local batch, [ ]( fetches the remote installed extensions and rejects removal if any non-UI extension depends on the local extension. It only receives the local server's batch, so the check does not account for the remote dependent already being scheduled for removal in the same overall request. The remote batch can therefore complete while the local batch fails against the earlier installed list. The operation collects the error but does not undo the successful remote removal. The dependency check needs to consider the full request and the order of removal. It should still protect extensions whose dependents will remain installed, including when removing a dependent fails. ### Verification and related work This was reproduced by executing the current workbench method and the backend and methods in an isolated harness with synthetic local and remote services. Selecting the actual callback produced a batch containing both extensions. When the remote installed-list read returned a snapshot containing the dependent, the combined call rejected after removing that dependent, leaving the local dependency installed. Delaying the read until after the remote removal made both uninstalls succeed, confirming that the failure depends on timing. This has not yet been reproduced end to end with packaged test extensions in a live WSL session. The environment details below are from the window in which the original uninstall problems were observed. The combined-uninstall feature was requested in #119243 and implemented in #221504. This report concerns the cross-server failure within that feature, rather than adding the ability to uninstall dependents. The automated reproduction isolates the built-in implementation with controlled service failures. <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.143.0, affected build . The relevant implementation is unchanged on main at . - OS Version: Windows x64; reproduced with the Electron unit-test runner and fake timers. Steps to Reproduce: 1. In , instantiate with the existing mock fetcher. Make both and consistently reject with of kind /HTTP 403 or /HTTP 404. 2. Call , then with the default interval. 3. Advance the test clock by one hour plus one millisecond, leaving the polling reference alive and the account/resource unchanged. 4. Count both fetch operations and inspect whether the model has loaded a PR. ### Actual For either persistent failure: That is **122 failed fetch operations for one inaccessible PR in a simulated hour**, including the initial refresh. Polling remains scheduled at the normal one-minute interval, with no failure backoff or access-recovery gate. Multiple distinct inaccessible PRs multiply this background traffic. ### Expected Persistent missing-resource/access failures should trigger bounded retry/backoff or a recoverable suspended state, rather than indefinitely polling both endpoints at the successful-operation cadence. Recovery should still be possible after an account/access change, a resource change, or an explicit user refresh. Preserve ordinary successful polling, shared model ownership, and cancellation. ### Cause and Impact - [Each refresh requests PR metadata and reviews together]( - [Failures are caught and logged]( so the refresh promise completes without conveying a persistent failure state to the poll scheduler. - [The poll cycle schedules the next refresh unconditionally while retained]( using the 60-second default interval. - [The session polling contribution keeps unknown PRs eligible for polling]( an unavailable PR is not recognized as a merged, inactive PR. This generates repeated background failures and warning/error logs, wastes requests, and can make the PR and Reviews domain failure rates rise together. ### Validation and Scope - Both controlled 403 and 404 cases reproduced the exact 61/61 counts with the real model scheduling logic. - They were executed alongside the commit-enrichment reproduction using: Result: **4 characterization tests passed**. These confirm the undesirable behavior; they are not a fix. The temporary investigation tests are not on main. - Read-only live GitHub probes returned 200 for an accessible PR and its review list, and 404 for a nonexistent PR and its review list. The 403 polling case was simulated rather than changing a live account's permissions. - The traced polling loop also predates the typed-client migration; this is not evidence that domain telemetry introduced the failure behavior. - This report establishes repeat amplification, not the exact missing-resource or permission cause behind individual production failures.

Preserve successful metadata caching and cancellation/disposal behavior. ### Cause and Impact [SessionGitHubCommitResolver.get]( starts a request whenever is unset. On failure it disposes the request store and resets to , making the next presentation evaluation immediately eligible to request the same metadata again. [The artifact sections derivation]( calls the resolver again when the artifact collection changes. Successful lookups remain cached, whereas failures repeatedly consume network requests and log warnings. This can disproportionately inflate request-weighted failure rates and waste API quota/network activity without improving the displayed metadata. ### Validation and Scope - The controlled 403 and 404 characterization cases passed with the expected 21 attempts each. - They were executed alongside the paired PR/review polling reproduction using: Result: **4 characterization tests passed**. text: Chat Customizations: Browse can take ~17 seconds to load; investigate caching and progress. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (built-in Chat Customizations UI) - VS Code Version: Insiders; exact version not captured - OS Version: Not captured - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Chat Customizations > Browse - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A - Logs: Request-timing telemetry is not currently available Steps to Reproduce: 1. title: Agents window freezes while background shell output streams (AgentHostOutputChannel rebuilds full output per chunk)
text: Agents window freezes while background shell output streams (AgentHostOutputChannel rebuilds full output per chunk). <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (core Agent Host / Agents window code) <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: Insiders, Agents window (trace captured 2026-10-20; exact commit isn't recorded in the trace) - OS Version: macOS Steps to Reproduce (inferred from the trace): 1. In the Agents window, have the agent start a long-running background shell that writes a lot of output (dev server, watcher, verbose test run). 2. Leave it streaming. 3. The window gets progressively less responsive until the renderer main thread is saturated. Workaround: reload the window or reopen the chat. The resubscribe gets a snapshot of at most 100k characters, so it's fast until the buffer grows again. ## What the trace shows This is from a 13.75s DevTools performance trace of the Agents window renderer ( ). I have the trace (76 MB) and can share it on request. - **The renderer main thread is busy for 97% of the trace** (13.3s active out of 13.75s), so the window is effectively frozen. - ** accounts for 10.4s of self time (78%).** It runs about 20 times a second at about 40ms per call, at a steady cost for the whole trace. - Call path: . Each incoming envelope triggers it. - **Garbage collection takes 1.07s (8%).** The heap climbs to ~2.77 GB, then a ~90ms full GC drops it back to ~975 MB about every 1.4s. That is roughly 1.3 GB/s of discarded strings, or ~65 MB per call, so the client-side terminal buffer is probably tens of MB of text. - The recurring ~135ms long tasks are each one full GC (~90ms) plus one call (~45ms). | Cost center | CPU time | Share of active time | |---|---|---| | (self) | 10.4s | 78% | | Garbage collection | 1.07s | 8% | | Session switch ( ) | ~0.9s | ~7% | There is also a separate, smaller problem: two 400–500ms tasks from switching sessions. In those, takes ~190ms each time, plus label rendering. It isn't what causes the freeze, but it's worth a look on its own. ## Root cause 1. ** rebuilds the entire output on every change.** Each update re-joins all content parts and runs a regex over the result. That is O(n) work per chunk, so streaming costs O(n²) overall: 2. **The client's copy of the terminal state has no size limit.** The host keeps only its own copy under (100k characters): - Limit: - trims only the host copy: - sends subscribers only the new chunk in a action, so the trim never reaches them: - The client's appends every chunk with no limit: Only a fresh subscription gets a snapshot capped at 100k characters. A subscription that stays open grows without limit, and so does the full-buffer rebuild in . 3. **Updates are not batched.** Every change also refreshes the chat terminal output view ( ): The output channel is attached here: ## Why it has gotten worse The full-buffer rebuild in and the unlimited client-side state have both existed since #327067 (July 23). They didn't cause problems because output stopped streaming when the command or turn ended. Changes over the last three weeks made output from long-running shells stream to the client without limit, in full, for as long as the chat stays open: | Merged | PR | Effect | |---|---|---| | Jul 23 | #327067 Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel | Added and the full rebuild in . | | Oct 2 | #339220 Stream attached background shell output in Agent Host chats | Background shells keep streaming after the async tool call returns. | | Oct 7 | #340222 Fix truncated and unscrollable output in the Background Shells preview | The host appends every chunk. Previously, once output passed 8 KiB, it received only short (~128 character) tail snapshots, so much less reached the client. | | Oct 7 | #340234 Keep all Agent Host shell output scrollable in the inline chat terminal | The inline chat terminal keeps scrollback up to . | | Oct 16 | #341700 Stream detached background shell output in Agent Host chats | Detached shells stream too, and output stays attached after the turn ends "until the command exits or the chat closes". **Most likely trigger.** | ## Suggested fixes 1. **Make incremental.** Convert only the newly appended text instead of re-joining everything. For example, use the delta from , or track how much of the content has already been converted. Handle a at the end of one chunk followed by at the start of the next. Fall back to a full rebuild only on or a snapshot. 2. **Limit the client's copy to the host's limit.** Trimming in isn't enough on its own, because the subscription's state still holds the full content. Options: - Enforce in the terminal reducer. That needs a protocol change, since the reducer is generated by . - Add a trim action that the host sends whenever drops content. - Have the host send a fresh snapshot (clear plus data) whenever it trims. 3. **Batch change notifications.** Coalesce into the output view refresh, for example once per animation frame, so the view doesn't refresh about 20 times a second. 4. **Consider stopping retained subscriptions for tool cards that aren't visible.** A retained detached-shell channel that nobody is viewing could stay unsubscribed and reload a snapshot when its card renders. Fixes 1 and 2 together should remove nearly all of the 10.4s, and fix 2 also removes most of the GC pressure.

title: Remote agent host: customization expansion asks the remote host to resolve the client's local plugin paths (file:///Users/...)
text: Remote agent host: customization expansion asks the remote host to resolve the client's local plugin paths (file:///Users/...). **Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH, Copilot CLI provider. Client: macOS. Host: Linux. ### Symptom When a remote agent-host session's customizations are listed, the remote host gets requests for the **client's** local plugin folders, and they fail: On the client, the same requests appear as . Each run sends 4 folders × 2 client plugins, twice (16 requests). It repeats every time the customizations are refreshed. ### Cause Client-synced plugins ( ) keep their original client-side URI ( ). In ( ), only the synthetic synced bundle ( ) is left alone. Every other URI goes through , including client-synced plugins: then passes that URI to . It assumes the URI is a remote root and resolves , , and through the agent-host filesystem, which points at the remote machine. Those paths exist only on the client. ### Impact - The expansion fails quietly and returns , so the remote session's customization listing can't include those plugins' children. In this repro, has 7 agents and 12 skills on the client and has 4 skills, and none of them can be enumerated through the remote host. - Each refresh sends useless round trips to the remote host, and both host and client log them as errors. ### Suggested fix For client-synced customizations ( set), don't wrap with . Resolve them against the client's own filesystem, for example by keeping the original URI, or through whatever the synced-bundle path uses. The same applies to the other call sites for client-owned items ( , children, ).

title: Chat: in markdown table cells renders as literal text
text: Chat: in markdown table cells renders as literal text. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. The rendering happens in core chat ( ), so any chat response that contains such a table is affected. - VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider ( , 2026-10-20) - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (arm64) - Surface: Agents window (Copilot CLI agent). The same code path renders every chat response. - Model: Claude Opus 5.5 ### Summary When a chat response contains a markdown table with inside a cell, the is shown as literal text instead of a line break. A multi-line cell ends up as one paragraph full of tags. Models emit here on purpose. GFM table cells cannot contain newlines, so is the de facto way to break lines in a cell, and GitHub renders it that way. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a chat (I used the Agents window) and send: > Can you give me a table of content about the 5 highest GDP countries. In the last column, give a few bullet points describing some demographic info like population size etc 2. The model answers with a table whose last column uses between bullets (row reconstructed from the rendered output): **Expected:** each bullet starts on its own line within the cell, as on GitHub. **Actual:** the cell renders verbatim as: > • Population: about 342M, the 3rd largest in the world<br>• Median age: about 39<br>• About 83% of people live in cities<br>• Still growing slowly, mostly through immigration Every row in the table is affected. The issue reproduces deterministically without a model: ### Root cause 1. Chat renders agent markdown **without** (correctly, because the content is untrusted), and [ ]( sets . 2. marked lexes in a table cell as an inline token. In [ ]( when is off, returns , which produces . 3. is already in , so the sanitizer would accept it, but it is escaped before reaching the sanitizer. Outside tables, chat already sets , so a plain newline becomes and models have no reason to write the tag. Table cells are the one place where is the only way to get a line break. A second, latent issue affects any fix built on marked's hook. While a response is streaming ( ), calls and directly, and those skip extension hooks, whereas runs them. Such a fix would therefore show the literal during streaming and the correct rendering only after the response completes. ### Proposed fix - Add a table-scoped marked extension to the chat render options. Its hook turns inline tokens that are exactly , , or (case-insensitive, including inside , links, and other nested inline tokens) into marked's native token. - In , run on the path to match , so streaming and final rendering agree. Scope and safety: - No other HTML is enabled. - outside tables stays literal text. - inside code spans and fenced code blocks stays literal. - The output is a plain without attributes, which the sanitizer already allows for chat.

title: Customization Migration keeps deleted prompts in the list
text: Customization Migration keeps deleted prompts in the list. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured. - VS Code Version: Insiders, commit , built 2026-10-20. - OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured. - Feature: Agents window > Customizations > Migration. - Selected model: Not applicable. - Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. The bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session data. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Customizations > Migration with user prompt files eligible for migration. 2. Open a prompt's context menu, choose Delete, and confirm. 3. Check the migration list. The deleted prompt can remain listed and still offer Delete. Expected: Deleting a prompt removes its row and updates the migration counts. Actual: The file is removed from disk, but the list can retain the row, making deletion appear unsuccessful. Repeating Delete can show another confirmation for the same prompt. ### Observed evidence On October 20, local log timestamps show: - 08:42:01: Delete confirmation for one prompt, followed by migration recomputation and a user-data filesystem change. - 08:42:10: Delete confirmation for another prompt, followed by another filesystem change and multiple migration recomputations. - 08:42:15 and 08:42:22: Delete confirmations appear again for the second prompt. Both prompt files were absent on disk when checked after the capture. No matching filesystem-delete error appears in the renderer logs. ### RCA A cancellation race was reproduced using the current source methods with controlled discovery timing. The relevant source matches the reported Insiders commit. - [deleteCustomizationFile]( deletes the file and refreshes Migration. An immediate refresh can still read pre-delete discovery results before watcher invalidation. - [refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo]( cancels the previous refresh when another invalidation arrives. - [listPromptFiles]( shares an in-flight promise tied to its first caller's cancellation token. The replacement refresh can inherit that cancelled scan even though its own token remains live. - [computeCustomizationMigrationInfo]( ignores the resulting cancellation, leaving the previous rows without an error state or retry. The controlled reproduction verified that both computations exit without applying updated candidates, while the replacement request's token is not cancelled. The logs are consistent with this race but do not record discovery cancellation directly, so attribution of this specific occurrence remains likely rather than conclusive. No live UI reproduction or fix validation was performed. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

Server: Copilot session: reports “requires authentication”; clicking Authenticate does not open a browser. Local session: the same Atlassian MCP configuration works reliably. Log evidence: VS Code successfully authenticated and discovered 32 tools, but the agent continued reporting “still requires authentication.” ### Steps to reproduce 1. The chat displays: > The MCP server com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server requires authentication. Authenticate? 4. Select **com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server** and restart it, using **Restart Server** or **Stop Server → Start Server**. 9. Complete any authentication prompted through the MCP server controls rather than the chat card. 10. Start a **new Copilot chat** and retry Atlassian. 11. The authentication problem persists. The above restart/authentication/new-chat sequence was followed without resolving the issue. ### Expected result Clicking **Authenticate** should complete authentication—opening a browser if necessary—and make the Atlassian tools available to the Copilot session. ### Actual result and log evidence Clicking **Authenticate** does not open a browser, and the Copilot session continues to require authentication. In the same VS Code installation, leave the Atlassian MCP configuration unchanged. 13. Open **New Chat (+)**. 14. Change **Session Target** from **Copilot** to **Local**, leaving the agent mode as **Agent**. 15. Attempt to use Atlassian MCP. **Result:** Atlassian works reliably in the **Local** session. (In my case: Kernel-Power 41; EventLog 6008 reports that the previous shutdown at 22:10:11 was unexpected.) 3. Start VS Code again. **Note — this is not an extension bug:** the failure happens during storage initialization ( ), *before* any extension is activated, and it wipes the of every extension that uses it at once. In my case the extension whose settings disappeared was , but the defect is in the core storage layer. *Deterministic variant, in case a power cut is impractical (this mirrors the verification steps that were used for #93428):* replace with a copy of a healthy DB in which one page is damaged such that the file still *opens* but fails. --- ## Summary After an unexpected power loss, contained a torn page. VS Code then: 1. **opened the DB successfully** — a torn page does **not** prevent SQLite from opening the file; it only fails when a read or write lands on the damaged page. That is precisely why — which never issues a — does not throw, and why the catch branch that would restore is unreachable. The fallback was never attempted; 2. failed **every** subsequent read and write with ; 3. reported — a "healthy" but empty storage — and then **silently rebuilt** the DB at shutdown from its in-memory cache, which never contained the old values because the initial read had already failed; 4. and on the **next clean shutdown** VS Code itself ran again and **overwrote ** with that empty shell — removing the one file that, by construction, predated the power loss and could have restored everything. Net result: all extension (API keys, provider configuration, custom modes) was **permanently and silently destroyed**, and — the file that exists precisely as the fallback for this situation — turned out to be **unusable**: it ended up with the *same byte size and the same mtime* as the freshly recreated, empty DB. **No warning was shown to the user.** The data loss was discovered hours later, when the extension came up unconfigured. The original corrupt file can no longer be attached, because **VS Code itself replaced it** during the sequence above. ## Actual behavior — log evidence The **complete, unfiltered** from — session started 2026-10-19 22:50:40, i.e. immediately after the unexpected shutdown: What this log shows, in order: - — fails and gives up, **but VS Code keeps running**. - — the smoking gun: . Storage is reported as successfully initialized and *empty*, and the user is told nothing. - → → → — writes keep being attempted and keep failing, with shrinking key sets: (1709 bytes) → (292) → (184) → (242). The extension is actively trying to persist its state and every attempt is rejected. - **No line anywhere mentions ** — the backup path is never taken. State of the files *after* that session ended: | File | Size | mtime | |---|---|---| | | 204800 bytes (50 × 4096-byte pages, header self-consistent) | 2026-10-19 23:05:03 | | | 204800 bytes | **2026-10-19 23:05:03** | The recreated DB holds only default values for , and **zero** entries — every encrypted secret that extension had stored is gone as well. ## Why this happens (code analysis) Verified against and ; identical in the shipped 1.140.0, in 1.142.0 (current stable) and in . | Location | Behavior | Consequence | |---|---|---| | | runs only and — it **never issues a ** | a torn page does **not** make throw, so the recovery branch inside 's is **unreachable** for this class of corruption | | | only sets and logs | no recovery is attempted at the point of failure | | | | because errors *were* seen, **no backup is written**; execution falls through to the recovery branch | | recovery branch ( ) | → fresh → insert | is 's — the **in-memory cache of the current session**. Because the initial failed, that cache never held the extension's state, so the rebuild writes only defaults | | | | VS Code keeps running on storage it knows is broken, and never tells the user | | | defined, but has **no caller anywhere in the product** | no integrity check at startup | | | plain copy of → , without / | once the rebuilt DB is healthy, the next clean shutdown copies it over , so **VS Code itself overwrites the only surviving pre-corruption copy with the empty rebuild** | This is the trade-off that was accepted in #93428 ("VS Code does not warn about or try to recover a corrupt state.vscdb", closed 2020-03-26 as completed). But: - #93428 concerned **workspace** storage, and its verification steps explicitly accept the outcome *"you should see all workspace state wiped out but things are still functional"*; - the **"warn about"** half of that issue's title, and the usefulness of , were never delivered for this path. title: Remote agent host: reconnect with a new clientId ends in-flight turns (notDispatched) while they keep running on the host
text: Remote agent host: reconnect with a new clientId ends in-flight turns (notDispatched) while they keep running on the host. **Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH (1.142.0-insider, 363a43fb), Copilot CLI provider ### Symptom The client loses its SSH connection to a remote agent host (here the Mac went to sleep). When the connection comes back with a new client ID, every in-flight request on that host ends in the UI, but the turns keep running on the remote host. They only re-attach when the user later reopens each session ( ). ### Timeline (client times EDT; macOS asleep with periodic DarkWakes) - - Reconnect attempts only run during DarkWakes. Each one fails with - → - A fresh connection initializes in 56 ms with a new client ID. - - All three in-flight requests end: (two , one ). - At the same time, the remote host log shows those sessions still running ( , for the same sessions). - Each session also logs dozens of . ### Cause On , ( ) calls and then . Disposing the old connection's handlers makes the pending in return with no completed turn. The outcome is recorded as and the chat request ends, even though the turn is still active on the host. Terminals are reconnected through , but active turns aren't re-attached until the session is reopened. ### Expected When the client ID changes, re-attach in-flight requests to the host's still-active turns, the way the session-open path already does ( ). At minimum, keep the request pending and show a reconnecting state instead of ending it. ### Note The in-place protocol reconnect (same client ID) failed 10 times with relay closes mid-reconnect, but the fresh connection right after succeeded in 56 ms. It may be worth checking why the in-place path couldn't finish when a fresh connect could. That fallback is what forces the client-ID change.

title: Agent host: session shows "Failed" while a turn is running (a failed subagent chat outranks InProgress)
text: Agent host: session shows "Failed" while a turn is running (a failed subagent chat outranks InProgress). **Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH, Copilot CLI provider ### Symptom A session is actively running a turn (tools executing, responses streaming), but the sessions list shows it as **Failed**. It stays Failed for the whole turn. ### Steps (as observed) 1. In a Copilot CLI agent-host session, run a turn that spawns subagents (this session has 40+ subagent chats). 2. One subagent fails. Here it was a brief network outage on the host: . Its subagent chat receives , so that chat's status becomes . 3. Later, send a new message in the session's default chat. The default chat is now . 4. The sessions list shows **Failed** for the session while the new turn runs. ### Root cause ( ) aggregates chat statuses with precedence , across **all** chats: A subagent chat never gets another turn, so once one ends with it keeps permanently. From then on the aggregated session status is , even while the default chat is . replaces the activity instead of being OR'ed with it. So in (which would prefer ) never sees and renders **Failed**. ### Suggested fix - Don't let a stale outrank live work: rank above when aggregating. - And/or ignore from finished subagent (read-only) chats. A failed subagent whose parent turn kept going, or later ended normally, isn't a session failure. ### Secondary (minor): catalog reconciliation treats a transient disconnect as a hard failure The catch-all in returns for , which happens while the Copilot SDK client is down or reconnecting: This is transient. It probably belongs under (for example, parked as until the client is back), not . Separately, the same busy session then logged 33 times in about an hour, because its dirty marker kept changing during the active turn. These outcomes only go to the log, so users don't see them. But they read like the cause of the Failed badge and sent the investigation the wrong way.

title: Auto "Move to Copilot" archives local chat but discards the new agent host session as empty ("Provider copilotcli is not ready", "Adoption declined: marker=missing")
text: Auto "Move to Copilot" archives local chat but discards the new agent host session as empty ("Provider copilotcli is not ready", "Adoption declined: marker=missing"). ### Description ## Summary On a machine with org-managed Copilot settings, opening an existing local (panel) chat triggers the automatic Move to Copilot. The new Copilot agent host session is created but never opened: the client subscribes with a URI, the provider refuses it, and about 30 seconds later the agent host disposes the session as empty. The original local chat is archived anyway. The user loses access to the chat (the session file is still on disk), and nothing replaces it. Unarchiving doesn't help. Opening the chat again re-runs the move, which archives it again and creates another empty session that is also discarded. ## Environment - VS Code 1.140.0 (stable), commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, built 2026-10-15 - Windows client, remote WSL (Ubuntu) workspace - Copilot agent host enabled, with the provider - Org-managed settings include a key ( ), which makes local panel chats read-only and turns on the automatic move ( ) - Affected chats are older local panel chats with long histories (the one I looked at is 131 MB in ) ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have a local panel chat with history from before the agent host change. 2. With the managed settings above in effect, open that chat from the Sessions view. 3. Wait about 30 seconds, then look at the Sessions list. 4. Unarchive the chat and open it again. ## Expected The history is moved into a Copilot agent host session that is saved and shown in the Sessions list. The local chat is archived only after the move has succeeded. If the move fails, the local chat stays as it was and an error is shown. ## Actual - The local chat is archived ( in ). - No new session appears in the Sessions list. - After unarchiving, opening the chat archives it again within seconds and creates another empty session. - No error is shown to the user. ## Log evidence Agent host log ( , remote), one attempt: 13:09:37.291 [Copilot] Chat created; its backing stays deferred until the first send: ahp-session:/479f41a8-… 13:09:38.040 [Copilot] Adoption declined for 479f41a8-…: marker=missing, provenance=unknown, cached=false 13:09:38.076 [ProtocolServer] Request 'subscribe' id=3165 failed Provider copilotcli is not ready to open copilotcli:/479f41a8-…; it may still be starting, so try again shortly 13:10:43.796 [AgentService] GC: disposing empty unsubscribed session ahp-session:/479f41a8-… The session is created as , but the client subscribes to . Nothing ever subscribes to the real session, so it is collected as empty and the moved history is never saved. The same happened four times in one day: , , and were all created and then removed with "GC: disposing empty unsubscribed session". Renderer log at the same time: [error] Error: [UriError]: If a URI contains an authority component, then the path component must either be empty or begin with a slash ("/") character at Object.fromAgentHost (...) [error] Error: TreeError [AgentSessionsView] Data tree node not found: vscode-chat-session://local/<base64 session id> ## Impact Several long-running chats can no longer be opened. The data is still on disk, but the only way back to it is to read the raw JSONL. Every attempt to open one makes it worse. There is no setting that lets a user turn the move off. ## Suggestions - Archive the local chat only after the target session has been saved (or written to disk before the "first send"). - Subscribe to the session with the URI scheme it was created with. - If the move fails, leave the local chat unarchived and show an error. Full and extracts can be provided on request. ### Issue Details Item|Value ---|--- Issue Category|Bug Target|Visual Studio Code VS Code Version|Code 1.142.0 (6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, 2026-10-15T03:02:17Z) OS Version|Windows_NT x64 10.0.26300 ### Additional Issue Data [issue-data.md]( <!-- generated by issue reporter -->

title: Agent host permanently wedged after Copilot CLI process exits (SDK disconnect throws, no recovery, 250 ms retry spin)
text: Agent host permanently wedged after Copilot CLI process exits (SDK disconnect throws, no recovery, 250 ms retry spin). ## Summary If the Copilot CLI child process exits while the agent host is running, the agent host stays broken until the whole process is killed by hand. The client is never restarted and active turns are never failed. Background loops then retry every 250 ms forever. This happened twice on a remote Linux agent host, on two different builds, a week apart. ## Environment - Insiders , also seen on - Remote agent host over SSH, Linux arm64, client is the Agents window - . The same code is still in on . ## Symptoms - Every Copilot session on the host stops working. A long-running session still shows its turn as in progress about 2.5 days after it started. - fills with about 73k warnings per 35 minutes. One 5 MB log file rotates out every ~17 minutes, and the crash context almost rotated away. ## Timeline (UTC) | Time | Event | |---|---| | 04:46:24.389 | Last line in the Copilot CLI log. The process exits with no stderr, no panic, and no core dump. | | 04:46:34.9 | That is exit + (10 s). The SDK's throws (stack below). | | afterwards | Every operation fails with , , or Recovery never runs. | | +20 h | Still wedged: 1,224 discovery failures, 9.6k , 2.6k catalog reconciliation failures | The second instance hit the identical stack on 2026-10-13 01:28:25Z and stayed wedged for a week (10,047 discovery failures). This only shows up in the CLI launcher's debug log ( ). It is not in . ## Root causes ### 1. SDK: a double throws inside cancels the same twice. It cancels in and again in . In vscode-jsonrpc, if was never read, the first sets , a frozen object with no method. The second then throws. The throw happens inside , which calls. Because of that, , , , , and never run. The client is left holding a disposed connection. This happens on every CLI disconnect, because VS Code always passes an . Suggested fix: guard the cancel with , or read eagerly. Also put the teardown in a . ### 2. The agent host only recovers from in only starts when returns . After a CLI exit, the errors are classified differently: - - - unclassified: - unclassified: So recovery never runs, not even for . Background work never goes through at all, including: - - subagent completion confirmation - - catalog reconciliation Suggested fix: treat every connection-loss kind as recoverable. Better, react to the client disconnecting or the child process exiting directly, rather than inferring it from failed operations. Then fail active turns and restart the client. ### 3. Retry loops spin with no backoff In , re-arms on any error every (250 ms), once per orphaned subagent, forever. has the same pattern. These loops cause the log flooding described above. ### 4. Nothing records why the CLI exited - The SDK swallows with , so "CLI server exited with code X" is never shown. - The agent host does not log the exit code, signal, or pid. - CLI stderr only reaches the launcher's debug log. In this case the evidence points to SIGKILL, probably the kernel OOM killer during heavy parallel builds: - there was no stderr and no core dump, and the log simply stops - the agent host's cgroup shows with This could not be confirmed. The agent host should log the exit code, signal, and the tail of stderr whenever the CLI exits. ## Workaround Kill the agent host process tree on the remote. The client relaunches a fresh one when it reconnects.

title: Agent Host: workspace-folder change triggers catalog reconciliation that destroys an active Copilot agent-host session and deletes its session-state (data loss)
text:
Agent Host: workspace-folder change triggers catalog reconciliation that destroys an active Copilot agent-host session and deletes its session-state (data loss). Type: Bug Environment VS Code 1.142.0 (6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1), Windows 11 (NT 10.0.26200) Copilot agent host (copilot-runtime.exe --headless … --remote), 3 windows open Multi-root workspace with about 11 folders (main repo, several git worktrees, sibling repos) About 5 agent-host sessions open at once. Sessions had been recovered or forked earlier (.workspace-fork.lock present). What happened At 15:27:37 a workspace-folder change was processed (Claude VSCode.log: Updated lock file … with new workspace folders). All sessions logged Syncing permission mode: source=config-change. At 15:27:39, AgentHostCatalogReconciliation logged will be retried: superseded for four ahp-session:/… entries, including the actively running ahp-session:/369c23c6-a81e-4941-b412-6c4636890886. The other three were not destroyed. At 15:27:43 the host logged [Copilot:64261a3b-…] SDK session shutdown received (destroy) … lifetimeMs=3912597. The session had been running for about 65 minutes and was waiting on an elicitation. It then logged Elicitation response: cancel and Discarding elicitation callback result after abort. ~\.copilot\session-state\64261a3b-… (including events.jsonl) no longer exists. %APPDATA%\Code\agentSessionData\64261a3b-…\session.db has 0 turns, so the conversation can't be restored. At 15:32 a client action against the stale UI entry logged [AgentService] async dispatchAction failed: Session was explicitly deleted: ahp-session:/369c23c6-…. The session disappeared from the Sessions view. Nothing in the logs says who requested the delete. The same workspace-folder change and reconciliation also occurred at 14:19:51. It destroyed nothing then, because the session didn't exist yet. Expected: Reconciliation never destroys or deletes the state of a running or active session. Changing workspace folders doesn't affect existing sessions. Actual: The active session is destroyed, its on-disk state is deleted, and the UI keeps showing it until a later action fails. Steps to reproduce (inferred, not yet isolated) Open a multi-root workspace containing several folders, including git worktrees. Start several Copilot agent-host sessions. Include ones previously recovered or forked, so the catalog has both ahp-session:/ and copilotcli:/ entries for the same work. Start a new session in the main folder and let it run a long task that ends in a question to the user (ask_user/elicitation). Add or remove a folder in the workspace (for example a worktree) while that session is running. Watch agenthost.log for AgentHostCatalogReconciliation … superseded. Check whether the SDK session is destroyed and ~\.copilot\session-state\ is removed. I have not confirmed that step 4 is the only trigger, or what differs between the session that was destroyed and the three that survived. The agenthost.log at 18:35 that day showed about 12 copilotcli:/… entries as sourceUnresolvable, meaning their state folders were already gone. text: Unified workspace picker: hard to select Chat submenu items with the mouse. ## Problem In the unified workspace picker, selecting an item from the **Chat** submenu with the mouse is difficult. title: Agents: PDF webview returns 401 for an allowed vscode-agent-host resource with matching _ah metadata
text: Agents: PDF webview returns 401 for an allowed vscode-agent-host resource with matching _ah metadata. # Agents: PDF webview returns 401 for an allowed vscode-agent-host resource with matching _ah metadata ## Summary A PDF opened from a remote agent-host filesystem in the Agents window fails with "Unexpected server response" and zero pages. The PDF extension correctly includes the document's parent directory in . VS Code's webview loader strips the query from the requested URI but not from the allowed root. Both originally carry the same agent-host routing metadata. The shared URI containment helper compares queries, so the modified request no longer matches its allowed parent. VS Code returns 401 before attempting the file read. This was diagnosed and temporarily worked around in the running application using dbgjs. Changing only this viewer's allowed-root query to empty changed the request from 401 to 200, after which the same PDF rendered successfully. ## Environment | Item | Observed value | | --- | --- | | Investigation date | 2026-10-18 | | VS Code | 1.143.0-insider | | Installed commit | | | Build date | 2026-10-15 | | Client OS | Windows build 26100, ARM64 | | Window | Agents | | Resource provider | Remote connection over WSS | | Extension | 1.2.2 | | PDF.js | 2.10.377, build | | Test document | A valid 13,264-byte PDF 1.4 document containing one page | | Current upstream checked | | The installed and checked upstream versions of are textually identical. This is source confirmation, not an end-to-end run of the newer build. The exact remote OS and first affected release were not established. No remote credentials, real connection authority, or document contents are required for this report. ## UI reproduction Preconditions: an existing remote agent-host connection in Agents and the PDF extension installed. 1. Put a valid PDF in a directory on the remote filesystem. 2. Open that remote PDF with the PDF custom editor. 3. Ensure its resource is represented as a URI with metadata, and that the extension derives its allowed parent directory by changing only the URI path. 4. Observe zero pages and the red "Unexpected server response" banner. 5. Expand "More Information": PDF.js reports an unexpected server response with status 401. These steps describe the observed setup. A clean-machine provisioning recipe and independent end-to-end reproduction on another machine have not been executed. ### Expected A PDF below an explicitly allowed directory, with matching host and backing-resource identity, is loaded and rendered. ### Actual The webview denies access before file reading, returning: The extension's scripts and styles load; only the document request fails. ## Sanitized URI pair The following preserves the relevant structure of the runtime values: The query above is the URI object's value, not a claim about serialized URL escaping. can display the equals sign percent-encoded. Here decodes to . It is routing metadata, not an authentication token. ## Root cause and source references All links in this section are pinned to the installed commit. 1. The extension retains the document query when deriving its parent directory. The installed extension's uses , and line 21 sets . 2. [Agent-host URI wrapping]( stores the original resource identity in . 3. [getResourceToLoad, line 120]( clears the request query. 4. [The containment call, line 128]( still passes the unchanged root. 5. [ExtUri.isEqualOrParent, line 173]( checks the scheme, authority, path, and query. [Line 191]( explicitly requires query equality. does not ignore queries. 6. [WebviewElement, line 966]( converts into status 401. This 401 is generated by VS Code's webview authorization layer. It is not evidence of a remote server authentication failure. ## Runtime evidence A non-pausing dbgjs logpoint inside inspected the actual request, roots, and . Using the live comparator produced: | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Request with query cleared against original root | | | Original request against original root | | | Query cleared from both request and root | | | Request against the extension's unrelated installation root | | A viewer-frame fetch independently reproduced 401 with the literal body . ### Controlled live workaround With the user's approval, a one-shot dbgjs logpoint replaced only the matching root in this viewer's array with . It did not add a directory, alter the root path/authority, clear the request metadata, or patch the global authorization function. The patch trigger was removed before reopening the document in PDF.js. Verified outcome: The fetch and viewer observations were collected in separate calls and combined here. This is a temporary workaround, not validation of a production patch. It lasts only for this viewer instance. All investigation logpoints were removed and debugger connections disconnected. ## Proposed regression test Add a focused test to the existing [resourceLoading.test.ts suite]( using its existing setup: This is a proposed test, not an executed repository test. It directly models the observed runtime inputs and expected preservation of routing metadata. ## Permanent fix requirements Ownership belongs primarily in VS Code's webview/agent-host resource authorization integration, rather than PDF parsing. The initial idea of stripping both queries indiscriminately is not a sufficiently justified production fix: - [Agent-host metadata]( can carry the original scheme, authority, query, a different backing content path, content-reference routing, and file identity. For those URIs, the displayed path alone does not necessarily identify what will be read. - [Existing containment tests, line 342]( explicitly expect a query-bearing root to remain rejected. A generic query-stripping change would alter that behavior. - [Existing query tests, line 363]( verify request-query preservation with queryless roots, but do not cover this positive agent-host request/root pair. Recommended direction: 1. Add the failing regression test first. 2. Define a narrow, scheme-aware containment rule for plain agent-host filesystem URIs carrying compatible backing-resource metadata. Preserve/validate that identity rather than globally discarding . 3. For content references or metadata that changes the effective backing path, check the actual resolved identity or retain explicit conservative rejection until a policy is defined. 4. Preserve the original request URI when calling the file service, including query and fragment. 5. Keep other schemes' existing behavior unless an intentional, separately reviewed change is needed. Do not globally change . Additional required tests: - Matching plain-file request/root succeeds and returns the original URI. - Different hosts, different backing identities, siblings, outside-root paths, and root-equals-resource remain rejected. - Existing traversal, UNC, Windows/POSIX, and literal-backslash tests remain green. - Missing/malformed metadata and content-reference/path-override cases have explicit expected results. - Queryless-root compatibility is defined and tested. - A test verifies the file service receives the unchanged request URI. - End-to-end: remote PDF fetch succeeds, page canvas renders, and the error banner clears after closing/reopening the viewer and after restarting VS Code, without debugger assistance. No production patch or complete test suite has been run. The regression's introducing commit has not been identified. Broader impact on other extensions is plausible but not reproduced. ## Debugging method dbgjs was decisive for connecting the visible symptom to the authorization failure: 1. Discover the Agents renderer and the PDF extension's iframe with , , and . 2. Inspect the iframe's inner viewer window with to read PDF.js's detailed error and document URL. 3. Use with to inspect the actual fetch response. 4. Search the exact loaded workbench bundle and use its source map to locate . 5. Install a non-pausing to inspect real URI/root inputs and compare alternative normalization choices. 6. Apply the approved viewer-only runtime workaround, remove its trigger, reload PDF.js, and verify successful fetch and canvas rendering. No application restart, rebuild, remote shell, or linkrpc call was needed for the diagnosis or workaround. The strongest causal evidence is the controlled change: the same viewer, request routing metadata, document, and remote connection went from 401/zero pages to 200/one rendered page after changing only the allowed-root query.

title: Steering the Copilot agent marks just-finished edits and background-agent work as cancelled
text: Steering the Copilot agent marks just-finished edits and background-agent work as cancelled. When you send a steering message while the Copilot agent is working, tool results from around that moment can show as cancelled and lose their output, even though the work ran. This makes it look as if steering killed the agent's background agents. The agents keep running; only the chat loses track of their results. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the Chat view (or the Agents window) and pick the Copilot agent (Agent Host). 2. Ask it to make several small file edits one at a time, or to start a background agent that edits files or runs commands. 3. While it is working, type a steering message and press Enter. ## Expected - The edit or command that finished just before your message shows as completed, with its diff or output. - A background agent's edits and commands keep completing in that agent's chat. - Your steering message starts a new request below. ## Actual - The edit or command that finished just before your message shows as cancelled (skipped), and its diff or output is missing. - A background agent's edit or command that finishes at that moment never completes in that agent's chat, and is later shown as cancelled. The same happens when you send a new message while a background agent is editing. ## Cause The runtime only shows the steering message after the current round of tools has finished, and it moves a foreground agent to the background instead of stopping it. VS Code records some results (file edits, shell output) asynchronously after the runtime reports a tool as done. When the steering message arrives, VS Code ends the running turn immediately. Ending a turn marks its unfinished tool calls as cancelled, and later updates to that turn are ignored. VS Code also dropped a background agent's pending result whenever the main chat's turn changed, even though the result belongs to the agent's own chat. VS Code does not call abort or cancel for any agent or task when you steer. ## Notes - Seen in the editor Chat view with the Copilot agent: sending a steering message right after starting a turn made running background agents look like they were killed. The same code path is used by the Agents window. - Confirmed with deterministic Agent Host tests on at , not with a live model run (test sign-in was unavailable). The runtime was checked by reading its source: steering with moves a foreground agent to the background and does not cancel background agents.
