text: Agent host (Copilot): converting a workspaceless chat with set_workspace misses the entire prompt cache. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host (Code OSS from source, plus the local fix for #340431) - VS Code Version: Code OSS dev build (1.143.0) - OS Version: macOS - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, workspaceless chat converted with , Copilot provider - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Claude Opus 5.5 (direct, not HydraFusion), medium effort, 1M context - Logs: and events from the Copilot SDK When a workspaceless chat attaches to a workspace with , the first model call after the conversion reads nothing from the prompt cache. The whole prompt (about 30k tokens) is written to the cache again, including the parts that are the same for every session. This is separate from #340431, which was about a chat that stayed workspaceless. With that fix, resuming an unchanged workspaceless chat reads about 96% from cache. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. In the Agents window, start a new chat with no folder. Send a short prompt and wait for the response. 2. Ask the agent to attach the chat to a local Git repository as a direct folder (no isolation), and confirm the prompts. 3. Compare the two events in , and the cache reads in the usage checkpoints around the conversion. ## Measured One session, same model throughout. events in this window reported no change of model or effort. | Call | Input | Cache read | |---|---|---| | Calls inside the converting turn (3, summed) | 92,280 | 91,058 (98.7%) | | First call after the conversion | 30,081 | **0 (0%)**, 30,077 written | | First call after a later SDK resume, workspace unchanged | 30,248 | 28,151 (93.1%) | First calls of new sessions in this run read about 17,073 tokens from cache in workspaceless sessions and 16,455 in a workspace session. That shared prefix was not reused by the conversion call either. ## What changes at conversion **System message** (37,547 → 37,089 characters; the first difference is at character 3,256): 1. The SDK environment lines change: current working directory, Git repository root, and an added Git repository line. 2. The skills list changes: some skills move from to and are reordered. In this run the scratch directory's Git root was the home directory, which is itself a Git repository on this machine, so skills under home were listed as project skills. This may not happen on other machines. 3. is removed. This is expected. 4. A block for the new repository is added. **Tools (inferred, not directly observed):** is loaded eagerly in workspaceless sessions and deferred otherwise (see in ). The conversion re-advertises server tools. A changed tool list would explain why even the shared prefix was missed. Tool definitions are not recorded in . ## Expected The agent has to learn that its workspace changed, so some cache loss may be unavoidable. But the stable part of the prompt (tools and most system instructions) should still be reused, rather than starting from zero. ## Notes - The host already sends a continuation message saying "The current session is now attached to <path>…", so the new workspace could be carried by a message instead of the system prompt. - Possible directions: keep tool definitions stable across conversion; move the working directory, Git details, repository-specific blocks and skill locations out of the early system prompt, or after the last cache breakpoint. The cwd and Git lines come from the Copilot SDK, so that part needs an SDK change. - Related: #339643 ( line breaks cross-session caching) and #340431. - Cost: one full cache write of about 30k tokens per conversion. Later turns cache normally. - Not measured: other models.

The outer rejects it because . - This validation throw occurs outside the provider-query error isolation, aborting the combined Browse query. Relevant code: - [Native request cap introduced by #342177]( - [MCP response serialization and queryPage]( - [Marketplace page validation and total aggregation]( - [Platform-provider wrapper]( ### Verification Reproduced with the actual implementation from local checkout , using live public registry responses and applying the 99-item request cap introduced by #342177 in the native-provider adapter. title: Chat Customizations: opening a skill from the plugin detail page opens its folder, and README relative links break (resolved against raw.githubusercontent.com)
text: Chat Customizations: opening a skill from the plugin detail page opens its folder, and README relative links break (resolved against raw.githubusercontent.com). Two related bugs found while testing the plugin detail page in Chat Customizations ( ). ## 1. Opening a skill from the plugin detail page opens its folder, not **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Open the Customizations/Agents management editor and navigate to an installed/marketplace plugin's detail page. 2. Under "Skills", click a skill entry to open it. **Expected:** The skill's opens in an editor (as it does elsewhere in the Skills list). **Actual:** VS Code instead tries to open the skill's containing folder, which it cannot render as a document, so nothing useful is shown. This goes through -> -> , which looks up the clicked (the file URI, see ) against the Skills section's entries via . If the Skills items model represents each skill by its folder URI rather than its file URI, the lookup can resolve to (or fall back to) the folder instead of the file. Worth checking and whatever normalizes skill list items for the mismatch. Separately (same underlying UX), the plugin page + "back to go back" navigation feels like it should be a tree view in the main editor pane (so a normal file-tree-like editor opens, instead of an embedded detail view you back out of). Noting this here for context, but the primary ask is the broken skill-opening behavior above. ## 2. README relative links are resolved against instead of the GitHub repo In , fetches a marketplace plugin's over HTTPS. For a URL it rewrites the fetch URL to the equivalent to download the raw content, but then sets: ends up being the raw.githubusercontent.com URL (used to fetch the content) instead of the original (the page URL). Any relative links inside the rendered README (e.g. , ) therefore resolve relative to , which doesn't serve navigable GitHub pages, so clicking them is broken/404s. **Fix:** should be set to (the original GitHub blob URL), not . --- Reported from internal testing/feedback on the Chat Customizations plugin detail page.

title: Background shell streams in Agent Host chats keep all output in lastSnapshot and can lose a detached shell's exit code
text: Background shell streams in Agent Host chats keep all output in lastSnapshot and can lose a detached shell's exit code. Follow-up to which streams a detached background shell's output from the Copilot SDK's into its tool call's terminal. Review of that PR found three things, none of which block it. The reload and restart gaps are already tracked in ** grows without bound for background shells** - appends every chunk to ([code]( and nothing trims it. The terminal content itself is kept to a rolling buffer by ([code]( 100 KB per [ ]( - Once a stream has switched to chunks, has two readers: returns early for a chunked stream ([code]( and compares it once when the tool call completes ([code]( For a shell that keeps running after its call completed, nothing reads it again. - Attached background shells have done this since because the Copilot SDK streams their chunks until exit. Detached shells are the long-lived ones (dev servers, watchers), and feeds their reads through the same path in ([code]( so a detached watcher that runs for hours keeps all of its output in the Agent Host process, untrimmed, until the chat is disposed. **The exit code reported before the log drained is lost if the read then fails** - When the task list, a notification, or a / result reports the exit while the log is still being read, remembers the shell as draining and returns without keeping the reported ([code]( - Normally the read's settles the terminal. If the read fails instead, finalizes with ([code]( so the terminal shows the shell as exited without a code even though one was reported. **A failed read gives up instead of reading again without a cursor** - stops on any error, logs a warning, and leaves the shell to the task list ([code]( - The docs in 1.0.23-preview.2 say a read fails when the output no longer reaches the cursor, for example because its log was removed, and to read again without a cursor. The terminal then stays at whatever had been read before the failure. Steps to see the first one, in a local Agent Host Copilot session with at its default, : 1. Ask Copilot: "Use your shell tool to run in async mode with detach set to true. Do not read its output or wait for it. Reply with exactly STARTED." 2. Attach a debugger to the Agent Host, or take heap snapshots before and after. The shell's **Background Shells** terminal holds under 100 KB, while the stream's holds the whole output, tens of MB. The other two are from reading the code; the mock in can force them. Possible fix: - [ ] Stop appending to in once the stream's is set, with a test that streams past the terminal buffer limit and checks stays bounded. - [ ] Keep the reported exit code with the draining entry and use it in , with a test: report , fail the read, expect . - [ ] On a read failure, read once more without a cursor before giving up. Reading without a cursor replays the log from the start, so reset the terminal before appending the replay.

title: Agent-session links ignore open-to-side requests in editor windows
text: Agent-session links ignore open-to-side requests in editor windows. ## Problem In a regular VS Code editor window, opening an link with an explicit open-to-side request ignores that placement and opens/reveals the session in the Chat view or its previous location instead. The link source can pass , but the editor-window agent-session link handler discards the opener options and always targets the Chat view. The separate Agents-window handler already supports side opening. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Keep a document or source chat visible in a regular editor window. 2. Follow an available session or peer-chat link with Alt+click. 3. Alternatively, with Quick Open link support from #342081, enter the link in Ctrl+P and accept it with Alt+Enter or the Open to the Side button. 4. Repeat with the destination session already open in the Chat view or an editor. ## Expected - Explicit side-opening requests open the requested session/chat in a chat editor beside the originating editor group, keeping the source visible. - An already-open session does not override the requested placement by merely being revealed at its previous location. - The exact peer chat and connection authority remain intact. - Relevant editor options, such as pinning and preserving focus, are forwarded. - Ordinary link activation and delegated request-origin navigation keep their existing behavior when no side-opening request is made. ## Actual The editor-window handler ignores side placement and targets the Chat view, or reveals the session at its existing location. ## Tracking - Navigation story: #342050. - General Alt+click behavior: #340724. - Implementation: #342109. - Quick Open link source: #342051 / #342081. The session-link handler fix is independent of Quick Open. ## Validation of the proposed fix PR #342109 adds session/peer-chat regression coverage for absent, false, and true side-opening options. The fix was tested in a live Code OSS instance with Quick Open via dbgjs: the session opened in a second editor group while the original document stayed visible.

title: Agents: relative update timestamps become recent after passive AHP session reads
text: Agents: relative update timestamps become recent after passive AHP session reads. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. - VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider (e9f10b90b50805aa31d65f3d35cf53c264d7235f) - OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Have an idle local Copilot SDK session in the Agents window. 2. Have an AHP client subscribe to the cold session's channel to inspect its state/history, without sending a message or continuing a turn. 3. Observe its relative update label and, when sorting by update time, its position in the session list. **Actual:** Old, untouched sessions become recently updated, e.g. "1 min ago". Background restore/resume, runtime warnings, and shutdown can advance the timestamp despite no conversation activity. **Expected:** The relative update label should reflect meaningful conversation activity, not passive inspection or provider lifecycle bookkeeping. ### Local evidence On October 16, a session whose last user message and assistant turn were on August 8 received background AHP subscriptions at 10:10 and 10:11 PDT. Agent Host restored it, the SDK appended and remote-availability warnings, and later idle eviction appended . No new user message or assistant turn was recorded. There were 23 distinct SDK sessions resumed during 10:11, matching the observation that several untouched sessions became recent together. ### Suspected mechanism - restores cold sessions; Copilot history loading resolves/resumes an SDK session. - SDK session listing derives from the filesystem modification time, which also advances for lifecycle/warning records. - VS Code forwards that value into the session adapter's and . This makes passive reads appear as user activity. The originating client feature for the observed batch has not yet been identified; attribution to a particular third-party client is not established. Related but distinct: #306025 concerns creation-time versus update-time display, not lifecycle writes manufacturing fresh update times. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

text: Sessions: PR refresh fails for PRs with auto-merge enabled, leaving stale "open" PR icons. Regression from #341842 (3a1a3fe60f2), first shipped in Insiders build (1.143.0-insider). text: Agents window change count uses a stale local base branch when origin/<base> is unreadable. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (the bug is in core agent host code, ) <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider (16d22415b62f4bd6b056011027f53c3e9978fbf4) - OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64) When exists but points to an object that is not in the repository, the Agents window's changes pill counts the session's changes against the **local** branch. If the local branch is behind, every upstream commit it lacks is shown as a session change. In my case, a session with 9 changed files (+253 −25, all uncommitted) showed **228 Files +11627 −2593**. Local was 13 commits behind the commit the session branch was created from, and those 13 commits (219 files, +11374 −2568) were counted as session changes. Steps to Reproduce: 1. In a repository where local is behind , start an Agent Host session whose worktree branch is created from . 2. Point at an object that doesn't exist, by writing the loose ref directly (this simulates the corruption described below; refuses missing objects): 3. Make any change in the session. **Expected:** The changes pill shows only the session's changes. When is unusable, the documented fallback is (uncommitted changes only), and the session's creation point (the reflog's entry) would be even better. **Actual:** The pill counts against the stale local , including every upstream commit it is missing. The only signal is a warning in , repeated on every refresh (260 times in about 50 minutes for me, from more than one session in the repository): ### Root cause [ ]( calls [ ]( That treats any failure as "no remote-tracking ref", so the caller falls back to the bare branch name ( ), which resolves to the local branch: exits 128 both when the ref is missing and when it is unreadable ( ). With a broken ref, still succeeds against the stale local branch, so the fallback is never reached. This contradicts the method's own doc comment, which says it prefers "so branch changes match a PR-style comparison even if the local base branch is stale". ### Suggested fix Distinguish a missing remote-tracking ref from an unreadable one. still returns the ref's target when the object is missing, while fails. If the ref exists but its object can't be read: - don't fall back to the local branch; - use (the documented "no usable base" fallback), or preferably the branch's creation point from the reflog; - log once per repository, saying that the base couldn't be resolved, instead of a raw warning on every refresh. ### How the ref broke (context) This part may not be a VS Code bug, but it explains how a user ends up here. About 30 worktrees share one in this repository. In 's reflog, a at 10:45:22 moved it to . The was rewritten at 10:45:24 and still lists , which no longer exists. is in no remaining pack and isn't stored loose, so the pack that fetch wrote appears to have been deleted afterwards. Another object ( ) existed in a remaining pack but couldn't be read until I re-added it loose, which suggests the multi-pack-index mapped it to the deleted pack. The Git extension's autofetch ran several times a minute across these worktrees (git 2.54.0, no , or config), so a concurrent fetch and auto-repack race is the likely trigger. I haven't confirmed it. Whatever the cause, a corrupt remote-tracking ref shouldn't silently turn into a change count 25 times too large.

The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: source at ; related runtime mismatch reported on VS Code 1.141.2 in #341730. - OS Version: not reproduced locally; source-level matching logic is platform-independent, while command resolution requires platform coverage. ## Problem The VS Code MCP matcher and the Copilot runtime can make different decisions for the same allowlist and resolved server configuration. Track this separately from registry-name validation in #341730 and missing package commands during gallery admission in #338879. In , accepts any matching entry and compares names literally and commands as exact arrays. The runtime's contract gives transport-specific entries precedence: a stdio server can match by name only when that allowlist has no command entries; a remote server can match by name only when that allowlist has no URL entries. Additional matching differences to resolve under the same contract: - The runtime expands / in command and URL policy values. VS Code's matcher compares policy command values literally. - The runtime schema specifies case-insensitive URL scheme/host matching and case-sensitive paths. VS Code's URL matcher currently lowercases full exact URLs and uses a case-insensitive regex for wildcard matches. ## Steps to reproduce These are source-derived test cases to execute, not a claim of a new end-to-end reproduction. 1. Configure with and . 2. Evaluate a stdio server named whose invocation is . 3. VS Code's current matcher accepts the name entry. Under the runtime contract, the command entry's presence means the name entry does not admit this server. 4. Repeat with a remote server named and a nonmatching URL when the list contains a URL entry. 5. Add cases for an environment-expanded policy command and for URLs whose paths differ only in case. ## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria - [ ] Agree and document one matching contract with the runtime owner. Resolve differences explicitly rather than relaxing policy to hide them. - [ ] Name fallback and command/URL precedence produce consistent decisions for each applicable allowlist. Preserve restrictive composition when multiple managed layers apply. - [ ] Define and test policy-value environment expansion consistently, including missing variables, defaults, and the environment of the host that executes the server. - [ ] Match URL scheme, authority, and path according to the agreed contract, including wildcard patterns and path case. - [ ] Exercise allow and deny paths, unset versus empty allowlists, nonmatching commands/URLs, exact argument ordering, and final enforcement after configuration resolution. - [ ] Keep unresolved-input handling explicit. A preliminary gallery check must not authorize a different command or endpoint at execution time. - [ ] Validate editor-owned servers and the supported Agent Host paths; cross-check the remaining scope of #328241. - [ ] Record tests and the VS Code/runtime versions used. Update directly related configuration descriptions or administrator documentation where behavior changes. ## Scope boundaries Do not normalize registry names by replacing separators. Do not add a second runtime permission interpreter in VS Code. Reuse the authoritative contract and available integration APIs where possible. Runtime charset acceptance and VS Code consumption of its fix remain tracked by #341730. Gallery package-command admission remains tracked by #338879. This issue covers matching semantics, not a new registry identity design. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

text: MCP managed allowlist: runtime validation rejects registry-style serverName values. ## Environment - VS Code 1.141.2 (commit ), Windows x64 - Bundled 1.0.73 ( ) - Copilot Business, enterprise **server-managed** settings - Default GitHub MCP registry ( ), ## Summary VS Code identifies MCP servers coming from a registry by their **raw registry name** (for example , ), both in the gallery and after install. The managed-settings validator only accepts allowlist values matching . VS Code applies **no normalization**, so a allowlist entry can never match a registry-sourced server whose name contains or , which covers practically every server in the official registry. Related: #338879. That issue covers the gallery ignoring . This one covers the path. ## Evidence (code at ) **1. Gallery identity uses the raw registry name.** maps into . The there is only used to derive / . → returns for gallery servers. **2. Installed servers keep that raw name as their label.** installs with . At runtime, checks . Observed installed labels: , , . **3. Matching is strict equality, with no normalization.** : **4. VS Code's own setting schema accepts any non-empty string.** , → . **5. The managed-settings validator rejects it.** The bundled Copilot runtime ( 1.0.73, ) contains the validation error *"Allowlist serverName must only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores"*. The bundled managed-settings schema declares, for the allowlist matcher only: The denylist matcher accepts any non-empty string. ## Repro 1. Try to allowlist the Playwright registry server by name in enterprise managed settings: . This is rejected by validation (charset). 2. Use the closest valid value instead: or . 3. Open the MCP gallery and search for Playwright → *"This Model Context Protocol server is not in the list of servers allowed by your organization."* ( ). ## Expected At least one of: - a documented, deterministic **normalization** of registry names applied consistently on both sides (validator and VS Code matcher), for example and → ; or - a dedicated, non-spoofable matcher for registry-sourced servers, for example (optionally scoped by registry URL), evaluated against the gallery identity and the provenance of installed servers; or - at minimum, VS Code's setting schema and docs aligned with the validator, stating that registry servers with namespaced names cannot be allowlisted by . ## Actual No supported way exists to allowlist a registry server by name. Combined with #338879, packages-only registry servers have **no** working matcher at gallery time. ## Related: semantics differ between VS Code and the Copilot runtime The bundled schema also states, for : *"for stdio servers the match must be a serverCommand entry (serverName counts only when no serverCommand entries exist)"*, and the same for remote servers and . VS Code's does not implement this precedence. So simply relaxing the charset would **not** be enough: the runtime would still ignore it whenever / entries exist. This points to a registry-identity matcher (or fixing #338879) as the robust fix, plus aligning with the runtime precedence.

The affected configuration logic is platform-independent. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Supply an additional plugin marketplace through enterprise managed settings using . Leave the managed key unset. 2. Set in VS Code user settings. A nonempty allowlist that omits the managed marketplace has the same effect on that marketplace. 3. Open the plugin marketplace picker or query available plugins. ### Actual behavior The user value activates strict marketplace enforcement and filters out the enterprise-added marketplace. The picker labels it "Disabled by Organization", even though the restriction came from user settings. This is not a user value overriding the same managed key. The user-controlled strict setting restricts marketplaces supplied through a different managed key. ### Root cause The enterprise control was implemented as an exposed, policy-backed application setting. and application scope do not make a setting policy-only. - [Setting registration]( exposes and maps managed to it. - [Strict enforcement]( uses without distinguishing user configuration from managed configuration. - [Marketplace filtering]( applies that result to all configured marketplaces, including managed additions. - [Picker labeling]( treats the same resolved value as an organization restriction. The setting originated in #318623. #322025 changed it from a boolean to a structured allowlist. ### Required change Remove as a user-facing setting. Strict marketplace restrictions must come only from enterprise-managed . No backward compatibility for the VS Code user setting. Do not migrate existing user values, retain an alias, or keep a hidden fallback that still honors them. Hiding the Settings editor entry alone is not sufficient. Preserve enterprise-managed enforcement across supported managed-settings delivery channels. A managed empty array must still block all marketplaces, and a managed nonempty allowlist must still restrict both user-added and enterprise-added marketplaces. Do not fix this by exempting managed marketplace additions from an actual managed strict allowlist. Update all consumers and related UI, including settings links, to use the managed restriction rather than infer organization policy from an effective user configuration value. ### Acceptance criteria - The setting is absent from the user-facing configuration schema and Settings UI. - A stale user value has no effect, including . - With no managed strict allowlist, a stale user value cannot filter out marketplaces supplied through managed . - Managed strict allowlists retain their existing semantics, including empty-array lockdown. - "Disabled by Organization" reflects an actual managed restriction. - Regression tests cover stale user values, managed marketplace additions, managed allowlists, and managed lockdown. title: Do not enforce minimum client version when sandbox is not enabled
text: Do not enforce minimum client version when sandbox is not enabled. ## Problem Sandbox-related minimum client version requirements should not apply when sandbox is not enabled in managed settings. The presence of a sandbox configuration object alone should not require a newer client. cc Example : ## Requested behavior Enforce the sandbox-related minimum client version only when the effective managed sandbox policy explicitly sets to boolean . - When is set, do not enforce the sandbox minimum version. - When explicit effective is absent—including an omitted field, empty sandbox object, or absent sandbox key—do not enforce the sandbox minimum version. - When sandbox is explicitly enabled, preserve existing minimum-version enforcement. - Preserve minimum-version requirements independently imposed by other policies. Use the effective enabled state after applicable policy composition and overrides, rather than the presence of the sandbox object or other sandbox subkeys. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Disabled sandbox does not trigger a sandbox-derived minimum-version rejection. - [ ] Missing , an empty sandbox object, and an absent sandbox key do not trigger a sandbox-derived minimum-version rejection. - [ ] Explicitly enabled sandbox continues to enforce its minimum version. - [ ] Policy composition and overrides use the final effective sandbox enabled state. - [ ] Unrelated applicable minimum-version requirements remain enforced. - [ ] Policy refresh from enabled to disabled removes any stale sandbox-only version requirement. ## Related work - ACP tracking issue: - Runtime counterpart: - GitHub App implementation issue: - [Slack discussion]( ✏️ with :heart: :zap: by Copilot for

text: Agents Window: Branch Changes dropdown has uneven top/bottom margin in modern editor header. ## Describe the bug In the Agents Window's "modern" editor header (desktop tabs layout), the **Branch Changes dropdown** (e.g. ) appears to have an uneven top/bottom margin inside its pill: the content sits visually closer to one edge than the other, instead of being perfectly vertically centered like the surrounding tabs. Related complaints from the same screenshot/thread (filed here for traceability, not necessarily the same root cause): - The left-most tab can get clipped/cut off. - Tab titles can be hidden/truncated by the close ("x") button before the title has a chance to ellipsize. - It's unclear why the changes-count/diff-stat badge ( ) is fused into the same clickable pill as the branch/changeset picker, rather than being a separate, non-interactive element. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Agents Window with the desktop tabs/editor-header layout enabled. 2. Open a session with pending changes so the "Branch Changes" dropdown shows a file-count + added/removed stats summary (i.e. ). 3. Compare the vertical space above vs. below the pill's content versus its container. ## Code pointers - (the dropdown's action view item) — - Desktop header host: ( , , , / ) - Desktop header CSS: - Pill styling: ( , ) - Animated stats badge: / While the explicit padding values declared along this chain are symmetric (e.g. and ), the button is vertically centered through ~5 nested levels ( → → → → ) that rely on , but none of their ancestors up to actually has a definite (non- ) height — only a . Per spec, a percentage height needs a definite containing-block height to resolve; here it does not, so each level's height instead hugs content and gets independently (re-)centered via /CSS grid, which is a common source of compounding 1px sub-pixel rounding drift. There is also an inherited/uncontrolled on the picker's text spans, which combined with flexbox centering is a classic cause of 1px visual top/bottom offset ("half-leading" rounding). Separately (not necessarily the cause of this specific bug, but a related cascade issue found while investigating), sets an explicit box for the chevron/icon, but the later, equal-specificity rule resets it back to , so the fixed icon box is silently lost for this specific picker. ## Suggested fix See follow-up comment / Slack thread — proposal is to (1) give the header row an explicit, definite height (matching / ) instead of only , so the nested chain resolves deterministically instead of drifting; (2) set an explicit, unitless on and descendants to remove half-leading rounding ambiguity; (3) restore the fixed icon box in ; (4) consider visually separating the diff-stat badge from the branch/changeset dropdown so the clickable control and the read-only summary aren't fused into one pill. --- Problematic UI from Slack discussion

text: Claude custom endpoint (Messages API): 400 "thinking block bound to a different conversation" mid-turn in long agent tool loops. Anthropic's [Preserved thinking docs]( say each thinking block's signature is tied to everything that came before it in the conversation. title: Agents window: picking a canvas from "+ › Canvas" fails with "command … not found"
text: Agents window: picking a canvas from "+ › Canvas" fails with "command … not found". In the Agents window, picking a canvas from the **+** (Add Tab) **› Canvas** menu sometimes does nothing, and this error is logged: It happens when the chat updates between opening the menu and clicking an item, so it shows up most while the agent is responding. Opening the menu again and picking the same canvas usually works. - VS Code Version: 1.142.0-insider (d5dfbe9aa2c84cc3cbc3d4926a5155983aceeef1) - OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 - Regression from #340575. That change is in , but not in 1.141.1 stable. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set to , and make at least one canvas available to the agent, for example the Agent Plan canvas. 2. In the Agents window, open a chat that has no canvas open yet, and send a message. 3. While the response is still coming in, click **+** above the right-hand editor area and open **Canvas**. 4. Wait a few seconds, then pick a canvas. **Expected:** the canvas opens. **Actual:** nothing opens, and the error above is logged. ### Why it happens 1. **Every canvas in the menu gets its own numbered command.** The menu item runs , and is assigned when the command is registered. A canvas is meant to keep its number for as long as it is listed. 2. **The list is emptied before every reload.** reloads the available canvases whenever the chat's value changes, and empties the list first. Emptying it unregisters all of those commands. When the reload finishes, they are registered again with **new** numbers. 3. **The chat's value changes much more often than its canvases do.** #340575 stopped deduplicating it on purpose, so that "canvas registry changed" signals from the agent host reach the window. As a side effect, a chat with no open canvas now produces a new empty array on every chat update, and every canvas state update produces a new array too. 4. **An open menu keeps the commands it was opened with.** If a reload happens before you click, the command behind the item no longer exists. In a running Agents window, logpoints showed the list being emptied and reloaded about 10 times in two minutes, with the open-canvas commands renumbered from to . Each reload also sent its own request to the agent host. ### Proposed fix - Keep the current list while the same chat reloads, and only clear it when you switch chats or canvases become unavailable. Canvases that are still listed then keep their command. - Skip the update when a reload returns the same list. - Run at most one reload per chat at a time, plus one follow-up for changes that arrive in the meantime. A possible follow-up is a dedicated "canvas registry changed" signal from the agent host, so the window doesn't reload the list on unrelated chat updates.

title: Webview extensions stuck loading in remote windows: resource requests return 401 ( ) — VS Code 1.141.1
text: Webview extensions stuck loading in remote windows: resource requests return 401 ( ) — VS Code 1.141.1. ### Environment | | | |---|---| | VS Code | 1.141.1 | | Commit | | | Client | Windows (desktop, Electron) | | Remote A | WSL2 — | | Remote B | Remote-SSH — | | Affected extension | 2.3.2 (any webview extension) | ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start VS Code 1.141.1. 2. Open window **A** and connect to WSL ( ); open any folder. 3. Open window **B** and connect to a remote over SSH ( ). 4. In window **A**, open a webview-based extension view (e.g. OpenChamber's sidebar). ### Actual behavior The webview stays on the loading screen forever. The application bundle never executes. DevTools console: ### Expected behavior The webview resource is served and the extension loads normally. The same window loads correctly when the other remote window is closed. ### Analysis The service worker does not originate the 401 — it forwards the status issued by the host renderer: The host issues for exactly one reason ( , ): comes from → : is only populated when the window's *current* remote connection matches the authority the webview asked for: So when the window's active connection is not the one that owns the webview, is and every resource is denied. This gate applies only to remote windows — local windows are unaffected. ### Secondary observation The authority reaching the host appears in escaped form ( encodes non-alphanumeric characters as , and the hostname is then lowercased by the URL parser): The reverse transform ( ) does not appear anywhere in the shipped (0 occurrences), so the host receives while the registered remote authority is . Since contains an uppercase character, the two can never compare equal. It may be worth checking whether an unescape step is missing here, or whether the comparison should be case-insensitive. ### Workaround Close the other remote window, then reload the affected window. Launching VS Code from the Windows Start menu (rather than running from inside WSL) also avoids the condition. ### Notes on confidence The workaround was confirmed, but the isolating experiment changed three variables at once (closed the SSH window, restarted all windows, and changed the launch path), so the single contributing factor is not fully isolated. The code path above was located statically and explains the observed 401, but has not been confirmed against a trace log.

title: Webview resources fail with 401 when the remote authority contains uppercase letters (e.g. WSL distro )
text: Webview resources fail with 401 when the remote authority contains uppercase letters (e.g. WSL distro ). Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. Reproducing it needs the WSL extension plus an extension that opens a webview from the remote. - VS Code Version: 1.141.1 (stable, commit 7baac39ec3), Windows desktop - OS Version: Windows 10.0.26300.9550 - WSL: 3.0.3.0 (kernel 6.18.54.1-1), distro (Fedora Linux 44) - WSL extension: ms-vscode-remote.remote-wsl 0.104.3 - Extension where it showed up: mhutchie.git-graph 1.30.0 ## Summary When a window's remote authority contains uppercase letters, webviews from remote extensions can't load their local resources. Every resource request returns 401 and the webview stays blank. With WSL, this happens when a folder is opened with from a distro whose name has capitals, which gives the remote authority . The same folder opened with the lowercase authority works. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use a WSL distro with uppercase letters in its name, here . 2. In that distro, into a git repository and run . The window log records . 3. Open a webview from a remote extension that loads its scripts and styles through and , for example **Git Graph: View Git Graph**. 4. The webview stays blank. The main window's DevTools console shows: The extension host never receives a message from the webview, because its script never loads. 5. Close the window and reopen the same folder with a lowercase authority: The webview now loads normally. **Expected:** webview resources load whatever the case of the remote authority. ## Cause This comes from reading the shipped 1.141.1 bundle. Names below are de-minified approximations; the source files are and . 1. **The authority gets lowercased.** Webview resource URIs carry the authority in a hostname: . The webview service worker rebuilds the authority from , which the browser always lowercases. So comes back as . 2. ** compares it case-sensitively.** It only looks up the remote OS when the request's authority exactly equals the connection's: 3. **The mismatch becomes a 401.** With undefined, returns nothing for a URI ( ). then logs at trace level and returns . answers the service worker with . The root check that follows ( → ) already ignores case. That makes the strict in the one case-sensitive step. **Suggested fix:** compare the authorities in with , or otherwise ignore case. **Workaround:** open WSL folders with a lowercase authority, either with or from **File → Open Recent**.

title: Webviews fail with 401 on WSL when distro name has uppercase letters (remoteAuthority case mismatch)
text: Webviews fail with 401 on WSL when distro name has uppercase letters (remoteAuthority case mismatch). ### Description In VS Code 1.141.1, all webviews (Markdown preview, Claude Code extension panel) render blank when the window is connected to WSL via (distro name with an uppercase letter), e.g. after running from the WSL shell. Opening the same folder as (lowercase) works. ### Steps to reproduce 1. WSL2 with a distro named , Remote - WSL installed. 2. In the WSL shell: (opens authority ). 3. Open any file and press Ctrl+Shift+V. Expected: preview renders. Actual: blank panel. Webview DevTools shows: GET net::ERR_ABORTED 401 (Unauthorized) ### Workaround (lowercase) makes webviews work. ### Analysis The service worker is registered and active (checked via remote debugging); it just forwards the 401 it receives from the window. The 401 comes from in workbench.desktop.main.js, which only resolves the remote OS when the connection authority equals the resource authority: const os = t.scheme === "vscode-remote" && remoteAgentService.getConnection()?.remoteAuthority === t.authority ? (await remoteAgentService.getEnvironment())?.os : undefined; If is undefined, the access check for vscode-remote resources returns AccessDenied, which becomes a 401. The resource authority is derived from the webview host name ( ), which the URL parser lowercases to , while the connection authority is , so the strict comparison fails. Suggest comparing authorities case-insensitively (host names are case-insensitive). The remote server is healthy: requesting the same file from /vscode-remote-resource with the right token returns 200, a wrong or missing token returns 403, and the server never logged the failing requests. ### Environment - VS Code 1.141.1 (user setup), commit 7baac39ec3ca969dab74ac12c097f6a486e46593, Electron 43.7.7 - Remote - WSL 0.104.3, WSL 2.7.3.0, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 - .wslconfig: networkingMode=mirrored, dnsTunneling=true, autoProxy=true, firewall=true

title: WSL Webview resources return 401 due to remoteAuthority casing mismatch (wsl+Ubuntu vs wsl+ubuntu)
text: WSL Webview resources return 401 due to remoteAuthority casing mismatch (wsl+Ubuntu vs wsl+ubuntu). ### Environment - VS Code: 1.141.1 - Commit: 7baac39ec3ca969dab74ac12c097f6a486e46593 - Windows desktop client connected to WSL Ubuntu - Remote - WSL extension: 0.104.3 - Affected extension: OpenAI Codex ( ) - Codex versions tested in WSL: 26.1007.21434 and 26.930.31730 ### Description The Codex Webview fails to load when I open VS Code from an Ubuntu terminal using . This workflow worked before October 13, 2026. Local updater logs show that VS Code completed an update on that day. I suspect an update regression, although I have not tested the previous VS Code version. Both Codex versions listed above exhibit the failure. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use Windows VS Code with the Remote - WSL extension and a WSL distribution named . 2. Install the Codex extension in WSL. 3. From an Ubuntu terminal, open a project with: 4. Open the Codex sidebar. 5. The Webview fails to initialize. ### Expected behavior The Codex sidebar loads normally when VS Code is launched using from WSL. ### Actual behavior Webview JavaScript and CSS requests return HTTP 401. The Windows renderer log reports: The WSL extension log shows that the Codex app-server initializes successfully, followed by: ### Investigation The WSL launch script constructs the connection authority using: Here, is , so the connection authority is . However, the failing Webview resource requests use . In the installed VS Code bundle, uses a strict comparison between the connection's and the resource URI's before obtaining the remote OS. When these differ in casing, remains undefined. The resource resolver then returns early, before checking the resource roots or reading the file. This produces , which is mapped to HTTP 401. An isolated check using the installed OS-selection and resource-loading functions reproduced this behavior. The URI and filesystem services in that check were test doubles, not a live Webview. The current Codex Webview assets exist and are readable, and its extension code sets and uses . ### Confirmed workaround Opening a new window with an explicitly lowercase authority restores the Codex UI: This suggests that inconsistent authority casing is responsible for the resource-loading failure. Could you investigate whether the remote OS lookup should use a normalized or case-insensitive authority comparison?

VS Code: 1.141.1 (commit 7baac39ec3), Electron 43.7.7, Chromium 150 OS: Windows 11 + WSL2, distro name "Ubuntu" Steps to reproduce: 1. Open a folder in WSL via from the Ubuntu shell (remote authority becomes ) 2. Open any .md file and run "Markdown: Open Preview" 3. Preview is blank Webview DevTools > Network: every webview resource fails with "401 Unauthorized (from service worker)", e.g. The direct vscode-remote-resource request to the server returns 200, so the server and connection token are fine. title: Remote webview resources denied (401) when WSL distro name has uppercase letters
text: Remote webview resources denied (401) when WSL distro name has uppercase letters. ### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled? Not tested — webviews from multiple unrelated extensions are affected (Atlassian and ), which points at core webview resource loading. - VS Code Version: 1.141.1 (commit ), Electron 43.7.7, Chromium 150.0.7871.250 - OS Version: Windows (client) + WSL distro named (remote) ### Summary When connected to a WSL distro whose name contains uppercase letters ( ), every extension webview stays blank. Their local scripts fail to load with . The same extensions render correctly in a local (non-WSL) window. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Connect to a WSL distro whose name contains uppercase letters (here ). 2. Open any extension webview that loads local resources via , e.g. **Atlassian: Open Settings** or a GitHub Pull Request description. 3. Webview remains blank/loading. ### Observed Webview devtools: Note the webview iframe query has (uppercase ), while the resource host is lowercase. Window log (trace): The file exists on the remote at that path. ### Suspected cause (from reading source; not verified with a debugger) In 1.141.1, resolves only when the authority matches exactly: and now returns (→ → 401) when for URIs. The authority is encoded into the resource **hostname** by / , and Chromium lowercases hostnames, so after the request authority is while the connection authority is . The strict comparison fails, so all remote webview resources are denied. In 1.140.0, / had no check, so this path did not exist there. (I have not yet confirmed by downgrading that 1.140 works on this machine.) A case-insensitive authority comparison (e.g. via ) would likely fix it. ### Things already ruled out - Restarting WSL ( ), reloading the window. - Corporate proxy / TLS interception: the 401 is produced by the webview service worker / , not the network. - Launching with an explicitly lowercase authority ( ) did not help, presumably because the WSL resolver canonicalizes back to the distro name.

title: Agent Host: create_pull_request runs the runtime's built-in tool instead of the GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool
text: Agent Host: create_pull_request runs the runtime's built-in tool instead of the GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool. In an Agent Host (Copilot CLI) session, calling the tool always reports . This happens even though the tool the model loaded is the one forwarded from the GitHub Pull Requests extension ( , reference name ). The logs show that two handlers run for the same tool call ID: 1. The window runs the GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool and sends a with that tool's own result. 2. The Copilot runtime also runs its **built-in** tool, which belongs to the cloud coding agent and needs a cloud-agent callback URL. Its failure is the result the model receives. The extension's result never reaches the model. ### Versions - VS Code Insiders 1.142.0-insider ( ) - GitHub Copilot Chat 0.70.2026101201 (bundled 1.0.73) - GitHub Pull Requests 0.169.2026101204 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start an Agent Host Copilot session in a worktree for a GitHub repo, and push a branch. 2. Ask the agent to open a PR so that it calls . 3. The tool fails with . ### Logs (same tool call ) : the extension tool runs in the window. In this run it also failed, for an unrelated reason covered below. AHP transport log: the client's completion is accepted, then a second completion from the runtime arrives about 30 ms later. The model sees the second one. : ### Likely cause [ ]( forwards client tools under their reference name. It only sets for tools listed in [ ]( and today that's only semantic search. So the forwarded has the same name as the runtime's built-in tool, and the runtime appears to execute its built-in tool. The SDK docs say a name clash without should be an error, but here the clash seems to go unreported. ### Impact - can't succeed from a local Agent Host session; the model always gets the error above. - If the extension tool **does** succeed, the PR gets created while the agent is told it failed. The agent then retries or falls back to , which risks duplicate attempts and extra turns. I see the agent fall back to regularly. ### Possible fixes - Set when forwarding a client tool whose name matches a runtime built-in, at least for . - Or exclude the runtime's built-in in local Agent Host sessions. - Or forward the extension tool under its full ID ( ) so the names don't clash. ### Related, separate problem The GitHub Pull Requests extension's tool looks for the repository among the window's open folders ( → "No repository found for microsoft/vscode. Make sure to have the repository open."). An Agents window session's worktree usually isn't open in that window, so the tool would fail there even after the name clash is fixed.

title: BYOK: is stripped from tool and sub-constraints are downgraded into description text, so the model fills mutually exclusive fields
text: BYOK: is stripped from tool and sub-constraints are downgraded into description text, so the model fills mutually exclusive fields. **Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?**: N/A - this requires a BYOK model provider. The third-party provider is not at fault (evidence below). ## Summary When a tool's JSON Schema uses a **top-level combinator** ( / / / / / / ), that constraint **never reaches the **. It is deleted, and the sub-constraints inside it are downgraded into plain description text. The model therefore has no way to know the fields are mutually exclusive, fills several of them at once, and the runtime - which still validates against the original schema - rejects every call. This makes a core built-in tool ( ) **unusable on any BYOK provider**, permanently. ## Environment | Component | Version | |---|---| | VS Code | 1.141.0 (commit ), win32 | | Copilot Chat extension | 0.69.0 (bundled) | | Agent host runtime | 1.0.17-unstable.37397886721.gad270aa | | Bundled CLI runtime (in the Copilot extension) | 1.0.73 | | Model | BYOK, registered via a third-party | ## Steps to reproduce 1. Register a BYOK OpenAI-compatible model and select it in agent mode. 2. Send any message that causes the model to call the built-in tool (i.e. ask it to message a subagent). 3. Observe: the tool call is always rejected, because the model emits + + together. **Control group:** the sibling tool has a single optional selector and only - it succeeds **100%** of the time on the same model. Only the tool whose constraint is expressed with fails. ## Evidence A - the source schema is correct Extracted verbatim from the Copilot SDK/CLI runtime binary ( ), identical in both runtimes present on this machine: Note and the 3-branch that makes the selector fields mutually exclusive. ## Evidence B - what the actually receives Captured in from , for the same request ( ): Top-level keys are now only ** ** - is gone. ## Diff | Keyword | Source schema | Delivered to provider | Disposition | |---|---|---|---| | (3 mutually exclusive branches) | present | **0 branches** | **deleted** | | | | | kept (so this is *not* strict-mode normalization) | | | present | present | kept | | | - | 0 across all 123 tools | removed | | / / | array **keywords** | moved into : | downgraded | | | keyword | moved into : | downgraded | Two independent rewrites are happening, and both are measurable in the same payload. ## Impact - : **568 / 568 calls failed** on this setup. : 6 / 6 succeeded. - Any BYOK model is affected; this is not model-specific. - Any tool using a top-level combinator is affected - not just built-ins. Across the 123 tools present in one request, **zero** carried / / / . - The failure is silent: the model is given a schema with no mutual-exclusion information, so from its perspective it is complying correctly. ## Not the BYOK extension's fault The third-party provider forwards to the wire unchanged. I verified this by calling its own converter offline with a schema containing : the was still present in its output. The loss therefore happens **before** the provider is called. ## Likely code location (lines ~132-139) deletes these keywords with no family guard: That matches the deletion, removal, and the fact that (which is in no removal set) survives. It does **not** explain the description downgrade - the / text does not exist anywhere in VS Code's shipped artifacts (verified with UTF-8 *and* UTF-16 full-text scans of all bundles, the asar, and both runtime binaries), so I assume that part happens in the Copilot runtime's schema projection. The value in matches the source schema's exactly. ## What I could not verify - I could not confirm the exact function/line that performs the description downgrade - it is outside VS Code's artifacts. - I did not test whether this also affects the built-in Copilot models (they may consume the schema through a different path). - Not retested on Insiders / 1.142+. ## Notes - is irrelevant here: is never expanded, so strict-mode normalization is not what is happening. - Related but distinct open issues: #320145 (params omitted), #320926 (schema not OpenAI-conformant). If keeping the restricted schema vocabulary is intentional, then the mutual-exclusion information needs to survive in the description text as well, otherwise only the model pays the cost of a validation the model cannot see.

title: Agent Host auth restart wait blocks history restore, unrelated session prompts, and cancellation
text: Agent Host auth restart wait blocks history restore, unrelated session prompts, and cancellation. ## Summary A GitHub authentication update from a reconnecting Mission Control client requested a restart of the shared Copilot SDK client. The restart was deferred while existing chats had in-flight work. Subsequently, opening an unrelated existing session blocked its history restore waiting for that restart. The important escalation is that a client action waiting for this restore occupied the window's **per-client dispatch queue**. Later actions for other sessions, including a new prompt and cancellation requests, were queued behind it. The host still answered pings promptly, and new session shells could be created, but the window could not advance its chats. This is related to #341007 and #340468, which describe the deferred-auth-restart wait during new-session preparation. This report captures the additional **history-restore → cross-session action-queue blockage → cancellation blockage** failure mode. The new prompt here did not reach or SDK initialization. ## Environment and evidence - VS Code Insiders on macOS arm64; exact installed commit not established. - Agents window using the local Copilot SDK Agent Host provider, with Copilot Connectors enabled and Mission Control connected. - Evidence: Export Agent Host Debug Logs bundle analyzed across desktop AHP traffic, Mission Control AHP traffic, Agent Host logs, and SDK process logs. Full bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session content. ## Observed timeline One incident on October 12, 2026. Times below are PDT (UTC−07:00). | Time | Observation | | --- | --- | | 15:25:50 | The desktop client authenticated for ` | | 15:27:19.368 | A Mission Control client initialized after attempting a reconnect. | | 15:27:19.952 | The Mission Control client sent for ` | | 15:27:20.189 | Agent Host logged . | | 15:27:20.203 | Agent Host logged . | | 15:31:41 | An existing chat's tool became ready. No completion for that tool appears through the end of the export. This supports at least one chat remaining busy; it does not establish every busy chat/subagent state. | | 15:40:19 | Opening an older session started a history restore. Agent Host again logged a connector-authentication restart deferred behind two busy chats. Desktop action sequence 43 ( ) for the restoring chat never received an authoritative echo. | | 15:41:19 | The watchdog logged for the older session. | | 15:42:06 | The requested new session was created successfully, with its SDK backing deferred until first send. Its initial chat snapshot had no turns. | | 15:42:11 | The desktop sent the new session's config, active-client update, and prompt as sequences 45–47. None received an authoritative echo. There was no SDK session initialization or model request for that prompt in the captured logs. | | 15:46:45 / 15:48:38 | Cancellation actions for existing chats, sequences 53 and 58, also never received authoritative echoes. Later actions remained blocked through export. | | Through 15:48:38 | AHP pings continued receiving responses in approximately 0–1 ms. The user reported that CPU was not pegged. | ## Mechanism 1. applies authentication to the shared provider. With Copilot Connectors enabled, a changed credential requests a shared-client restart. 2. requires the SDK client's captured connector authentication to match the current credential. On mismatch, it requests a restart and awaits . 3. deliberately defers that restart while any live chat has an active turn or subagent, to avoid tearing down active work. 4. for a nonresident session must acquire the SDK client to resume it. In this incident that acquisition waited for the deferred restart. 5. serializes asynchronous dispatches by **client ID**, across session channels. The read-state action joined the pending restore, holding up all subsequent actions from that window, including cancellation of existing work. The triggering sender was Mission Control in this incident, but the provider-level mechanism is not Mission-Control-specific: another AHP client, such as an editor window, can trigger it if authentication changes the token value or credential refresh mode. Re-sending the same token with the same mode is a no-op. There is no evidence here of a CLI command, sign-out, or token expiration. **Diagnostic limitation:** is emitted when either the token value or refresh mode changes. Tokens are redacted, so this bundle does not distinguish those cases or identify the remote device behind the Mission Control client. ## Relevant implementation Source inspected at (not asserted to be the installed build's commit): - [Credential change detection]( - [Provider authentication update and restart request]( - [Session acquisition waits for connector-authentication restart]( - [Restart deferral behind busy chats]( - [History lookup resolves/resumes the SDK session]( - [Per-client dispatch serialization and restore wait]( The connector-authentication acquisition wait was introduced by Paul ( ) on September 26 in #337649. Steps to Reproduce: The following is inferred from the captured incident, not an independently rerun reproduction: 1. Enable Copilot Connectors and keep a Copilot Agent Host chat busy, for example waiting for user input. 2. Have an AHP client authenticate with a credential that changes the shared provider's token value or refresh mode while existing work remains active. 3. In the desktop window, open a nonresident session whose history needs SDK resume. Let its read-state action wait for the restore. 4. Create another session and send a prompt from the same window. 5. Attempt to cancel existing work from that window. ## Expected behavior / fix requirements - An authentication-blocked history restore must not indefinitely block unrelated sessions' actions from the same client. - Cancellation must remain actionable while restores or session acquisition are blocked. - The UI should expose the actual wait reason or an actionable error rather than spinning indefinitely with no model request. - Preserve the safety of existing turns: restarting the shared SDK client underneath active work is not a sufficient fix. No fix or independent reproduction was performed as part of this log investigation. Restarting the agent host is a likely recovery because it clears the in-memory waits, but recovery was not verified in this incident. (Written by Copilot)

title: Agents Window: agent asks to retry a scheduled workspace move before ending its turn
text: Agents Window: agent asks to retry a scheduled workspace move before ending its turn. Testing #340889 ## Environment and Reproduction Scope - Code OSS 1.143.0, development build, Agents Window. - Commit: . - Windows x64, build 26200. - Authenticated local Copilot agent host; **Auto selected GPT-6 Luna** on the affected turn. - **Observed once. This is a model-dependent workflow failure, not an established deterministic host or Git defect.** ## Steps Leading to the Failure 1. Open the Agents Window in Code OSS, sign in to Copilot, and start a folder chat in a dedicated Agent Host Protocol (AHP) checkout. Have a separate VS Code checkout available. 2. Ask it to explain how AHP represents main/peer chats and their state updates, without editing. 3. Ask it to move the same chat to the absolute path of the VS Code checkout and trace how VS Code implements those concepts. Confirm use of the folder directly, without isolation. Wait for the successful move and continuation. 4. Ask a follow-up and request the return move, for example: > Using both repositories, briefly explain how creating a peer reaches the Agents Window. Separate the protocol contract from the VS Code implementation. Then move THIS chat back to using the folder directly, and clarify the relevant protocol definition. Continue in this chat and do not make changes. 5. Approve the workspace-change confirmation. 6. On the affected run, observe the agent's tool calls before it finishes the initiating turn. ## Expected After the move is scheduled, the agent ends its turn. The host then changes the workspace and automatically continues the original task in AHP, without requiring another move request or user intervention. ## Actual The workspace-change tool acknowledged the scheduled move, but the agent continued during the same turn: 1. It ran AHP-relative commands while its working directory was still the VS Code checkout, producing missing-file errors. 2. It queried session metadata, which still reported the old working directory. 3. It interpreted that as a failed move and asked the user to confirm retrying the same move. The additional question kept the initiating turn open, preventing the pending move from completing. ## Recovery Instead of approving another move, I replied: > Do not retry. The workspace move is scheduled to happen AFTER this turn ends. End your current turn now, without more tools, so the pending move can complete. The agent ended the turn, the workspace-change notice appeared, and the original task continued automatically in AHP with its conversation history intact. The workspace-change tool description already instructs the agent to finish its turn. This report is not attributing the failure to a missing instruction, and further reproduction is needed to establish frequency. ## Screenshot The screenshot shows the unnecessary retry question: the agent says the move was acknowledged but treats the still-old working directory as a reason to retry. ![Agent requests a retry while the acknowledged workspace move is still pending](

title: Copilot Connectors: WorkIQ and Kusto Sign In still fails with insufficient_scope after #340547
text: Copilot Connectors: WorkIQ and Kusto Sign In still fails with insufficient_scope after #340547. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host / Copilot SDK provider. Exact runtime version was not established from the retained logs. - VS Code Version: Insiders , commit , build date . - OS Version: macOS. - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents Window, Copilot Connectors surfaced as MCP servers, Sign In. - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-6.1 Sol; the failure occurs during connector authentication, independently of model invocation. - Logs: Agent Host debug export captured October 12. Sanitized evidence is included below. The full archive contains credentials/session content and is not attached publicly. ## Follow-up to #340546 WorkIQ and Kusto connector **Sign In** still repeatedly fails in Insiders after the fix in #340547. The installed build contains the fix: comparing its commit with the merge commit of #340547, , reports the installed build is 186 commits ahead and zero behind. Installed product metadata predates the captured failures. The exported logs independently identify the Insiders profile, but do not include a definitive build fingerprint, so this verifies the installed build rather than independently identifying the running process's commit. The earlier PR stops retrying an unchanged token after silent authentication is rejected and restores the Authentication required state. It does not establish that interactive Sign In updates the credential the managed connector actually uses. This report tracks that remaining end-to-end failure, not just the spinner presentation. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open an Agents Window Copilot session containing the WorkIQ and Kusto Copilot connectors. 2. Open Customizations and inspect their MCP server entries. Both require authentication. 3. Use **Sign In** and retry the affected connector. 4. Observe that the connector does not become usable. It returns to with an insufficient-scope challenge despite client logs reporting authentication success. **Expected:** Sign In obtains the required authorization for the selected account, updates the credential used on subsequent connector requests, and allows tool discovery. A rejected credential produces an actionable failure rather than an unverified success report. **Actual:** Both connectors remain unable to authenticate. The GitHub connector gateway receives a credential without the required scope. Client-side token forwarding reports success, but subsequent MCP requests still fail. ## Confirmed log evidence All times in this section are October 12, 2026, Pacific daylight time, UTC-7. The same session records the failure for both connectors at approximately **10:30:14, 10:34:11, and 10:45:55**. The affected endpoints are: - ` - ` Both return: Representative ordering: The client forwards requests with . All 239 matched connector authenticate RPCs across the captured client connection return without a JSON-RPC error. That count includes other sessions and automatic activity; it is not 239 manual sign-in attempts in the affected session. Captured incremental connector state updates alternate between and , with . None of those updates reaches a ready state. At 10:31:29.581, the client lists GitHub authentication sessions with: Those recorded session scopes do not prove that GitHub granted them to the token sent on the connector request. The gateway's header is the evidence for the effective credential. These failures occur at the **GitHub connector gateway**, before any WorkIQ or Azure Data Explorer backend authentication can explain them. ## Suspected mechanism, not yet proven for the exported runtime Source inspection suggests a credential-routing mismatch: - Generic MCP Sign In supplies a resource-scoped OAuth token. - Runtime-owned connectors use the selected session account's GitHub credential provider rather than the generic MCP OAuth token provider. - A separately scoped token can therefore be handed off without replacing the credential used on the connector's HTTP requests. Separately, the VS Code client logs after forwarding the token, without waiting for a successful MCP connection or tool-list request. A successful RPC is not proof that the gateway accepted the credential. The logs prove the incorrect effective scopes and success/failure mismatch. Matching the exported runtime revision or reproducing with credential-origin diagnostics is still needed to establish the precise routing cause. ## Suggested investigation and acceptance checks - Verify whether connector Sign In updates the same account credential source used by managed connector HTTP requests. - Preserve the selected account while acquiring . - Confirm the gateway sees the required scope after authorization and both WorkIQ and Kusto reach ready state and expose tools. - Avoid reporting verified sign-in success based only on token forwarding. - Keep the rejected-token suppression from #340547; confirm automatic retries do not replay the same rejected credential. - Add an end-to-end regression case where an ordinary GitHub session and a connector-scoped session coexist, then exercise Sign In through tool discovery. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: GitHub Share menu should allowlist supported resource schemes
text: GitHub Share menu should allowlist supported resource schemes. ## Problem The built-in GitHub extension contributes to with this condition in : This excludes one unsupported scheme instead of explicitly including supported schemes. As a result, the command appears on chat editor tabs whose resource uses , even though it cannot share the chat. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open a workspace with a GitHub repository. Use a local branch without an upstream to reproduce the publication prompt below. 2. Open a Copilot CLI chat in an editor tab in the normal VS Code window. 3. Right-click the chat tab and select **Share > Copy vscode.dev Link**. ## Actual behavior The action is offered for the chat editor. A live dbgjs trace confirmed that its handler receives an URI. The GitHub link builder falls back to the workspace's GitHub repository when the resource does not belong to a repository, then runs its publication checks. In the tested workspace, this displayed: > The current branch is not published to the remote. Would you like to publish your branch before copying a link? The offered action was **Publish Branch & Copy Link**, despite the user selecting Share on a chat rather than a repository file. No publication was approved during the investigation. ## Expected behavior / proposed fix Use an **inclusion list of supported resource schemes**, not an exclusion list of unsupported schemes. Only show this contribution for resources the GitHub link implementation actually supports. Determine the allowlist from supported local, remote, and virtual resource workflows rather than assuming that every scheme other than is valid. The link builder should also reject unsupported resources before falling back to a repository or running publication checks, so direct command invocation cannot trigger unrelated Git actions. ## Related surface The GitHub Pull Requests extension contributes **Copy GitHub Permalink**, **Copy GitHub Permalink as Markdown**, and **Copy GitHub Head Link** to the same submenu with conditions based on GitHub remotes and window type, without a resource-scheme restriction. Its permalink action was also tested on the chat and returned These contributions should follow the same supported-resource inclusion approach in that extension. ## Environment - Windows - VS Code Insiders commit: ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2 - GitHub Pull Requests extension: 0.169.2026101204

title: Copilot Connectors: new chat waits for shared-client restart while another chat is active
text: Copilot Connectors: new chat waits for shared-client restart while another chat is active. ## Summary After Copilot Connector authentication changes, a new Copilot chat can wait indefinitely for the shared Copilot client to restart while an unrelated chat in another window has an active turn. The waiting chat displays , then , although it has not reached a model request. This also blocks agent-driven testing: the controlling chat waits for the new chat, but its own active turn prevents the client restart needed to launch that chat. ## Environment - Windows, VS Code Insiders commit - Copilot session target; two windows sharing an agent host - - ## Steps observed 1. Keep a Copilot chat running in window A. In this case it used dbgjs Playwright to control window B. 2. In window B, connect Microsoft Learn Docs and Azure Data Explorer through Customizations > Discover > Copilot Connectors, completing browser authorization. 3. Reload window B and start a completely new Copilot chat. 4. Send: 5. Keep the original chat in window A active while waiting for or investigating the result. ## Actual The new chat remains in , without a tool call or model response, while the UI indicates reasoning/model delay. At 11:09:42 the agent-host log reported: At 11:10:42: A non-pausing dbgjs logpoint in the live agent host confirmed: - Pending restart reasons: and . - A restart waiter existed; credential updates were no longer running. - The only busy chat was the controlling chat in window A ( , ). - The pending turn belonged to the new chat in window B. No credential values were inspected. The diagnostic logpoint was removed afterward. ## Recovery verified Ending the controlling chat turn allowed the waiting test chat to finish. On the next inspection, its transcript contained the requested Microsoft Learn title and URL and reported a total duration of **12m 28s**. No forced client restart was performed. Connector tool-call details were still being verified when this issue was filed. ## Relevant implementation At the tested revision: - [copilotAgent.ts:1228]( waits for a restart when connector authentication differs. - [copilotAgent.ts:1356]( restart is deferred while another chat has in-flight work. - [copilotAgent.ts:1502]( busy work is counted across live sessions. - [copilotAgent.ts:1395]( chat completion retries the deferred restart. ## Expected Connector authentication changes should not silently block new chats behind unrelated long-running turns. If a shared-client restart cannot be avoided, show the actual wait reason and provide a safe way forward instead of presenting it as model reasoning. Consider refreshing connector authentication without restarting the client shared by unrelated windows. One observed reproduction, with live-state confirmation and recovery; not independently rerun.
