title: Agent-host sessions with BYOK models: responses are buffered until completion — no incremental streaming, cancel does not reach the provider
text: Agent-host sessions with BYOK models: responses are buffered until completion — no incremental streaming, cancel does not reach the provider. - Copilot Chat Extension Version: bundled (VS Code 1.141.0) - VS Code Version: 1.141.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 (also present on a second machine with the same version) - Feature: agent sessions running in the local agent host process (the mode picker option "Copilot (runs the Copilot SDK agent in a local agent host process)") - Selected model: any BYOK model via a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (verified through a local logging proxy) - Logs: outgoing request timings captured at a local OpenAI-compatible proxy (details below) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a BYOK provider with an OpenAI-compatible base URL. 2. In the chat mode picker, choose the agent host option ("Copilot (runs the Copilot SDK agent in a local agent host process)") rather than "Local". 3. Send a prompt that produces a longer answer (thinking + body). 4. Observe: nothing renders incrementally. The full content (reasoning and body) appears at once when the turn completes. 5. Press Stop while the turn is running: the request to the provider **keeps running** (visible at the proxy / provider logs) until it completes on its own. 6. A/B control: in the same window, switch the mode picker to "Local" and repeat — streaming renders incrementally and Stop terminates the provider request immediately. ## Actual result - No incremental display of reasoning/body — the whole response is emitted at completion time. - Cancel does not propagate to the provider; the upstream request runs to completion (billing/tokens still consumed). - Tool-call progress is also not shown live (tool invocations appear only after the turn finishes) — possibly the same root cause, listed here as a suspected co-symptom. ## Expected result The agent-host path should stream incrementally like the "Local" path, and Stop should cancel the in-flight provider request. ## Root cause hypothesis (source-level, from reading current main) The BYOK LM bridge appears to be buffered by design: - — its doc comment states "ships the request to the renderer and **resolves with the buffered completion** the renderer produced from the LM API". - — synthesizes SSE frames from the buffered result after completion, which matches the "everything at once" rendering and the missing live tool-call progress. - Cancellation seemingly does not cross the reverse-RPC bridge back to the renderer's LM API request. For machine-driven agent turns this is tolerable, but for interactive use the mode picker makes it easy to land in this path for regular chat, and the experience regression vs. the "Local" path is severe (no live tokens, no effective Stop, provider cost keeps accruing after cancel). ## Relationship to recent work #339830 (forwarding tool-result images across this same BYOK bridge) recently landed — great to see this path under active maintenance. Streaming and cancellation feel like the next gaps on the same bridge. ## Workaround Switch the chat mode picker back to "Local" for interactive use.

title: Renderer livelocks in EINTR loop when automatic renderer profiling ( ) starts — Settings editor freezes
text: Renderer livelocks in EINTR loop when automatic renderer profiling ( ) starts — Settings editor freezes. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> I did but it is the number of extensions and not the extensions themselves which causes the issue ## Environment - VS Code: 1.141.0 (commit 2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c), snap package (rev 268), x64 - Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-146-generic - Session: GNOME on Wayland, VS Code running under XWayland ( ) - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti, driver 580.178.04 - : (renderer runs with , GPU process ) - : tmpfs, 32G, ~1% used - ~56 extensions installed ## Steps to reproduce 1. Linux, hardware acceleration disabled ( in ). 2. Have a typical set of extensions installed, enough that opening the Settings editor causes a long task. 3. Open Settings (UI) and search for (or navigate to the GPU Acceleration setting). ## Expected Settings editor renders. At most there's a brief stall. ## Actual The window freezes permanently. The renderer main thread stays at ~100% CPU until the process is killed. The window never recovers; it's killed or force-closed, which looks like a crash. The renderer log shows the long task right before the hang: The profiling session never completes. ## Diagnosis - **CDP:** with , the hung renderer doesn't answer or , so the main thread isn't executing interruptible JS. - ** :** 99.93% of samples are in . - ** :** a tight loop: - fd 47 → . This is a shared-memory region of ~18.5 MB, presumably a software-compositing bitmap, since GPU compositing is disabled. **Interpretation:** the long-task watchdog in ( ) starts a V8 CPU profile on the renderer. The V8 sampling profiler delivers to the main thread at a high rate. Chromium's shared-memory allocation calls on a large file and retries on . Allocating ~18.5 MB on tmpfs takes longer than the interval, so every attempt gets interrupted and restarted from scratch. The thread livelocks, never returns to the event loop, and the profiler never gets to stop. ## Isolation - : no freeze. Settings renders fast enough that no long task is reported, so profiling never starts. - Extension bisect and manual elimination: freezes with every subset tested. No single extension is responsible; any set that makes Settings slow enough triggers it. - **Workaround that fixes it:** in user settings. ## Suggested fixes - Don't let the automatic profiler run while the renderer is doing large shared-memory allocations, or lower its sampling rate. - Or upstream in Chromium: avoid restarting from zero on (block around the call, or fall back to and touch pages). - Consider defaulting to off on Linux until fixed.

title: Remote Agent Host sessions become undiscoverable after update to 1.141.0
text: Remote Agent Host sessions become undiscoverable after update to 1.141.0. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> ## Environment - Remote host: Microsoft Dev Box, Windows - Client: macOS VS Code - Connection: - Remote VS Code before update: 1.140.0 - Remote VS Code after update: 1.141.0 ## Summary After updating VS Code on a remote Windows Dev Box, existing Agent Host sessions can no longer be opened. New sessions work correctly, and the Dev Tunnel remains connected. Attempting to open an existing session reports: > Provider copilotcli is not ready to open copilotcli:/session-id; it may still be starting, so try again shortly The underlying Copilot SDK session directories, event histories, session databases, checkpoints, and worktrees still exist on disk. ## Observed update sequence 1. Windows Restart Manager began the VS Code update. 2. The pre-update remote Agent Host and Copilot runtime remained alive. 3. The replacement tunnel/Agent Host started using VS Code 1.141.0. 4. The old runtime continued holding session locks. 5. The new host initially failed to connect to the selected Agent Host with: 6. After terminating only the verified orphaned process tree and removing its stale lock files, the replacement Copilot provider started and authenticated successfully, but existing sessions still could not open. 7. Startup logs report that the provider listed only one SDK session, despite many intact session-state directories. 8. The local session index contains zero session rows. 9. Creating a brand-new remote session succeeds. ## Steps to reproduce The exact race may depend on update timing: 1. Run a persistent Agent Host through on Windows. 2. Create and use multiple Copilot CLI-backed Agent Host sessions. 3. Update VS Code on the remote host while the tunnel and Agent Host are active. 4. Reconnect from the client. 5. Attempt to open a pre-update session. ## Expected Existing sessions should be rediscovered and reopened after the update. An interrupted migration should be retryable and must preserve the prior session catalog. ## Actual Existing sessions remain visible or addressable by their Agent Host URIs, but opening them repeatedly fails with . New sessions work. The raw session data remains under , but cannot find the underlying SDK session because it is absent from the new runtime's session index. ## Additional notes - The Dev Tunnel itself is healthy. - Relay authentication and Agent Host protocol selection succeed. - Restarting the tunnel does not repair the catalog. - Restarting the replacement Agent Host does not repair the catalog. - Removing only verified stale locks from the dead runtime does not repair it. - This may be related to #339049 and presents a potential data-loss risk similar to #340552 if empty-session cleanup runs. Full logs contain private paths and repository/session information, but sanitized excerpts can be provided.

title: Markdown editor: Japanese IME candidate window and composition underline are not displayed
text: Markdown editor: Japanese IME candidate window and composition underline are not displayed. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: [1.140.0] - OS Version: [Windows 11] - Editor: Built-in Markdown Editor ( ) - IME: Japanese IME Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open any file in VS Code. 2. Reopen it using the built-in **Markdown Editor** ( → ). 3. Enable the Japanese IME (Google Jpanaese Input). 4. Start typing Japanese text and begin an IME conversion. Expected: - The IME candidate window should be displayed while converting Japanese text. - The text currently being composed/converted should have the normal IME composition indication, such as an underline. - The behavior should be equivalent to Japanese IME input in the standard Text Editor. Actual: - The IME candidate window is not displayed at all. - The text currently being composed has no underline or other visual indication of the active composition. - The text can still be converted and committed, but there is effectively no visual feedback while the IME composition is active. This appears to be specific to the built-in Markdown Editor. Japanese IME input works normally in the standard VS Code Text Editor, including both the candidate window and composition indication. There are some existing issues involving CJK/Japanese IME handling in the new Markdown Editor (for example #337197 and #336899), but I could not find one covering this specific behavior where both the candidate window and composition indication are missing.

title: Keyboard focus is not visible when focus moves to the Search Results tree view:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Search_Keyboard
text: Keyboard focus is not visible when focus moves to the Search Results tree view:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Search_Keyboard. ## GitHub Tags #A11yTCS; #Visual Studio Code Client; #E2E_VisualStudioCodeClient_Win32_Oct2026; #DesktopApp; #FTP; #Win32; #A11ySev2; #A11yMAS; #WCAG2.4.7; #Focus Visible; #a11ydb-focus-missing-no-cue; ## Issue Subcategory No visible focus indicator and no other cue ## User Experience People primarily using keyboard to navigate, with low or full vision, cannot tell which control currently has focus, so they cannot reliably predict their placement in the interface, or what would occur if they were to press Enter or Space keys. ## Repro Steps Open VS code > search in left navigation > Observe the issue ## Actual Result When keyboard focus moves to the Search Results tree view, no visible focus indicator is displayed on the focused tree item. As a result, keyboard users cannot visually determine the current focus position. ## Expected Result When keyboard focus moves to the Search Results tree view, a clearly visible focus indicator should be displayed on the currently focused tree item so keyboard users can identify the current focus location. ## How to Fix The browser default focus indicator must not be removed without an appropriate replacement. Ensure every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator, which may be rendered using the or pseudo-classes. Providing an outline is the most robust and recognizable type of focus indicator. Other styles may be used instead, but they will need to be checked when High Contrast themes are applied. E.g., styles are not rendered when a user enables Windows High Contrast themes. An easy work around is to use a transparent outline along with your custom focus style. The custom style may not render in the High Contrast theme, but the transparent outline _will_ appear. ## Environment details Application Name: VS Code (1.41.0) Edition Windows 11 Enterprise Version 25H2 OS build 26200.8390 ## Note - Please do not close this bug. title: Agents Window: workspace picker search should find older workspaces beyond visible recents
text: Agents Window: workspace picker search should find older workspaces beyond visible recents. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: Insiders, exact build not captured. Source RCA at f6f19d60c583323dc697da49cdc67c5436fccac6. - OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a local folder, then open at least ten other distinct local folders so the first folder is older in VS Code's recent history. Use ordinary folder names, not generated worktrees or folders. 2. Confirm the older folder is still available through VS Code's Open Recent picker. 3. In the Agents Window, open the new-session workspace picker using the unified picker presentation. 4. Enter the older folder's exact name in the Search field. ## Actual behavior The older folder is not found. Search filters only the items already loaded into the truncated picker list. Workspaces I can find elsewhere in VS Code, or that I opened a while ago, remain unavailable unless I browse for them again with Open Folder. ## Expected behavior Search should find matching entries from the full available workspace history, including older VS Code recent folders, folders from saved workspace files, and eligible workspaces known from existing agent sessions. Keeping the default list short is useful. That display limit should not determine which workspaces are searchable. With an empty query, show the compact recent list. With a query, search the larger known catalog and show matching entries even when they fall outside the default ten. This does not require searching arbitrary filesystem directories or discovering repositories that VS Code has never opened. ## Source-level RCA The limits apply before search: - Agents' own picked-workspace history persists only ten entries, dropping older picks: [history persistence]( - Importing VS Code history stops after ten eligible standalone folders, reads at most ten workspace files, and caps the combined imported folder list at ten: [history loading]( - The new picker then caps the merged candidates, including session-derived workspaces, at ten before building the searchable rows: [picker construction]( - The picker delegate supplies no callback to retrieve additional candidates. The action list matches text against labels and descriptions of existing items: [picker delegate]( [filtering]( Removing only the final picker limit would leave the upstream truncation in place. History retention/loading and search need to be independent of the default display cap. Existing tests explicitly enforce the ten-entry limits and should be extended to verify that search can find older entries. Validation for this report was source inspection, not an automated live reproduction. ## Related issues - #317633 asks for adding a search/filter bar. This issue concerns its search scope now that the bar exists: filtering visible recents does not solve the missing older-workspace problem. - #337129 asks to reduce visible recents so Remote remains discoverable. Searching the full history should preserve that compact default list. - #335656 asks to search parent directories. This issue only asks to search workspaces already known to VS Code or agent sessions. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: Agent picker and runtime desynchronize during Agent Host hydration and harness switching
text: Agent picker and runtime desynchronize during Agent Host hydration and harness switching. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built into VS Code Insiders 1.142.0-insider - VS Code Version: 1.142.0-insider - OS Version: macOS arm64 - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host custom-agent picker and harness switching - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Auto - Logs: Agent Host debug export showed the affected SDK session using the generic base identity instead of the selected custom-agent identity. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a new Copilot Agent Host chat and select a custom agent such as **Learn Writer**. 2. Materialize the session by sending a request. A customization refresh during the untitled-to-real session rebind can temporarily expose only the draft agent list. 3. In a new chat, switch the same composer from the Copilot harness to the built-in Local harness. **Expected** - The selected custom agent remains active while the Agent Host session hydrates. - Switching to a harness outside the agent's declared session types resets the picker to **Agent** before another request is sent. **Actual** - During session hydration, host-only custom agents can disappear from the mode list, dropping the selected agent and its instructions. - After switching to Local, the picker can still display **Learn Writer** even though the Local harness runs the generic agent. **Recordings** Before: After: **Diagnosis** - The customization provider used the merged session/draft fallback result to decide whether to wait for the first real session snapshot. A non-empty draft list could therefore bypass readiness and evict cached host-only agents. - Harness switching validated the mode target but not the mode's declared session types. Related to #336761, which has the same visible fallback symptom but also tracks a Remote-SSH agent-URI mismatch. Proposed fix: #340607

title: Agent Host: open canvases close when a send triggers a session configuration refresh
text: Agent Host: open canvases close when a send triggers a session configuration refresh. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (Agent Host core code path) - VS Code Version: Code - Insiders 1.142.0-insider (f4dfb91d30e). The code path is unchanged on at 38d9885c158. - OS Version: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64) When a message send makes the Agent Host refresh a Copilot chat's session configuration, every canvas open in that chat closes in the Agents window and doesn't come back. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Enable and, in the Agents window, start a new local Copilot session in a new worktree. 2. Have the agent open a canvas ( ) in the first turn. It opens as a tab in the side pane. 3. Send a follow-up message in the same chat. **Expected:** The canvas stays open. At most it's briefly unavailable while its provider reconnects, as with an extension reload. **Actual:** The canvas tab closes and doesn't reopen. The runtime still has the instance open: calls on it keep succeeding, and calling again with the same brings it back, as a new tab. shows the send restarting the SDK session. The same pattern was observed in two chats: The Agents window's AHP log shows the host publishing an empty canvas list at the same instant: ### Root cause 1. [ ]( [destroys the live SDK session]( and resumes it whenever the chat's configuration snapshot changed. 2. [ ]( calls [ ]( which publishes with no canvases. The Agents window treats this as authoritative membership and [closes the canvas editors]( 3. The replacement session's [ ]( adds every instance in to , and projection starts out not ready, so the runtime's rehydration events are [dropped]( Nothing re-projects the canvas, even though the runtime still has it open. This follows the [documented contract]( ("A new SDK residency starts with an empty projected canvas collection and does not restore prior open canvases"), but a configuration refresh of a chat that's in use is currently treated as a new residency. ### Why the refresh happens in this flow - The synced customization bundles are identified by [ ]( which is . The host materializes each bundle under a [path derived from its URI]( - A new worktree session starts with the repository folder as its customization scope. Once the worktree is known, the scope is re-acquired for the worktree folder. - So the bundle's / and directory change even though its content doesn't. - [ ]( then reports a difference, and the next send restarts with [ ]( - These logs predate #340079. After it, both the synced and the standalone bundle identity still include the scope hash. ### Proposed fix Hand the canvas projection over across a configuration refresh instead of clearing it: - Before destroying the live session for a refresh, capture its projected canvases, and don't publish an empty collection. - Keep each canvas resource stable per , so the Agents window keeps the same tab. Publish the carried state without a (shown as temporarily unavailable) until the provider reconnects. - Resume with , and don't ignore carried instances in the replacement session. - Let publish the new URL. - Reconcile with / once projection is ready, because rehydration can happen before that. - Drop carried canvases the runtime didn't restore. Publish an empty collection only if the resume fails. - Cold residencies (eviction, host restart) keep starting empty. Update the contract in accordingly. - Tests: a refresh keeps the canvas resource, never publishes an empty collection, and publishes the new URL without waiting for a user message. **Caveat:** even with the hand-off, the refresh restarts the canvas extension process; the canvas URL changes. The canvas therefore reloads and loses any in-memory state. Avoiding that means avoiding the restart: - Don't restart when the bundle content is unchanged. Either make the bundle identity independent of the scope roots, or materialize bundles by content. This alone fixes the flow above. - Longer term, apply client customization changes to the live session, e.g. with or , instead of restarting. This still needs validation against the runtime. ### Related - Canvases also close when switching sessions (editor working-set swap in the Agents window). That's a separate renderer bug, being fixed separately. - Residency eviction of an inactive session also drops its canvases. That's separate and not covered here. - #336587 and #337470 also concern configuration refresh/restart, but not canvases.

title: Chat sticky scroll clips messages starting with bullet points
text: Chat sticky scroll clips messages starting with bullet points. In the Agents window, long messages starting with bullet points are cut off in sticky scroll instead of showing a short preview with an ellipsis. ### Repro 1. Send a long message starting with a bullet point, e.g. . 2. Scroll until the message becomes sticky. **Expected:** Two lines followed by an ellipsis. **Actual:** The list stays expanded and is abruptly clipped, sometimes mid-line (see screenshot). ### Why The two-line clamp and ellipsis styles only target a top-level paragraph ( ). Bullet-point messages render as lists ( ), so they bypass those styles and get cut off by the sticky row's 150px height limit. This predates the resize optimization in #340147; the paragraph-only clamp dates back to #296433. ![A long bullet-point message is abruptly cut off in the Agents window sticky scroll without an ellipsis](

title: Windows emoji panel (Win+.) inserts nothing in the editor when is enabled
text: Windows emoji panel (Win+.) inserts nothing in the editor when is enabled. Type: Bug ### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled? unknown ### Environment - VS Code Version: 1.141.0 (system setup) Commit: 2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c Date: 2026-10-06T10:15:52+02:00 Electron: 43.7.7 ElectronBuildId: 15553055 Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 Node.js: 24.21.0 V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0 /copilot: 1.0.92-4.unstable.r37397886721.gad270aa /copilot-sdk: 1.0.17.37397886721.gad270aa OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 - OS Version: Windows 11 Version 25H2 (Build 26200.9168) - Keyboard layout / input language: German (de-DE) ### Description Since VS Code 1.141.0 (or even earlier), characters selected from the Windows emoji panel (opened with or ) are no longer inserted into the editor. The panel opens normally and a character can be selected (e.g. ❗, 👍, ✅), but nothing is inserted at the cursor position. No error is shown. Inserting the same characters via the clipboard (Ctrl+V) works without problems, so the issue is not related to font rendering or the characters themselves, but to text input coming through the Windows input framework (TSF/IME). The issue occurs in several workspaces. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open any text file in the editor (with default setting ). 2. Place the cursor somewhere in the text. 3. Press to open the Windows emoji panel. 4. Select an emoji or symbol, e.g. ✅. **Expected:** The selected character is inserted at the cursor position. **Actual:** Nothing is inserted. ### Workaround Adding the following to the user settings fixes the problem: "editor.editContext": false The emoji panel works again immediately after changing the setting, even without restarting VS Code. This strongly suggests that the issue lies in the EditContext-based input handling of the editor. ### Regression unknown

title: Keyboard focus moves to the document element and no visible focus indicator is displayed:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Welcome_Keyboard
text: Keyboard focus moves to the document element and no visible focus indicator is displayed:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Welcome_Keyboard. ## GitHub Tags #A11yTCS; #Visual Studio Code Client; #E2E_VisualStudioCodeClient_Win32_Oct2026; #DesktopApp; #FTP; #Win32; #A11ySev2; #A11yMAS; #WCAG2.4.7; #Focus Visible; #a11ydb-focus-missing-no-cue; #SCIM:Bug3672156; ## Issue Subcategory No visible focus indicator and no other cue ## User Experience People primarily using keyboard to navigate, with low or full vision, cannot tell which control currently has focus, so they cannot reliably predict their placement in the interface, or what would occur if they were to press Enter or Space keys. ## Repro Steps Open VS code > Help control > Welcome control > Observe the issue ## Actual Result When navigating using the keyboard, focus unexpectedly moves to the document element. At this point, no visible focus indicator is displayed, making it difficult for keyboard users to identify the current focus location. ## Expected Result Keyboard focus should move only to meaningful, interactive elements. When an element receives keyboard focus, a clearly visible focus indicator should be provided so users can determine where the focus is located. ## How to Fix The browser default focus indicator must not be removed without an appropriate replacement. Ensure every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator, which may be rendered using the or pseudo-classes. Providing an outline is the most robust and recognizable type of focus indicator. Other styles may be used instead, but they will need to be checked when High Contrast themes are applied. E.g., styles are not rendered when a user enables Windows High Contrast themes. An easy work around is to use a transparent outline along with your custom focus style. The custom style may not render in the High Contrast theme, but the transparent outline _will_ appear. ## Environment details Application Name: VS Code (1.38.0) Edition Windows 11 Enterprise Version 25H2 OS build 26200.8390 ## Note - Please do not close this bug. This bug should only be closed by TCS, C+AI Accessibility tester after bug verification. - "[Check out Accessibility Insights!]( - Identify accessibility bugs before check-in and make bug fixing faster and easier." ## Attachment

title: Agent host (Copilot): workspaceless chats drop the workspaceless instructions on resume, breaking the prompt cache between turns
text: Agent host (Copilot): workspaceless chats drop the workspaceless instructions on resume, breaking the prompt cache between turns. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host (Code OSS from source, at 58afa23a1cb) - VS Code Version: Code OSS dev build - OS Version: macOS - Feature: Agents window, workspaceless chat (no folder), Copilot provider - Selected model: Claude Sonnet 5.5; also seen with HydraFusion (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-6-luna) - Logs: per-request in the AHP transport log, and system prompts from the Copilot SDK In a workspaceless chat, the system prompt changes between turns 1 and 2, so turn 2 can't reuse turn 1's prompt cache. The block is present on turn 1 and missing after the SDK session resumes. This is a cost and latency problem. It also means the agent loses its scratch-directory guidance after the first resume. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. In the Agents window, start a new chat with no folder (default Chat mode). Send a short prompt and wait for the response. 2. Send a second prompt about a minute later. 3. Compare the two events in that session's , and the cache reads in for each turn's first model call. ## Measured Each chat was workspaceless the whole time, with no call. The Agent Host session database had . | Session | Turn 1 input | Turn 2 first call: cache read | |---|---|---| | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 26,823 | 14,643 (55%) | | HydraFusion, gpt-6-luna | 26,965 | 19,281 (72%) | | HydraFusion, gpt-5.6-sol | 16,532 | 8,560 (52%) | Later calls within the same turn read 93–99.7% from cache, so the miss happens only between turns. In all three sessions, the SDK session shut down and resumed between turns ( → ). The turn 1 system prompt contains ; the turn 2 system prompt doesn't. In the Claude session, that block (about 1,100 characters) was the only system-prompt difference, and the cache stopped matching there. In the Claude session, turn 2 read the same 14,643 tokens that turn 1 read on its first call. That's the prefix shared across sessions (see #339643), not the ~26.8k turn 1 sent. ## Cause ( ) builds the resume plan with . comes from , the Copilot SDK session's database. isn't stored there; it's stored on the Agent Host session ( ). So the resumed session gets , and skips . Evidence from one run: - Agent Host session database: - Copilot SDK session database: no key ## Expected A resumed workspaceless session keeps the block, so its system prompt doesn't change between turns and turn 2 reads turn 1's prompt from cache. ## Notes - This is separate from #339643, which covers a cache miss across sessions caused by the line. This one is a miss within one session caused by the prompt content changing, so the SDK bump for #339643 won't fix it. - Not measured: why the SDK session resumes between turns. One session logged just before its resume; another didn't. - Not measured: whether chats opened in a folder also miss the cache on resume.

title: NativeEditContext: Enter from a composing Android keyboard corrupts the new line
text: NativeEditContext: Enter from a composing Android keyboard corrupts the new line. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (vscode.dev, no extensions installed) - VS Code Version: vscode.dev 1.141.0 (2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c) and insiders.vscode.dev 1.142.0-insider (35c48f9946eecf40beed751940607f184a03b6de), same result on both - OS Version: Android 13 (API 33, arm64 emulator) - Browser: Chrome 154.0.8037.59 - Keyboard: Gboard 12.4.05, which composes: after a tap, the word under the caret is underlined - : default ( ) With a keyboard that composes the word at the caret, an Enter typed after a tap inside a word writes part of that word over other characters of the new line, and each Enter typed at column 1 makes the next Backspace do nothing. gives the EditContext only the caret's line and moves it to the new line when the keyboard's own Enter moves the caret, while the keyboard still acts on its own copy of the text: the old line with a line break at the caret. This is separate from #338890, which is in the same file. #242069 and #202787 report Backspace not removing empty lines in vscode.dev on Android, but both were filed while stable vscode.dev still used the textarea input (the EditContext default became for stable in 1.101.0) and neither has steps; this report is about the path, with steps on the current builds. Steps to Reproduce: Enter inside a word: 1. Open in Chrome on Android and run File > New Text File. 2. Type with the on-screen keyboard. 3. Reload the page; the untitled file is restored. This clears the copy of the line that #338890 leaves in the EditContext text, which would otherwise also be in what the keyboard reads. 4. Tap between and . Gboard underlines . 5. Tap Enter on the keyboard. Expected: and . Actual: and . Enter at column 1, then Backspace: 1. Run File > New Text File. 2. Tap Enter on the keyboard three times. The file has four lines. 3. Tap Backspace on the keyboard three times. Expected: one empty line. Actual: the file still has four lines. A fourth Backspace deletes one line break. With Gboard 18.4.1 on Android 16 (Chrome 154, same vscode.dev build), an Enter after a tap inside a word split the line correctly, and each Backspace after three Enters deleted a line break. Read over DevTools, shows what the keyboard is given. In the first sequence, before the Enter its text is with the selection at 8; after it, the text is the new line alone ( once the keyboard has written to it), with offsets starting again at the new line. The result is what a keyboard produces whose copy after its Enter is : there is at [9, 11), and in the new line [9, 11) is , the two characters that were replaced by . In the second sequence the text is with the selection at 0 before and after every Enter. ### Root cause gives the EditContext the text of the lines the primary selection is on, with offsets counted from column 1 of the first of them ([nativeEditContext.ts L479-L498]( When the keyboard's Enter moves the caret to the new line, the next replaces that text with the new line and the offsets start again at 0 ([L416-L431]( An Android keyboard keeps its own copy of the text and can act on it before it hears what an edit did. Gboard 12.4 sends Enter as a key press and at once recomposes the word after the caret at the offsets of its copy, which now point into a different line. In the Android app mentioned below, built on the same code, the events of an Enter typed after a tap in a word were , keydown 229 with an empty at the caret, a trusted keydown Enter and , and then, within about 1 ms, , a over a range shifted by the old caret offset plus one, and a second writing the word into that range. When the Enter leaves the text and the offsets unchanged, as at column 1 where the empty line before is the empty line after, sends neither nor , so the keyboard is never told anything moved. It keeps the line break it believes it typed before the caret and spends the next Backspace deleting it. In the same app (Code - OSS 1.139.1), those Backspaces arrived as keydown 229 with an empty over [0, 0), which changes nothing. A fix needs the EditContext text to stay where the keyboard expects it after the keyboard's own edits: - After an edit the keyboard made (its or its Enter), keep the window's start line, so that the text becomes with the caret at 9, which is what the keyboard assumes. - On every other caret change (a tap, a cursor key, a command, an undo) move the window to the caret's line as today; the keyboard is told about those and reads the text again. - Let a Backspace the keyboard sends for a line break before the caret join the lines. clamps at column 1 of the caret's line ([cursorTypeEditOperations.ts L815]( which turns that Backspace into nothing even when the window holds the line break. - Build the window with whatever the model's line ending, since the keyboard counts a line break as one character, and map the composition decorations and character bounds through the window's own start line rather than the selection's. Where text follows the caret, keeping the start is not enough on its own in indented code: the editor puts the indentation after the line break, so the keyboard's copy lacks it, and the recomposed range lands that many characters early. Starting the window at the caret's offset in the keyboard's copy, the event's own selection for a and one past the old caret for the Enter, covers that case. We found this while embedding the web workbench in an Android app (VSCodroid), where a change of this shape, applied on Android only as a source patch, is being tested; in those tests, Enter inside a word, before a word and at column 1 keep the text intact on Gboard 12.4, and the Backspaces after them join the lines again. The defect is in code that is not Android specific, but the keyboards that act on their own copy before the page answers have only been seen on Android.

title: Sessions: orphaned "Session" entries load, then disappear when opened
text: Sessions: orphaned "Session" entries load, then disappear when opened. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded - VS Code Version: Code - Insiders; exact build not recorded - OS Version: macOS; exact version not recorded - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Sessions list, local Copilot Agent Host - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not applicable to opening the existing entry - Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. Sanitized findings below; the raw bundle is not attached because it can contain sensitive content. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Find an existing entry titled "Session" in the sessions list. 2. Click the entry. It loads for about three seconds. 3. The entry disappears from the list instead of opening a conversation. I do not yet have reliable steps to create the orphaned entry. The observed entry was created the previous day, October 6, 2026, and appeared in the list before I clicked it. ### Expected An orphaned placeholder should not appear as an ordinary, openable session. If the host discovers that an already-visible entry cannot be opened, explain what happened rather than silently making it disappear. ### Observed log sequence October 7, 2026, local time, UTC-07:00: | Time | Event | | --- | --- | | 10:34:54.049 | The client subscribes to restore the selected session and its chat. | | 10:34:54.082 | Copilot reports with . | | 10:34:57.067 | Restore fails with , protocol error . | | 10:34:57.418 | The host sends for the selected entry. | | 10:34:57.552 | The renderer removes the entry. Five other entries disappear in the same batch. | The session was registered locally, but the host could not resolve its provider metadata. There is no client deletion request in the captured AHP traffic. ### Investigation The error matches the provisional-session check in [agentService.ts]( Once the provider catalogue becomes readable, can retract published entries that remain provisional and have no provider backing. in [agentHostStateManager.ts]( removes the list entry without deleting conversation files. This points to a stale placeholder being exposed before catalogue validation, then retracted after the user tries to open it. The logs do not establish why the backing was absent or whether the provisional classification was correct. They do not show conversation data being deleted by the click. Related: #321269 and #321469. No "Mark Done" action was observed as part of this reproduction. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: Copilot CLI shim recurses infinitely (fork bomb) when is a symlink
text: Copilot CLI shim recurses infinitely (fork bomb) when is a symlink. ## Summary On Linux systems where is a symlink (e.g. Fedora Atomic desktops: ), the Copilot CLI terminal shim ( + ) fails to remove its own directory from , so / resolve back to the shim itself. The shim then recurses forever: each level is a + an process that stays alive in , effectively a fork bomb. On my machine this created **~940 + ~920 processes** in about 8 minutes. The VS Code Flatpak scope peaked at **11 GB RAM + 7.2 GB swap**, filled all swap, froze the desktop, and the kernel OOM killer started killing unrelated apps (it killed Steam first, then VS Code). ## Environment - VS Code 1.139.1 (Flatpak , Electron 43.6.0), built-in Copilot Chat extension - Fedora 44 Atomic desktop, kernel 7.2.8, KDE Plasma (Wayland) - (default on Fedora Atomic / Silverblue / Kinoite and derivatives) - (both on the host and inside the Flatpak sandbox) ## Root cause strips its directory from with a plain string match against : - The directory is added to (via ) using , which is . - Node resolves symlinks for the main module, so is . - The strings don't match, the directory stays in , and / execute the shim again → infinite recursion. Minimal confirmation inside the Flatpak sandbox: This is not Flatpak-specific: any setup where the global storage path that is added to contains a symlink (symlinked , symlinked , bind/symlinked home directories, etc.) should hit it. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use a Linux system where is a symlink (e.g. Fedora Silverblue/Kinoite). 2. Open VS Code with Copilot Chat enabled so the shim is installed and its directory is contributed to the terminal . 3. Make sure no real binary appears earlier in . 4. Run (or ) in the integrated terminal. **Expected:** the shim finds no real CLI and offers to install it. **Actual:** unbounded process recursion until the system runs out of memory. ## Suggested fixes 1. Filter by resolved path instead of string equality, e.g. drop every entry where (ignoring entries that fail to resolve). 2. Add a recursion guard to the generated wrapper / shim (e.g. set an env var such as and bail out with an error if it's already set). This guarantees the shim can never fork-bomb, whatever the cause. 3. Optionally, have the wrapper itself remove its directory from before launching Node. ## Workaround I replaced the generated wrapper with one that strips any entry from and includes the recursion guard above, then made the file read-only. The extension rewrites and on every activation, so the fix doesn't survive otherwise.

title: Inline chat terminal stops updating for long-running background shells
text: Inline chat terminal stops updating for long-running background shells. In an Agent Host Copilot chat, the inline terminal in a shell tool card doesn't keep up with a long-running background shell's output: - Once the output passes 8 KiB, it stops updating or collapses to a 128-character fragment of the latest line, the same as the Background Shells preview (#340225), because both read the same Agent Host terminal. #340222 fixes that part for both surfaces. - With #340222, the inline terminal still falls behind. In a 2,000-line run it stopped updating at and didn't catch up after the shell exited. The window still received terminal data through and kept its terminal subscription until after the shell exited, so the output arrives but the tool card stops rendering it. - It stopped around the time the shell's Background Shells preview was closed. I haven't confirmed whether that's related. ### Repro steps 1. Save this as in a folder: 2. Open the folder in the Agents window and send this in a Copilot chat: 3. While it runs, watch the inline terminal in the tool card. Open and close the shell's **Background Shells** preview a few times. 4. When the command exits (about 5 minutes), check the inline terminal's last line. ### Expected The inline terminal keeps up with the output and ends at . ### Actual - Without #340222: it stops at , like the Background Shells preview. - With #340222: it stops partway through, at in my run.

title: Background Shells preview truncates long-running shell output
text: Background Shells preview truncates long-running shell output. In an Agent Host Copilot chat, the **Background Shells** preview doesn't show a long-running shell's output reliably: - Once the output passes 8 KiB, the preview stops updating or collapses to a 128-character fragment of the latest line. - When the preview resizes, it clips the middle of its last line instead of re-wrapping it. - While the preview is open, it keeps only rows (1,000 by default). Older lines drop off, and the view jumps while scrolled up. ### Repro steps 1. Save this as in a folder: 2. Open the folder in the Agents window and send this in a Copilot chat: 3. Open the **Background Shells** pill and hover over the shell to show its preview. Keep the pointer on it. ### Actual - The preview stops at , where the output passes 8 KiB, while the shell keeps printing until . - The last line is missing its middle: one row ends partway through the URL, such as , and the next row starts at . - Once every line streams, keep the preview open past and scroll up while output arrives. The view jumps, and the top is no longer . ### Expected The preview streams every line, shows its last line in full, and keeps all of the shell's retained output scrollable.

title: Automations: choosing a folder in the automation dialog's workspace picker doesn't add it to history
text: Automations: choosing a folder in the automation dialog's workspace picker doesn't add it to history. 🤖 AI Assisted Bug Report When creating or editing an automation, choosing a folder through the workspace picker in the automations dialog does not add that folder to the workspace history. title: Agent Host: first-turn materialization waits ~8.5s after SDK initialization
text: Agent Host: first-turn materialization waits ~8.5s after SDK initialization. <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates --> <!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue --> - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured for this report. Agent Host SDK: . - VS Code Version: , commit . - OS Version: Windows. Exact OS build not captured for this report. - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Copilot Agent Host, first turn of a new session. - Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Auto, resolved to . - Logs: Sanitized timing findings below from an Agent Host debug-log export. Raw customer logs are not attached publicly. Steps to Reproduce: 1. On Windows, create a new Copilot Agent Host session using a folder that is not a Git repository. 2. Submit a short prompt and capture Agent Host debug logs. Compare SDK initialization completion, host session materialization, and provider dispatch. These describe the observed scenario, not a reliable minimal reproduction. The affected Windows environment has not been reproduced locally. ## Observed delay The host recorded before the first provider dispatch. A separate followed it. This issue concerns the preparation delay, not subsequent model or tool latency. The October 6 capture contains these milestones, normalized to UTC: | Milestone | Timestamp | | --- | --- | | SDK wrapper attached | | | Server tools advertised | | | Host session materialized | | | Session ready notification | | | Provider called | | About **8.45 seconds pass after server-tool advertisement before materialization completes**. In the deployed implementation, advertisement is the final operation in , after its awaited setup. The relevant materialization and Git methods were checked against the exact deployed commit. Expected behavior: a new session should reach provider dispatch promptly once SDK initialization finishes. Project enrichment and persistence should not introduce an unexplained multi-second wait. ## Investigation The remaining awaited path in [ ]( is: 1. Await the Git-based project-discovery promise started alongside SDK launch. 2. Persist session metadata. 3. Read/write the deferred SDK execution marker. 4. Optionally persist selected-agent metadata, then finish materialization. Repeated failures report that the folder is not a repository. Across five first-session captures, materialization follows the immediately preceding failed probe by 224-276ms. [ ]( serializes same-directory lookups and caches only successful roots. Queued negative lookups each launch another Git process. A controlled experiment using the actual compiled service, with only its per-instance Git runner replaced by a 100ms probe, confirmed the mechanism: | Eight concurrent callers for one directory | Probe invocations | Maximum concurrent probes | Elapsed | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Non-repository result | 8 | 1 | 808ms | | Successful repository result | 1 | 1 | 102ms | Assertions passed. This verifies amplification of negative lookups, not its contribution to this customer incident. ## Attribution is not yet confirmed An independent adversarial review confirmed the late materialization wait, but did not establish that Git queueing caused it. The logs omit Git operation IDs, cwd correlation, enqueue times, and execution durations. The failed probes cannot be placed ahead of this session's project lookup in the queue. Metadata writes also run through database sequencers, so persistence queueing/I/O remains a competing explanation. SDK setup and the identified client resource callbacks do not account for the interval; those callbacks completed in 33-36ms. ## Next diagnostic step Instrument one reproduction on the affected Windows host: - Record initialization completion, project-promise settlement, project-await resumption, and start/end of each persistence await. - Link the materialization project lookup to a Git operation ID. Record an opaque directory key, enqueue time, queue-entry time, subprocess completion, and result category. This will distinguish redundant Git queue wait from slow Git execution or persistence. Avoid logging prompts, raw paths, credentials, or customer content. Related: #333284 covers session-listing starvation and repeated Git probes. This report isolates the remaining first-turn materialization delay after SDK initialization. _🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

title: Agent Host BYOK bridge drops provider configurationSchema and statusIcon from the model picker
text: Agent Host BYOK bridge drops provider configurationSchema and statusIcon from the model picker. **Title:** Agent Host BYOK bridge replaces extension-published model metadata, so provider submenus and status icons silently disappear from the model picker **Labels:** , , , --- ## Summary When an extension provides with a (and / / / / ), the model picker renders those correctly in a Local/ chat. As soon as the composer is bound to an Agent Host harness (here: ), the picker renders the Agent Host's *bridged* copy of the same model instead, and that copy is built only from / / . Every provider-supplied UI field is dropped — most visibly the nested submenus ("Model Mode", "Output Length") and the . The confusing part for users: there is no duplicate row. The host copy is given , so it renders *inside our own provider's group* and silently replaces our fully-described entry with a degraded one. ## Environment - VS Code **1.140.0** (system build, commit , x64) - Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26300 - Affected extension: (published as ) **1.37.0**, with and - Reproduced in a **normal Chat (chat prompt) window**, not the Agents window. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install an extension that registers a and returns including (nested properties), , , . 2. Enable Agent Host BYOK models ( ). 3. Open a normal chat editor and send one message to the provider's model in a **new** chat → the picker shows the provider's icon and the submenus. 4. Reload the window / reopen that conversation. - **Expected:** picker keeps icon + submenus. - **Actual:** the icon is gone and the submenus are gone; the model still runs and its configured values are still applied. ## Evidence log for the affected window — the composer starts in a good state and is *moved* onto the host by conversation restore: Trace-level dumps in the same window, same moment — the provider's own entry is complete (redacted, field names verbatim from the log): The Agent Host's resolve (same window) contains our models under a namespaced identifier, missing exactly those fields — note , present only as a warning conditional, set to our vendor, token budgets and capabilities carried over, and no / / / / : Host-native models in the same dump *do* get a schema (so the picker path works in general) — only knows six hardcoded keys: ## Cause → builds every BYOK row from scratch, so a model that has no native ends up with no at all, and no icon/tooltip/detail/banner/price: The picker only builds submenus from that field ( → → , which returns unless exists), and the provider's stored configuration is merged back separately — which is why the **Model Settings panel still shows and applies Model Mode / Output Length while the picker cannot show them**. That makes the bug look like a provider bug to users: their settings work, but the UI to change them is gone. Also note the mapping gap even if the schema were forwarded: whitelists only and , and its own comment warns that an ungrouped property makes the picker hide itself entirely. Provider-defined keys (e.g. ) map to . ## Expected Metadata for a BYOK model that also comes from a local extension should be enriched from the extension-published entry — e.g. when , take / / / / / / from (the same fallback style already uses for limits and billing). At minimum, a provider should not be silently discarded just because the model is reachable through the host. ## Proposal 1. In , when a is available, fall back to the locally-published for , , / , / and price. 2. For , either pass the provider schema through as-is or preserve when it is already one of the picker's group ids, so non-hardcoded provider keys still render. ( only requires and a non-empty .) 3. If the intent is that BYOK models deliberately get no provider UI, then the picker should not pretend otherwise: the degraded host row should not claim our while dropping our UI. ## Not a problem for you No protocol change needed — the host already knows the BYOK identifier and already performs this kind of fallback for billing and limits. This is an enrichment gap in the editor-side provider. ## Related (open, same area) - [Bug] Some BYOK models report zero context limits (input and output) when selected in the model picker #338099 - Agent Host models should not be registered in global / regular LanguageModelsService #333802 - [Bug] Copilot BYOK: user-configured max output tokens ignored — requests over max context fail with 400 #339509 - [Tracking] Agent Host BYOK models #339761 Provider side for reference: vLLM-Copilot ( , , , ) and ( ).

Use the affected Insiders build with Copilot and multiple workbench/Agents windows. 2. Inspect the Copilot Chat output for dense batches of requests and HTTP 429 results. 3. Correlate the requests with the language-model API's calling extension/feature before attributing the burst to Agent Host or a particular consumer. ### Observed frequency A timestamp-filtered local audit covered 4 October 2026 13:14 through 6 October 2026 13:14 CEST (UTC+02): - 3,243 records, paired with 3,243 request summaries for . - 3,550 successful summaries for the same model, plus two cancellations. - Peak: 141 rate-limited results logged during the single second 5 October 11:22:18 CEST. This is a count of logged completions, not a measurement of dispatch rate. - 2,994 rate-limited summaries on 5 October and 249 on 6 October; failures persist after the 6 October 11:43 update/restart. Example: Three adjacent summaries from the peak second: ### Impact and uncertainty The observed consumer is repeatedly doing failed model work. title: Remote agent host: large chat history exceeds tunnel gateway frame limit and causes terminal timeout
text: Remote agent host: large chat history exceeds tunnel gateway frame limit and causes terminal timeout. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: --> <!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: --> <!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. --> <!-- 🔧 Launch with to check. --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. <!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. --> <!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> - VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider on the host, commit , built October 5, 2026. The client was also running the latest October 5 desktop Insiders. - OS Version: macOS 27.0 on the host; client OS not captured. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Make an existing agent host available through a remote tunnel and connect to it from desktop Insiders on another device. 2. Open a long-running Copilot CLI session whose main chat history is larger than 16 MiB when serialized. The affected session was . 3. Observe that loading the session interrupts the connection and the terminal reports a launch failure after approximately 25 seconds. Reconnecting and opening the same chat repeats the problem. Some other sessions on the same host open successfully. ### What I ran into : opening this session from my other device consistently produces: The tunnel ID is redacted. This looks like a terminal problem, but the failure starts while loading the main chat, before the terminal gets a launch response. **In simple terms:** opening the session sends its whole conversation history through a gateway. This session's history is about 17.9 MiB, but the gateway only accepts individual WebSocket frames up to 16 MiB. It rejects the history and stops forwarding. The terminal uses the same connection, so it reports the connection timeout rather than a shell error. ### Matching client and host evidence The attempt matching the exact error follows this sequence. Times below are October 6, 2026, in UTC+2: | Time | Event | |---|---| | 00:00:43.762 | Client requests the session's main/default chat. | | 00:00:43.944 | Host AHP trace records the chat subscription response: **18,774,427 bytes**, containing **52 turns**. | | 00:00:44 | CLI gateway logs a frame-size rejection for that exact byte count. | | 00:00:44.108 | Last incoming protocol message recorded by the client. | | 00:00:44.130 | Client requests a terminal in the session's working directory. | | 00:00:49.108 | Client sends a heartbeat ping. | | 00:01:09.112 | Client forcibly closes the connection after 25 seconds without incoming data. | | 00:01:15.289 | Client reports successful reconnection, but loading the same chat again hits the same gateway limit. | The main chat subscription, terminal creation, and ping receive no response on the client. There is no remote shell-launch response identifying a bad executable or working directory. The decisive entries are in the host's CLI gateway log, . These timestamps are UTC, two hours behind the table: The host-side AHP trace identifies the first response as this session's default chat snapshot, with and . The host logs contain **20 gateway rejections of that exact payload size**. ### Causes - **Mismatched transport limits.** The gateway's [TCP and socket target connections]( use Tungstenite's default configuration. Its [default maximum frame size is 16 MiB]( while the [client tunnel implementation allows 100 MiB]( The default message limit and frame limit are different; this rejection is specifically the **frame** limit. - **A large history is sent in one message/frame.** The snapshot contains thousands of tool calls and their results across 52 turns. It exceeds the gateway limit even though smaller sessions work. - **The useful failure reason does not reach the UI.** On this error, [the gateway proxy logs and returns]( The client ultimately surfaces a generic connection timeout through the terminal, hiding the history-size rejection. ### Potential fixes 1. **Align bounded WebSocket frame and message limits across the gateway and client.** Configure both target-dial paths and the client-facing gateway socket explicitly, rather than relying on library defaults. A consistent limit such as the existing 100 MiB client limit could address this case without removing limits entirely. 2. **Propagate gateway failures promptly and clearly.** Close/notify the other side when forwarding fails, and preserve a useful cause such as "session history exceeds the connection limit," rather than waiting for the heartbeat timeout and showing a terminal-launch error. 3. **Longer term, avoid sending the entire history in one oversized frame.** Consider frame fragmentation or protocol-level chunking/pagination for chat restoration. A regression test should pass a single chat-sized frame above 16 MiB through the actual gateway, covering both TCP and socket targets, and verify that configured-limit failures are surfaced rather than leaving the client waiting. Increasing the heartbeat timeout alone would not fix this: the gateway rejects the frame immediately.

title: Connected tabs: customized active background exposes shoulder join artifacts
text: Connected tabs: customized active background exposes shoulder join artifacts. <!-- bug_report_template --> ## Problem Connected tabs show awkward joins at both bottom shoulders when the active tab's customized background differs from the editor background. The joins stand out in regular dark themes and in high contrast. In HC, the active tab's inset multi-selection outline adds a horizontal bottom stroke that makes the connection look closed. Expected: customized tab backgrounds should retain clean shoulder/separator joins. Selection indicators must remain distinguishable without relying only on color. ## Reproduction Observed in the local macOS Component Explorer using the production editor-tab control. A native Code OSS reproduction should be verified separately. 1. Open in Component Explorer. 2. The active tab has a teal ; the editor keeps its default dark background. is also selected. 3. Move the pointer away from the tabs and inspect the left and right bottom shoulders of . 4. Repeat with . For native verification, enable Modern UI with Connected tabs, open three files, select the first two with the middle file active, and customize: The attached screenshot shows both themes at rest. Red arrows identify the shoulder joins. ## Investigation context - Shoulder and edge-mask paint uses the active tab background, while the editor body uses a different surface color. - A controlled stylesheet-level comparison using the same scene showed the underlying issue before #339028 and #338796. #339028 changed the shoulder radius/mask dimensions, so the exact appearance changed. - This comparison did not rebuild historical binaries; it is evidence of pre-existing styling behavior, not a definitive native regression bisect. - The custom-color scene was added by #338796. This is deferred work discovered while validating #339957, not part of that close-button fix. - Related but not established as duplicates: #339749 (border colors mixing), #338446 (HC clipped/missing borders), and #326833 (non-color selection indication). ## Follow-up Investigate custom-background shoulder paint and the HC multi-selection outline together. Preserve default connected geometry, clean joins in focused/unfocused groups, and accessible non-color selection indicators. ![Dark and Dark High Contrast customized tabs, with red arrows marking both bottom shoulder joins](

title: Align Connected and Pill tab visual heights within each density
text: Align Connected and Pill tab visual heights within each density. ## Investigation Connected and Pill editor tabs have visibly different painted heights at the same density. Determine whether this is part of the original Connected-tab design or an unintended divergence before changing geometry. ## Reproduction and measurements 1. In Component Explorer, compare and . 2. Keep default layout density and editor tab height in both scenes. 3. Compare their painted tab fills, not just the tab-row hitboxes. Current local browser measurements: | Style | Tab hitbox | Active fill | Inactive fill | |-----------|------------|-------------|---------------| | Connected | 32px | 34px | 33px | | Pill | 32px | 24px | 24px | The screenshot compares the two scenes without hover. This is headless component-fixture evidence, not a native Code OSS capture. ## Design/history question **Investigate whether the taller Connected fill was intentional from the very first Connected-tab design, including the early commits by Lee Murray ( ).** - Trace the original introduction of Connected tabs, its design rationale, and changes to the vertical gutters, tab borders, separator slot, and active-fill extension. - The inspected height rules already existed before #339028 and #338796. This is not established as a regression introduced by either merged PR. - Extending the active fill over the separator explains part of the geometry, but does not by itself establish that the overall visual-height difference was intentional. - Compare default and compact densities, single and wrapped rows, and both regular and HC themes. - Verify in native Code OSS before deciding on a design change. Expected outcome: document the original intent. If the difference is unintended, align the visual height while preserving the active tab's connection, consistent Close/Unpin geometry, and stable row layout. Related: #336320 (broader Connected design feedback), #337502 (compact layout concerns), and #337446 (corner/spacing inconsistency, closed by #339028). This tracks the specific cross-style height/design question separately. Parked during #339957 validation; it is outside the HC Close-visibility fix. ![Connected and Pill tabs at the same default density, with measured hitbox and visual fill heights](
