title: Agents Window: support Compare Agents in local and empty Git repositories
text: Agents Window: support Compare Agents in local and empty Git repositories. ## Current limitation Compare Agents currently requires both a Git remote and at least one commit before comparison setup is available. Neither restriction reflects the actual isolation requirements: committed local branches can already create worktrees without a remote, while an unborn repository can be isolated by snapshotting its current non-ignored files into an internal base commit before creating each attempt worktree. This blocks local-only projects and newly initialized projects from using Compare Agents even though they can run safely in independent worktrees. ## Requested behavior - Offer Compare Agents for a local Git repository without a remote. - Offer Compare Agents for an unborn repository with no commits. - Preserve independent worktree isolation for every attempt, Judge, and Synthesizer session. - For an unborn repository, snapshot the current tracked, staged, modified, and non-ignored untracked files without changing the user index or creating a commit on the source branch. - Start each isolated branch from that snapshot so the worktree is populated and clean and comparison diffs include only agent changes. - Continue honoring the existing ignored-file copy and symlink configuration. - Keep existing committed local and remote repository behavior unchanged. ## Validation Cover no-remote eligibility, unborn-branch worktree selection, and a real-Git end-to-end flow proving the source branch remains unborn while the isolated worktree is populated and clean.

title: Improve GPT Live Voice Mode startup latency
text: Improve GPT Live Voice Mode startup latency. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> ## Feature Request Improve initial Voice Mode startup when using an OpenAI GPT Live model, and reuse safe setup work across repeated starts. ## Motivation reported that GPT Live Voice Mode took approximately **9 seconds end-to-end** to start before the improvement. This is a rough user-observed baseline, not an instrumented benchmark. Startup currently repeats OpenAI model discovery during availability checking and session creation, with an additional model-availability request in between. These serial network requests delay microphone acquisition and connection setup. ## Requested Behavior - Reduce redundant model-discovery and availability requests during startup. - Briefly cache successful discovery/availability results in memory, scoped to the current API key and voice model. - Preserve fresh credential and BYOK policy checks, cancellation, explicit refreshes, cache expiry, and failure retries. - Do not persist credentials or model caches to disk, keep the microphone open between sessions, or reuse live sessions. ## Implementation and Validation Addressed by #343553, which adds one-minute caches for silent OpenAI model discovery and successful GPT Live availability checks. A separate, small instrumented macOS sample measured click-to-WebRTC-connected repeated-start medians of **4.009 seconds before** and **2.297 seconds after**. Those measurements use a narrower timing definition and do not replace the approximately 9-second user-observed end-to-end baseline.

title: Support localized approvals in GPT Live Voice Mode
text: Support localized approvals in GPT Live Voice Mode. ## Feature request Support explicit spoken approval and rejection phrases in all 25 speech-recognition languages supported by Voice Mode, including languages selected through Automatic mode. Currently, GPT Live's client-side approval routing is English-only. For example, with set to , saying “verwerfen” does not resolve the pending confirmation even if the voice agent says it rejected the action. See #342526. ## Proposed behavior - Recognize complete, deterministic approval/rejection phrases in the selected voice language, retaining English commands as a fallback. - Cover Arabic, Czech, Danish, German, English, Spanish, Finnish, French, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian Bokmål, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese, and Chinese, including simplified/traditional Chinese variants. - Do not infer consent from substrings, qualified answers, negations, or ambiguous replies; prompt for an explicit reply or manual interaction instead. - Preserve pending-confirmation identity checks, stale-response rejection, duplicate protection, and acknowledgement only after the client reports success. - Read pending prompts and provide appropriate response guidance. For question forms, invite a voice reply or use of the controls in chat rather than requiring English, including for follow-up questions. - Apply voice-language changes immediately without reconnecting. This should not require an additional language-model request to classify a confirmation reply. ## Question reply language When the agent supplies a question and choices in the user's language, the user can answer by voice in that language using an exact displayed choice label, a choice number, or free text where the question permits it. For example, a German question with “Westen” and “Osten” accepts “Osten”; a following text question accepts “Meine Bereitstellung.” English replies remain available, but are not required. This is not unrestricted multilingual natural-language parsing. Shorthand commands such as “skip,” “other,” and “second,” and the multi-choice conjunction “and,” remain English-only. Localized paraphrases or ordinal words are outside this change. The question text and choices come from the chat agent. Changing the VS Code locale or does not itself translate that content; localized replies work when the supplied choices are localized, and free-text answers preserve the user's language. Implementation: #343301.

title: Support standalone managed Code OSS launches
text: Support standalone managed Code OSS launches. ## Problem Development tools and tests need to launch Code OSS from a source checkout, wait until the window is ready for automation, and stop that specific instance afterward. The existing launch skill already handles isolated profiles, authentication seeding, and debug ports for agent-driven development. A repository-level launch command would let terminal users, tasks, tests, and the skill reuse the same implementation. ## Proposed behavior Provide a Node.js command that: - Launches a selected checkout with isolated user-data, extensions, and shared-data directories, optionally seeded from an existing local profile. - Emits one JSON readiness record with the application PID, debug ports, run directory, and log path once the browser debugging endpoint responds. - Offers to remain alive until the application exits and return its exit code. - Forwards application arguments and keeps diagnostics separate from machine-readable output. - Cleans up only the selected run, preserving other development windows and the source profile. Cover readiness, lifetime, profile isolation, and exact-run cleanup with automated tests. Implementation: Parent tracking issue: ## Follow-up after merge Create a separate tracking issue to migrate the launch skill to this command while retaining its build/sign-in, UI automation, and debugger guidance. Verify option/output compatibility, profile/authentication behavior, and cleanup across Windows, macOS, and Linux before removing the duplicated implementation.

title: Agents Window: support Compare Agents in Dev Containers
text: Agents Window: support Compare Agents in Dev Containers. Follow-up to #342686. ## Current limitation Compare Agents must not be offered when Dev Container execution is selected. Normal composer drafts explicitly require container execution, but comparison creates fresh sessions without carrying that requirement. Hiding the comparison controls and rejecting stale comparison sends is the intentional interim behavior; a normal single-agent request remains available. The comparison launch architecture may change soon, so defer full container integration rather than expanding that path in the Environment picker PR. ## Follow-up scope - Carry explicit container execution intent through the comparison lifecycle and persisted state, including attempts, Judge/retries, and synthesis. - Reuse the existing experimental container-worktree path ( ) where supported; preserve independent worktree isolation and never fall back to source-host or shared-folder execution. - Preserve comparison attribution, participant identity/grouping, models, and permissions across the source-to-container session handoff. Validate access to attempt evidence from the Judge. - Cover unsupported capabilities, partial launch failures, cancellation, reload/retry, and container/worktree cleanup. - Restore comparison availability only for supported combinations; Dev Container samples currently do not support the worktree combination. ## Expected interim UX Selecting Dev Container removes comparison setup and clears an existing comparison selection once configuration settles. Returning to a compatible non-container destination restores comparison availability under its existing gates. Stale comparison sends report an explicit error instead of launching on the host.

title: Launch skill: fast, robust TypeScript launcher for Code OSS
text: Launch skill: fast, robust TypeScript launcher for Code OSS. The repo's agent skill ( ) starts isolated, debuggable Code OSS instances for agents. Today it is slow and fragile: - Launch logic is duplicated between and , with two different profile exclude rules. - On Windows a launch takes ~10s or more (eager scanning, robocopy of the whole profile, pre-launch run serially). - Arguments are passed through ( ), so paths or titles with or break. - A PowerShell caller that captures the output hangs until Code OSS exits, because Electron inherits the capture pipe. - Run directories can collide, are never garbage collected, and cleanup matches processes by command line (8-14s). ## Expected - One TypeScript launcher core with thin PowerShell/bash wrappers. - Fast launches (~1-2s until CDP is ready), incremental profile copies, optional run-directory reuse. - Robust argument passing, no hang when capturing output, unique run directories with automatic cleanup, and a cross-platform cleanup that stops the recorded process tree.

title: Unify model configuration across chat, subagents, utility flows, and image/speech models
text: Unify model configuration across chat, subagents, utility flows, and image/speech models. ## Problem Model selection is configured through a growing set of independent, flat settings. Each has its own ID format, its own meaning for "empty", and its own picker UX. Three recent developments make this worse: 1. **The runtime prompt advertises , which VS Code doesn't expose.** In the Copilot runtime's tool schema, the , , and descriptions all say: *"The runtime resolves preferences when these fields are omitted; do not copy them merely because they appear in ."* is a CLI command, and VS Code intentionally hides it (it is in in ). So the model is told about a preference surface that VS Code users can't reach, while VS Code has its own unrelated per-subagent settings (below). The same schema also injects a flat enum containing every available model (22 in the e2e snapshots, and 50+ in a real session with BYOK and OpenRouter models), plus prose lists of which models support each reasoning effort and long context. 2. **Many settings use very long flat lists.** Several settings build a dynamic enum of every user-selectable chat model ( ). With BYOK, OpenRouter, and on-device models, each of these becomes a long, flat, unsearchable dropdown (#317420). The Settings editor repeats it once per setting, and each copy has to be repopulated whenever models change. Other settings are free-form strings with no discovery or validation (#319191). 3. **Non-chat models are arriving.** Image generation is a boolean ( ) with the model hard-coded to GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, so users can't choose an image model. Speech, voice, embeddings, completions, NES, and on-device models each have separate settings too. is centered on chat models, and nothing shared describes "the model for capability X". We need one unified way to configure all of these. ## Inventory of current cases ### Main conversation | Setting | Owner | Shape | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | | workbench | free string ( , family alias such as , or full id) | Policy-backed ( , managed / ) | | | workbench | dynamic enum of all tool-calling models | format | | Per-session model picker | workbench | state, not a setting | | ### Agents and subagents | Setting / surface | Owner | Shape | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | | workbench | dynamic enum | format | | | workbench | dynamic enum | format | | | Copilot extension | free string | Duplicates the workbench setting above | | | Copilot extension | free string | | | | Copilot extension | free string | | | | Copilot extension | free string | Extension harness | | | agent host | free string (CAPI model id) | Agent host harness; restarts the SDK client | | | Copilot extension | free string, default | Description and defaults are inconsistent (#341517) | | | agent host | free string (runtime model id), default | Empty means "inherit parent"; restarts the runtime | | frontmatter | prompt files | | Doesn't map to tool ids (#340844) | | tool / / | Copilot runtime | chosen by the model; flat enum | Points to and | | CLI preferences | Copilot runtime | CLI config | Not reachable from VS Code | ### Utility and background flows | Setting | Shape | Notes | |---|---|---| | | dynamic enum | format | | | dynamic enum | format; synced to the agent host | | | enum / / | Only applies when the main model is BYOK | | | free string, default | | | | fixed enum ( , , ) | | | Commit message generation | n/a | Requested in #328619 | ### Auto, routing, and per-model behavior | Setting | Shape | |---|---| | | string / null | | , , , | booleans / variants | | and | per-model object maps, duplicated across harnesses | ### On-device and BYOK | Setting | Shape | |---|---| | , , | boolean / boolean / path | | | boolean | ### Non-chat modalities | Capability | Setting | Shape | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Image generation and editing | | boolean | Model hard-coded to GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; pricing lives in the description | | Dictation (speech to text) | | fixed enum (on-device Nemotron / MAI cloud) | Policy-backed | | Voice Mode (realtime) | | free string (OpenAI live model id) | | | Code completions | | free string, set through a command | | | Next edit suggestions | , | string / object | | | Embeddings | | free string | | | Instant apply | | free string | | ### Other places models are chosen | Surface | Shape | Notes | |---|---|---| | | string or ordered list | The first available model wins | | and | string or ordered list / enum | only applies in the Copilot harness | | (per profile) | JSON file | BYOK providers and per-model configuration ( ), kept outside | | Model picker visibility (hide/show models) | profile storage | Not a setting, so users can't edit it directly and admins can't manage it | | Agents window **Compare Models** | attempts, judge, synthesizer | Three more role-like model choices | | Codex harness | session config | Harness-specific effort control | | Agent handoffs in | string | Uses the format, for example , so it has the same ID mismatch as #340844 | | MCP server sampling: → | list for each server | Chosen through a separate quick pick | | Completions status-bar picker ("Change Completions Model...") | Copilot extension UI | A separate picker that writes | ## Inconsistencies - **ID formats.** Settings use qualified names (plan, explore, inline chat, ), (utility models), CAPI ids (search subagent), runtime ids (execution subagent, tool), family aliases ( ), and for BYOK models in the tool enum. #340844 is a direct result of this. - **BYOK model identity.** Model IDs are , and for custom endpoints the is also the model name sent to the endpoint, with per-model settings keyed by it. Renaming a group changes the IDs of all its models and breaks anything that references them, and one group can't contain two entries for the same upstream model. The format used by the utility settings drops the group, so models that share a vendor and ID across groups are dropped from those pickers (related: #325069). - **Harness scoping.** The standalone model management editor filters models by harness ( ), but the Models section in Chat Customizations doesn't, so it shows every harness's models. As far as the code shows, only the Copilot harness can use BYOK models in the agent host, but the catalog lists them under every harness without saying so. - **No model limits for subagents.** The only controls are hiding a model everywhere and org policy. The tool lists Copilot and BYOK models together, so a BYOK user can't keep subagents on their own models. - **Empty values mean different things.** Depending on the setting, an empty value means "Auto (Vendor Default)", "runtime default", "inherit the parent session model", "use configured default behavior", or "use the hosted model". - **Picker UX.** Settings use dynamic enums (unsearchable, repeated per setting, rebuilt on model changes), free-form strings (no discovery or validation), or fixed enums. - **Duplication across harnesses.** The same concept has both a setting and a / setting with different semantics. Examples include the explore, search, and execution subagent models and the capability overrides (#341517). - **Apply semantics.** Some settings apply immediately. Others restart the SDK client or runtime after active turns finish. - **Policy.** Only and can be managed by policy. - **Prompt cost.** The full model list, plus per-model reasoning-effort and long-context lists, is injected into every tool schema. ## Proposal (strawman) - **Capability-aware model registry.** Describe models by capability (chat, image generation and editing, speech to text, realtime voice, embeddings, completions), so that image and other non-chat models can be listed, gated, priced, and picked like chat models. - **One home for each model choice.** Choices made while chatting stay in the input's model picker (chat, inline chat), with one order for which model a new conversation starts with. Agent models belong to the agent: built-in and custom agents, including subagents, get a model in the Agents list. Everything with no picker at the point of use (utility, image, dictation, voice, embeddings, completions) goes on one Feature models page. Use explicit / "same as conversation" / inherit values instead of empty strings, and allow optional reasoning effort and context tier. See the proposal comment below. - **One canonical model reference format.** Accept it in settings, frontmatter, the tool, and policy. Normalize the legacy formats on read. - **One searchable picker.** Group models by vendor and capability, and show pricing in AI credits. Use the same picker in the Settings editor, Models management, and the chat model picker, instead of injecting dynamic enums into the settings schema. - **Bridge to runtime subagent preferences.** Feed VS Code role assignments into the runtime's subagent preferences so that reflects what the user configured in VS Code. Otherwise, stop advertising in VS Code sessions. Also consider trimming the flat enum from the tool schema. - **Policy.** Expose role assignments through managed settings so admins can control more than the default model, including image models. - **Migration.** Deprecate the per-feature settings, migrate their values, and remove the duplicates between and . ## Resolution order The runtime already reports where a subagent's model came from ( : , , , ). However, the order isn't documented, and users can't see which source won. A unified design should define one order across all roles, for example: an explicit request in the current turn, then the custom agent definition, then the role assignment, then inheriting the parent model, then . The UI (subagent pill, debug view) should show the resolved model and where it came from. ## When the configured model is unavailable Behavior differs by surface: - : an unavailable model makes the search tool unavailable. - : an unavailable model disables the runtime execution subagent. - / : the file can list models in order, and the first available one is used. - : a family alias resolves to the latest available model in that family. We should pick one behavior (for example, an ordered fallback list plus a visible notice) and apply it to every role. ## Experiments, sync, and scope - Many of these settings are experiment-controlled ( ), and some track whether the value is still controlled by its default ( ). A unified setting must tell experiment-provided defaults apart from explicit user choices. #341517 shows the reset / "modified" confusion this causes today. - Settings Sync can carry a model ID to another machine, account, or org where that model isn't available or is blocked by policy. - Scopes are inconsistent: some of these settings are , some , some , and some use the default window scope. We need to decide whether workspace-level overrides are allowed. Repos can already pin models through . ## Extension API The , , , and APIs are proposed, but there is nothing for image models. Models that extensions contribute, of any modality, should be able to appear in the same registry and be assigned to roles. ## Cost visibility Pricing is no longer one number. Each model has AI credit rates per 1M tokens for input, cached input, cache writes, and output, sometimes with separate long-context rates, and image models add separate image-token rates. Today, image generation pricing appears only in the setting's description, and subagent and utility model choices don't show pricing at all, so picking a more expensive subagent model silently increases cost. Every role should show a relative price indicator ( ), with the full AI credit breakdown on hover or in the picker's details. ## Requirements - Hide the unified surface when AI features are disabled ( / ). - Make the picker keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible: searchable, grouped, and with proper ARIA labels. - Allow admins to manage role assignments, including restricting or disabling image generation. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Every model choice in the inventory has exactly one home: the picker, the agent, or Feature defaults in the Models section. - [ ] Settings, prompt and agent files, the tool, and policy all accept one model reference format, and legacy formats are migrated. - [ ] Image models and other non-chat models can be selected, with their AI credit pricing shown. - [ ] The resolution order and unavailable-model behavior are documented, and each subagent shows its resolved model and where it came from. - [ ] The runtime prompt only references preferences that VS Code users can actually set. - [ ] Model references stay valid when a BYOK group is renamed, and two groups can serve the same upstream model. - [ ] Users and admins can limit which models subagents may use. - [ ] The per-feature settings are deprecated, with automatic migration. ## Open questions - Where does the unified configuration live: , , or a dedicated Models editor backed by one of them? - The proposal makes agent models per harness and feature defaults shared across harnesses. Should any feature default be harness-specific? - How do plugin-contributed model providers identify their groups, and which harnesses can use them? - Are reasoning effort and context tier part of the role assignment, or per-model settings (as in )? - Are workspace-level role overrides allowed? - How do org policies restrict which models are available for each role? ## Related #319191, #317420, #341517, #340844, #328619, #325069

title: Show available link handlers in a Quick Pick
text: Show available link handlers in a Quick Pick. ## Feature request Provide a Quick Pick listing the available handlers for a link so users can choose which view opens its target. ## Expected behavior - Show distinguishable handler names and identify the current/default handler where known. - Open the target using the selected handler. - Allow reopening the current target with another matching handler without reconstructing the link, preserving navigation context and placement where supported. - Preserve the original target and opening intent (including opening to the side) when delegating to the selected handler. - Cancelling leaves the current view unchanged. - Ordinary link clicks should not require a picker every time. Parent story: #342050. ## UX ideas to explore These are alternatives to evaluate, not finalized interaction requirements: - After opening a link, show a status bar action for approximately 20 seconds that lets the user change the handler used for that target. Use a slow fadeout rather than an abrupt disappearance. - And/or let Ctrl+Alt+click or Ctrl+Alt+Enter open the handler Quick Pick directly, so the user can choose a handler before opening the target. - Check platform conventions, existing keybinding conflicts, and accessibility (including reduced-motion behavior and a keyboard-accessible alternative to the transient action) before finalizing the gestures and fadeout. Changing the handler for the current target is distinct from changing the default handler for future links; do not implicitly change the default.

title: Support link hovers in the Markdown editor and chat
text: Support link hovers in the Markdown editor and chat. Add consistent hover support for links in the Markdown editor and chat. Hovering a link should reveal its target and applicable navigation gestures (including opening to the side), and support richer target-specific information where available. Keep hover information consistent with the target and navigation behavior, without changing ordinary-click behavior. ## Acceptance criteria - Rendered links expose their target on hover. - Hovers make applicable opening gestures discoverable. - Target-specific hover information can be surfaced where supported. - The hover remains usable when moving the pointer into it. Parent story: #342050. Related: - #335448: Rich GitHub issue previews. - #265995: Link targets on hover in Markdown Preview.

title: Reconnect only the newest tool call for each shell ID when restoring detached shells in Agent Host chats
text: Reconnect only the newest tool call for each shell ID when restoring detached shells in Agent Host chats. Follow-up to streams a detached background shell's output into the tool call that started it, starting when that call completes. has no other caller ([code]( so after the Agent Host or its Copilot client restarts, nothing reads a still-running detached shell's output again. Restoring that needs to reconnect each restored shell to its tool call, and the shell ID alone doesn't say which one. **A chat can contain several shell tool calls with the same shell ID** - After the Copilot client restarts, shell IDs can start again at , so a new command can get the ID of an earlier tool call in the same chat. **Reconnecting an older tool call settles the running shell's terminal** - treats a reused shell ID as meaning the command that held it has finished, and settles that call's terminal ([code]( - A settled terminal ignores new output: returns early once the stream is finalized ([code]( - So reconnecting tool calls in chat order can settle the terminal of the shell that's actually running, and its output stops appearing. Found while prototyping restore for Possible fix: - [ ] When restoring, reconnect each running shell from only to the newest tool call with its shell ID, and leave older calls with that ID settled, with a test that has two tool calls for shell across a restart.

title: Allow disabling Copilot's Co-authored-by trailer in agent-host sessions
text: Allow disabling Copilot's Co-authored-by trailer in agent-host sessions. ## Feature Request Provide a setting to disable the trailer for commits made by Copilot sessions running in the agent host, including the Agents window. Currently, the Copilot runtime instructs these sessions to add the trailer by default. Neither (which controls commits through the Git UI) nor the CLI app setting controls SDK-hosted agent-host sessions, so users must ask the agent to omit the trailer in each session. Add , defaulting to to preserve existing behavior, and apply it when Copilot sessions are created or resumed. Setting it to should disable the runtime’s co-author instruction. Existing open chats and other providers are outside the scope of this change. Sub-agent inheritance depends on the upstream runtime fix in github/copilot-cli#4576. Fixed by #339437. Related: #314311.

title: Open path-hinted Git commit links in multi-diff with rich metadata
text: Open path-hinted Git commit links in multi-diff with rich metadata. ## Feature Make rich Git commit links show useful commit metadata and open the commit's changed files in the native multi-diff editor. ## Expected behavior - Display the commit subject and addition/deletion counts rather than a redundant authored label. - Resolve a repository hint relative to the authoritative Markdown document for both metadata lookup and link activation. - Open the commit using the existing multi-diff implementation, preserving normal Git diff behavior, including root commits. - Support local and forge commit links; forge links must match the hinted repository's remote. - Open a hinted repository through the Git extension when necessary and require workspace trust for newly opened repositories. - Report invalid or missing repository hints explicitly instead of silently falling back to an unrelated repository. ## Completion Implemented by #341570, **Show rich commit metadata and open path-hinted commits in multi-diff**, merged on 2026-10-14. This is a retrospective tracking issue for that completed work. The PR records 11 focused extension-host tests, extension build, renderer type-check, lint, and hygiene validation. It also records a live dbgjs/Code OSS test showing real commit metadata and the native multi-diff editor with three changed files. ## Story Part of #342050: link-addressable document/commit sinks, useful rich link sources, and consistent activation semantics.

title: Add Copy Link for Agent Host chat editor tabs
text: Add Copy Link for Agent Host chat editor tabs. ## Feature Add **Copy Link** to Agent Host chat editor tab context menus so users can share or revisit the exact session or peer chat through a stable link. This supplies a chat link source for the consistent-navigation story #342050. ## Expected behavior - Right-click a chat editor tab and choose **Copy Link**. - Copy a session/chat URL supported by rich session/chat pills and the session-link opener, rather than an editor UI resource or external product-launch URL. - Preserve backend session identity, connection authority, and the selected peer chat. - Support inactive tabs and multiple selected tabs, copying one unique URL per line. - Wait for pending provisional identities; report unavailable/uncreated sessions without changing the clipboard. - Keep the command consistent with AI-feature availability and accessibility help. ## Completion Implemented by #341095, **Add Copy Link to Agent Host chat editor context menus**, merged on 2026-10-13. This issue is created retrospectively to track that completed deliverable in the navigation story. The PR includes seven focused regression tests and recorded build, lint, hygiene, and 13 focused test passes. Its description notes that the new menu entry was not exercised end-to-end in an updated UI build during that work. Related: #342050 (story), #342119 (honor side-opening intent for agent-session link targets).

title: Support links that open a pull request directly in its multi diff view
text: Support links that open a pull request directly in its multi diff view. ## Feature request Support a shareable link that opens a GitHub pull request directly in its **multi diff view in VS Code**, showing the PR's changed files together, rather than requiring navigation through the PR overview first. Part of microsoft/vscode#342050 (the general link-navigation story). ## Motivation When sharing a PR in chat or a markdown document, it should be possible to link directly to the review surface showing all of its changes. The recipient should not have to open the PR overview and then manually find the action to open its multi diff view. ## Proposed behavior - Provide a supported link format that identifies a GitHub repository and PR and explicitly targets its multi diff view. - Make it easy to obtain/copy this link from the PR or its multi diff view. - Opening the link resolves the PR and opens its changed files in a multi diff editor without requiring an intermediate PR overview. - Integrate with the shared link-opening infrastructure so links can be followed from chat and markdown, and from direct link input in Ctrl+P once supported (#342051). - Honor placement intent: Alt+click opens the multi diff view beside the originating panel/editor group and keeps the source visible (see #340724). - Preserve ordinary GitHub PR link behavior; targeting the multi diff view should be explicit, or selected through shared handler preferences rather than unconditionally changing all PR links. - Give clear feedback if the repository/PR cannot be accessed or the required handler is unavailable. The concrete URI format and handler registration can be decided during implementation; this request is for a supported direct-link capability, not a specific URI scheme. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Copy a direct multi diff link for a PR and place it in a chat or markdown document. 2. Follow it: the intended PR's multi diff editor opens directly. 3. Alt+click it: the multi diff editor opens beside the originating view without replacing that view. 4. Existing PR overview links continue to work as before. Assigned to for the PR/multi diff link sink.

title: Support opening links directly from Quick Open (Ctrl+P)
text: Support opening links directly from Quick Open (Ctrl+P). ## Feature request Allow Quick Open (Ctrl+P) to accept a supported link directly and open its target using VS Code's link-handling infrastructure. Part of #342050. ## Motivation A copied link should be a usable navigation input, not something that first has to be pasted into a document or chat to become actionable. This should work with the views that can handle that link, rather than assuming every input is a file-name query or every URL belongs in an external browser. ## Proposed behavior - Recognize supported links entered or pasted into Ctrl+P and offer a clear action to open the target. - Use the shared link-handler resolution/defaults, including contributed handlers where applicable. - Provide a discoverable keyboard open-to-side action, equivalent to the story's Alt+click intent. Place the target beside the editor group from which Quick Open was invoked, preserving that view. - Preserve navigation context encoded in the link where supported by the selected handler. - Keep existing file-search and Quick Open prefix behavior intact; recognize links without broadly reinterpreting ordinary search text. - Give clear feedback for invalid or unsupported links rather than silently opening the wrong target. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Paste a supported link into Ctrl+P and open it in the appropriate view. 2. Use the open-to-side action for the same input: the target opens beside the originating view, which remains visible. 3. When multiple handlers match, honor shared selection/default behavior rather than introducing a separate Ctrl+P-specific routing policy. 4. Existing file-name searches and Quick Open prefixes continue to work. Exact link detection and interaction details can be refined in this issue; the shared handler-selection infrastructure is tracked by the parent story.

title: [Story] Consistent link navigation: Alt+click, link sources and sinks, and handler selection
text: [Story] Consistent link navigation: Alt+click, link sources and sinks, and handler selection. ## Story Make links a consistent navigation mechanism across VS Code: users should be able to follow a link from different surfaces, open it beside the originating view with Alt+click, and easily choose or change the view that handles it. Alt+click is the visible gesture, but the story spans three areas: link sources, link sinks, and opening/handling infrastructure. ## 1. Improve link sources Make links actionable with consistent navigation semantics from: - The markdown editor. - Chat messages and responses. - Quick Open (Ctrl+P): accept a link directly as input, not just file names, and offer to open its target. Alt+click should open beside the originating panel/editor group without replacing it. Keyboard-only entry points such as Ctrl+P should offer an equivalent open-to-side action with a discoverable shortcut. Sources should preserve the target and navigation intent when delegating to a handler. ## 2. Improve link sinks Support useful destinations and views for links, including: - Documents, including relevant locations/selections where represented by the link. - Chats. - Multi diff editors: direct PR multi diff links tracked in #342075 (assigned to ). - GitHub PR views. Each supported sink should honor the opening intent, including opening to the side, rather than silently replacing the originating view. Define the supported link forms and navigation context for each destination as part of its focused work item. ## 3. Improve link opening and handling in general Separate two decisions: 1. **Placement:** open here or to the side of the originating panel/editor group. 2. **Handler:** which matching view renders the target. When multiple views can handle the same link: - Make the available handlers and the current/default choice easy to discover. - Make it easy to configure which view handles that kind of link, with a clear scope for the preference. - Make it easy to switch the current target to another matching view, for example through a status bar item. - Preserve the target, navigation context, and placement intent when changing handlers where supported. Define predictable fallback behavior for unsupported targets or unavailable handlers. Avoid turning ordinary link navigation into a mandatory picker on every click. ## Current support (code inventory, not yet validated end to end — see #342545) | Target | Link forms | Rich presentation | Opens in VS Code | Open to side | |---|---|---|---|---| | Agent session / peer chat | | ✅ chat + Agents window ( ) | ✅ editor window + Agents window openers | ✅ (session pills in chat tool results, #342119) | | Git commit | , /-/commit/<sha> ?path= git.viewCommit` (multi diff). Elsewhere: no opener; https goes to the browser | ❌ | | GitHub issue / PR / repo | ` repo root | ✅ core GitHub provider (status, checks) | ❌ no core opener; browser/external opener (GitHub PR extension not verified) | ❌ | | Workspace file | , , , relative paths | ✅ Markdown editor ( ) | ✅ text editor (generic opener) | partial (depends on source) | | Folder | folder inside the workspace | — | ✅ Reveal in Explorer; OS file manager in the Agents window | n/a | | Web URL | | — | ✅ external openers: Integrated Browser, Simple Browser (localhost) | n/a | | Copilot CLI session | | ❌ | ❌ no opener found | ❌ | | Commit via | — | — | ❌ the Git URL handler only supports | — | Gaps: commit links outside the Markdown editor, GitHub issue/PR sinks, links, and in chat Markdown links ( does not pass it). ## Success criteria - Alt+click opens a supported target beside the originating view and keeps that view visible. - Placement is relative to the source, not an unrelated previously active editor group; reuse an appropriate adjacent group where possible. - Ordinary-click behavior remains unchanged unless explicitly addressed by a focused work item. - Opening intent works end to end across the sources and sinks listed above, including contributed/custom editors. - Ctrl+P can open a supported link supplied directly as input, including via its open-to-side action. - Users can discover matching handlers, choose a default, and switch the current target's view without reconstructing the link. - Links in the Markdown editor and chat expose their target and applicable opening gestures on hover, with richer target-specific information where supported. ## Breakdown Use focused sub-issues rather than implementing this as one large change: - Direct link input and opening in Ctrl+P. - End-to-end link support audit and compatibility matrix, including sessions and commit multi-diff routing: #342545. - Copy Link for Agent Host chat editor tabs: #342121 (completed in #341095). - Consistent Copy Link in editor tab context menus: #342551. - Chat Copy Link active-editor restriction: #342552 (separate follow-up to #342121). - Cross-surface Alt+click sub-story (Markdown, chat, GitHub issue/PR views, and shared webview handling investigation): #340724. - Link hover support in the Markdown editor and chat: #342543. - Link-addressable sinks for documents, chats, multi diff editors, and GitHub PR views, split as needed. - Rich Git commit metadata and path-hinted commit links opening in multi-diff: #342125 (completed in #341570). - Agent-session links honoring open-to-side requests in editor windows: #342119 (implementation: #342109). - Quick Pick listing available link handlers: #342544. - Integrated Browser as an external URI opener, so one place picks the opener and Quick Open lists it: #342934 (builds on #342544). - Shared handler selection/default configuration. - Discoverable switching between matching views: #342544 (including exploring a temporary status bar action for approximately 20 seconds with a slow fadeout, and/or Ctrl+Alt+click / Ctrl+Alt+Enter to open the handler Quick Pick). ### Existing related work - #340724: Alt+click links to open beside the originating panel (open). - #340725: Alt+click in the breadcrumbs dropdown (closed as completed); related work to align with, not a new request to duplicate. This story tracks the end-to-end experience and cross-surface consistency; focused issues should own the individual deliverables.

title: Improve editor tab scrollbar placement
text: Improve editor tab scrollbar placement. # Improve editor tab scrollbar placement VScode version: 1.142.0 OS version: MacOS ## Problem When multiple editor tabs are open, the horizontal scrollbar appears along the top edge of the tab bar, visually overlapping the area occupied by the tab headers. This makes the tab bar look less clean and reduces the visual separation between the scrollbar and the tabs themselves. ## Current behavior When the number of open tabs exceeds the available width, the scrollbar is displayed directly above the tab headers, as shown in the attached VS Code screenshot. Although the scrollbar serves its purpose, its placement introduces an additional visual element into an already dense navigation area. ## Why this matters - **Visual hierarchy:** The scrollbar competes with the tab headers for visual attention. - **Visual consistency:** The line disrupts the clean appearance of the tab bar, particularly when tabs have distinct backgrounds, borders, or rounded corners. - **Interaction clarity:** Placing the scrollbar so close to the tab headers may make the two controls feel visually connected, potentially causing confusion when interacting with them. - **Overall polish:** The tab bar feels less cohesive when many files are open, which is a common workflow for developers. ## Proposed improvement Consider placing the scrollbar in a dedicated area that does not visually overlap or interfere with the tab headers. Alternatively, explore a tab-scrolling design that keeps the scrollbar visually separate from the tab bar. The goal is not to remove tab scrolling, but to preserve the visual integrity of the tabs while maintaining convenient navigation between open editors. ## Reference The attached JetBrains IDE screenshot illustrates an alternative approach to tab navigation, where the tab headers retain a clearer visual separation from the scrolling mechanism. This is intended as a UX reference rather than a request to replicate the exact implementation. ## Expected result - Tab headers retain their visual integrity and clear boundaries. - The scrollbar does not visually interfere with tab labels or tab shapes. - Scrolling between open tabs remains intuitive and accessible. - The overall tab bar feels cleaner and more visually consistent. ## Screenshots

title: Agent Host: provide optional sandbox trusted CA setup and management
text: Agent Host: provide optional sandbox trusted CA setup and management. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> ## Problem and motivation Agent Host sandboxing uses the Copilot runtime's credential proxy. Some tools running inside a sandbox rely on the operating system's certificate trust store rather than the per-process certificate bundle supplied by the runtime. Those tools can need the sandbox proxy's certificate authority (CA) to be trusted on the machine running the agent host. VS Code currently lacks a discoverable, host-aware workflow for checking and managing that trust. A user can encounter certificate-related tool failures without knowing which certificate is involved, whether installing it is relevant, or whether the affected trust store is on this computer or a remote agent host. Manually running CLI setup can also target a different runtime or machine from the active VS Code chat. The CLI/runtime already provides the underlying CA lifecycle APIs. VS Code should reuse those APIs, not implement its own certificate generation, platform-specific trust-store scripts, or file deletion. This is specifically the **sandbox credential-proxy CA**, not general corporate CA configuration, TLS-verification bypass, or an instruction to disable sandboxing. ## Why installation must remain optional An uninstalled CA is not the same as a missing required sandbox dependency. Runtime-provided per-process certificate bundles remain useful, and not every tool or credential configuration requires OS trust. Checking the CA must not block chat startup, message sending, or sandbox operation, and merely opening a chat must never install, rotate, or remove a CA. Installing a CA changes trust on the selected agent host and can affect other chats using the same runtime. It must be an explicit, informed user action with the target host identified. ## Proposed experience - Check relevance, platform support, and CA status asynchronously through an already-running SDK runtime. - When the focused chat has a relevant, installable, untrusted CA, show a dismissible informational notice in the existing sandbox notification area: - **Sandbox trusted CA is not installed** - **Some tools running in this session's sandbox may need a trusted certificate on the agent host. Install** - Keep required dependency warnings higher priority. Do not offer Disable Sandboxing merely because the optional CA is not trusted. - Provide one discoverable Command Palette entry: **Sandbox: Manage Trusted CA**, with **Install**, **Rotate**, and **Remove** choices. - Use the last-focused chat's agent host, including after the notice is dismissed. Capture that target before opening the picker; a later focus change must not silently redirect an operation. - Use brief, host-naming confirmations, visible progress, and explicit errors. - With no applicable agent-host connection/controller, show **No agent host detected.** - Support keyboard navigation, cancellation, and discovery through Chat Accessibility Help. ## Operation semantics | Choice | Expected behavior | | --- | --- | | Install | Create/trust the CA, replacing an incompatible CA when needed. Already-compatible trusted CAs are a no-op. | | Rotate | Explicitly replace the installed CA and private key and establish trust for the replacement. Running tools may need to restart. | | Remove | Remove OS trust only. Retain the stored CA and private key. Tools relying on OS trust may stop working. | The current SDK has no delete/purge operation for the stored CA. Removal must not be described as deleting certificate files. ## Architecture and reliability requirements - Share in-flight and completed checks by SDK runtime and relevant credential configuration; do not repeat checks for each chat or message. - Bound status reads, cache explicit failures, and never interpret an error or unsupported state as "not installed." - Publish per-chat status through ordinary session snapshots and , using optional, validated, versioned metadata keyed by the host-advertised chat URI. - Preserve the local host-control boundary: local desktop CA mutations use trusted Management IPC; remote mutations use independently advertised, VS Code-specific AHP extension capabilities. - Do not assume a remote host supports rotation/removal because it supports installation. - Revalidate the connection, chat, and runtime scope after confirmation. Reject stale targets and serialize mutations per runtime. - Invalidate cached observations around operations and refresh live chats after both success and failure. - Do not start or restore a runtime solely to perform a CA mutation. - Keep AI-disabled visibility and existing managed sandbox behavior intact; no additional installation setting or policy is needed. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Missing, relevant CA trust is explained without blocking chat or treating it as a required sandbox dependency. - [ ] A single management command exposes all three operations and continues to work after notice dismissal. - [ ] Local and remote actions reach the selected chat's owning host through the appropriate authorized transport. - [ ] Cancellation, duplicate invocation, focus changes, disposal, disconnects, and runtime replacement cannot produce an unintended mutation. - [ ] SDK outcomes are validated before reporting success. - [ ] Removal clearly means OS-trust removal, not deletion. - [ ] Unit tests cover cache/lifecycle behavior, metadata transport, capabilities/ownership, operation arguments/results, and accessible UI behavior. - [ ] A UI demo documents the notice and management flow; live OS authorization and platform trust-store behavior are validated separately. ## Related work Related to #337535 (interactive installation of required Agent Host sandbox prerequisites), but deliberately separate: optional credential-proxy CA trust must not be conflated with the prerequisites required to enable sandboxing.

title: Polish guided model comparison setup and results
text: Polish guided model comparison setup and results. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> ## Feature request Polish the guided model comparison (Agent Bake Off) workflow so configuring attempts and reviewing the Judge result is stable, responsive, and easy to scan. ## Proposed behavior - Select attempt models with checkboxes and complete each setup step with clear Done/Next actions. - Keep the picker anchored and stable while models, effort variants, and Details configuration change. - Allow the same model to run as distinct attempts with different supported configurations, while preventing duplicate effective configurations. - Keep committed comparison state valid when a model's persisted base configuration changes. - Identify comparison attempts consistently in the composer, with responsive icon treatment in expanded, compact, and minimal layouts. - Present the Judge result as an Attempt/Time/Tokens scorecard with visible winner badges where space permits. - Keep rationale and validation evidence in expandable attempt details, including keyboard-accessible evidence source and purpose. - Provide direct Open Attempt actions for every result row and retain complete Accessible View content. ## Verification 1. Enable and open the model picker in the Agents window. 2. Start Compare Models, select multiple distinct models, and verify the list updates in place without the popup moving or resizing unexpectedly. 3. Add a second attempt of one model at another effort, change the base effort, and verify duplicate effective attempts are removed. Cancel and reopen setup to verify committed state remains valid. 4. Complete setup with and without Judge/Synthesizer choices, then run the comparison. 5. In the Judge result, verify Attempt, Time, and Tokens stay aligned; wide layouts show metric Winner badges and narrow layouts do not overlap adjacent values or Open actions. 6. Expand attempts and verify rationale, validation status, validation evidence hover/focus behavior, and Open Attempt actions. 7. Resize the composer through expanded, compact, and minimal states. Distinct attempts show individual icons when expanded and the layers fallback when compact/minimal; repeated-model variants keep an identifiable summary. 8. Exercise the workflow with keyboard navigation and the Accessible View. ## Accessibility - Setup remains fully keyboard operable. - Expanded validation evidence is focusable and exposes its source and purpose from the keyboard. - Metric winner meaning remains in row accessible labels when visual badges are hidden. - Comparison result content remains available in the Accessible View.

title: Extension API: conditional WorkspaceConfiguration.update (write only if the value still equals an expected value)
text: Extension API: conditional WorkspaceConfiguration.update (write only if the value still equals an expected value). ## Use case An extension shows its own settings page (a webview) for settings the user can also change elsewhere: in , in the Settings editor, through Settings Sync, or from another window. When the page saves, it should write only if the setting still holds the value the page last showed. Otherwise it should keep the newer value and show the user a conflict. ## Current behaviour always writes. An extension can call first, but another writer can change the value between that read and the write. That writer can be the user editing , Settings Sync, another window or another extension. Its newer value is then overwritten without any signal. fires only after the fact. All the extension can do is detect the overwrite and try to put the value back, and that putback races in the same way. The closest earlier report is #134803: two extensions overwrote each other's update to the same setting. It was closed as a question; the answer was that updates go through a queue and the last write wins. Locking inside the extension doesn't help here, because the other writers (the user, Settings Sync, other windows) never take part in an extension's lock. ## Request An optional precondition on that the configuration service checks when it applies the write from its queue. For example: An alternative would work just as well: a per-target version or etag returned by and accepted by . ## Minimal reproduction Steps: run the snippet from a command, then edit during the 5-second wait. ## Why it matters Any extension with its own settings UI, any extension that keeps a setting in sync with outside state, and any pair of extensions that cooperate on one setting all hit this race. With a precondition on the write they could stop guessing.

title: [Story] Consistent Alt+click link opening across VS Code surfaces
text: [Story] Consistent Alt+click link opening across VS Code surfaces. ## Feature request Support **Alt+click to open a link in an editor to the side of the current panel/editor group**, leaving the originating view visible. ## Motivation When exploring links in a chat response, opening a linked resource in the same editor group can replace the response being used as context. For example, clicking a GitHub issue link in a chat response can open the issue editor in place of the chat. It should be possible to explicitly open the linked resource beside the source instead. ## Proposed behavior - Support links in Markdown files rendered in the Markdown editor, as well as links in chat messages and responses. - Alt+click on a link opens its target in an editor group to the side of the group containing the clicked link. - Keep the originating panel/view visible and unchanged. - Reuse an appropriate adjacent editor group where possible instead of creating another split on every click. - Preserve ordinary-click behavior. - Propagate the side-opening intent through link handlers and contributed openers, including targets rendered as webview/custom editors, such as GitHub issue editors. - Leave external-browser-only targets unaffected when they cannot be opened inside VS Code. The placement should be relative to the view containing the clicked link, not an unrelated previously active editor group. ## Example With a chat response containing a GitHub issue link visible, Alt+click the issue. The issue opens in an editor beside the chat, so both the response and the issue remain visible. ## Cross-surface task checklist This story tracks consistent Alt+click link opening across sources, routing infrastructure, and destinations. Split implementation into focused sub-issues as needed. - [ ] Support Alt+click on links in the Markdown editor. - [ ] Support Alt+click on links in chat messages and responses. - [ ] Support Alt+click on links inside GitHub issue and PR views. Reported behavior: Alt+click currently does not open these links to the side; not yet independently reproduced for this story. This concerns those views as link sources, not only as destinations. - [ ] Investigate generic webview link handling: determine whether a shared anchor-click/link-opening bridge can preserve modifier keys, the originating view/editor group, and explicit side-opening intent. Identify extension-specific click handlers or message bridges that still need changes rather than assuming a generic host change covers all webviews. - [ ] Propagate side-opening intent end to end through contributed openers and custom editors, including already-open targets. Use the completed agent-session work in #342119 (implementation: #342109) as related coverage, not proof that every handler is fixed. - [ ] Add cross-surface regression coverage: placement relative to the source, adjacent-group reuse, keeping the source visible, unchanged ordinary-click behavior, and unaffected external-browser-only targets. Coordinate exact link forms and expected/actual results with #342545. ## Tracking - Parent link-navigation story: #342050. - End-to-end link support audit and compatibility matrix: #342545. - Related completed work: #340725 (breadcrumbs Alt+click), #342119 (agent-session side opening).

title: Chat context-usage widget cannot be fed by third-party language-model providers (no usage surface on the provider path)
text: Chat context-usage widget cannot be fed by third-party language-model providers (no usage surface on the provider path). <!-- ⚠️ Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> - VS Code Version: 1.106.x (Insiders stable line, October 2026) - OS: macOS **Repro (any extension that registers models via the proposed API):** 1. An extension registers a language model provider ( , proposed ). 2. The user picks one of its models in the chat panel and sends a chat request. 3. The provider's response stream yields s (and a with mimeType carrying ). 4. The chat panel's context-usage widget (the bar showing "X% of context used" / tokens used of the model's window) stays hidden/empty — no per-response token usage is ever displayed. **Expected:** there should be a supported way for a language-model provider to report the actual token usage (prompt/completion) it observed, so the chat context-usage widget can display it — the same way chat participants can today. ## What the current build actually does (evidence from the shipped bundle) 1. **The widget reads only.** computes over the model's , and hides when is unset. 2. ** has exactly three feeders:** - when the progress chunk is ; - the agent-host progress-chunk handler, same shape; - the session-restore path (persisted / fields). 3. **The only extension-host producer of a progress chunk is ** — i.e. a *chat participant* response stream, gated on the proposed API. A *language-model provider* has no equivalent: there is no -shaped progress, no field on , and nothing in the proposal that carries usage. (Grep of the shipped and the stable d.ts: zero usage-surface hits.) 4. **The only consumer that decodes a with mimeType is the agent-host BYOK path** ( , service , channel ). It parses exactly out of the data part, returns it over the agent-host protocol to the node side, where the BYOK loopback proxy folds it into the Responses-API usage — which then reaches and the widget. So for agent-host sessions with BYOK models, an in-band usage data part works end-to-end. 5. **On the plain panel path, that data part is silently dropped.** The default chat agent consumes the provider stream, but its handling of s only covers , , images, and PDFs (history filtering / request re-serialization). mimeType is never decoded there — and the default agent's own token accounting comes from parsing usage out of *its own* raw API responses, which a third-party provider's stream never contains. ## Net effect - Third-party extensions (this is how e.g. internal gateway-backed model providers register) can never feed the context-usage widget on the normal panel path — the widget silently shows nothing. - The agent-host BYOK path already demonstrates the intended in-band contract (a data part with the payload), so the decode-side machinery exists; it is just not wired for the plain panel/participant path. ## Asks Either would resolve this: 1. **Provider-side surface:** let (or a -proposal extension of it) carry usage — e.g. accept a with mimeType on the provider stream and populate from it, mirroring what already does on the agent-host path; or 2. **Participant-side fallback:** document/wire a supported way for the default panel flow to surface provider-reported usage (e.g. the default agent forwarding a data part as progress when present). Concrete extension context: our extension registers an internal LiteLLM-gateway model set via and already emits the data part (with the exact payload shape the BYOK decoder expects). It renders the counts on our own output channel, but the panel widget cannot consume it.

title: API Proposal: Support Custom Native Floating Modal Dialogs for Complex Data Workflows
text: API Proposal: Support Custom Native Floating Modal Dialogs for Complex Data Workflows. ### Problem Statement & Use Case We are migrating complex developer tooling from Eclipse RCP to VS Code extensions. We have encountered a major layout and workflow blocker regarding advanced user input and data validation. In Eclipse RCP, the architecture allows launching modal frames to handle heavy data orchestration (e.g., database schema mapping, multi-row environment setups, and complex multi-field forms) without breaking the user's active editor split layouts. Currently, VS Code offers no viable alternative for dense, non-linear data collection: * : Highly restrictive. It only displays static strings and buttons; it cannot collect complex user input. * / Multi-step InputBox: Built for linear selection. It completely fails when workflows require structural matrices, multi-column tables, cross-field validation, or complex form controls. * (Editor Tabs): Opening a full-sized tab for a transient 10-second task disorients the user's layout, breaks active editor splits, and introduces a messy tab lifecycle management overhead. ### Proposed Solution We propose an API extension such as —that allows extensions to spawn a temporary modal overlay surface over the workbench: * **True Modality:** Blocks interaction with the underlying workbench layout until explicitly submitted or cancelled to guarantee data sequence integrity. * **Floating & Centered:** Container floats centered over the active VS Code window (similar to native OS message boxes). * **Webview Driven:** Powered by standard sandboxed Webview HTML/JS, allowing developers to build custom data grids, checkboxes, validation logic, and input fields safely. * **Transient Lifecycle:** Exists entirely outside the editor tab bar, managed explicitly by the extension backend or user actions ( / Close buttons).

title: Support expiring GitHub tokens with the offline_access scope
text: Support expiring GitHub tokens with the offline_access scope. GitHub sessions only expire today when they're brokered through Microsoft Entra (#335183). Those sessions report and renew themselves before they run out. Ordinary GitHub OAuth sessions are stored in the keychain with no known expiry, and nothing ever renews them. The GitHub Authentication extension should support expiring GitHub tokens for those sessions too, by requesting the scope. With , sign-in returns an access token that expires plus a refresh token. The extension would: - store the refresh token next to the session - report the access token's remaining lifetime through - renew the access token before it expires, the same way Entra-brokered sessions renew today The renewal path in ( ) only handles transient Entra-brokered sessions. It will need to give persisted sessions their own expiry and branch on how a given session renews. Related: #335183, #335184

title: Agent Host: send_message should replace its unacknowledged queued message with an up-to-date one
text: Agent Host: send_message should replace its unacknowledged queued message with an up-to-date one. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> When one session messages another with and the target chat is busy, every call adds another queued message. If the sender follows up before the target has started the first one, the target ends up with a stack of separate, unacknowledged messages from the same sender. Each becomes its own turn, and the earlier ones are usually out of date by the time they run. ## Proposal When sessions talk to each other, the sender should read the most up-to-date state and keep one complete, current message in the target, not a stack of unread updates: - The sender can read its own undelivered message, including any edits made to it while it waited, before sending again (for example, through ). - Sending again before the target has started that message replaces it with one complete message that reflects the current state, not just what changed. The message keeps its ID, its place in the queue, and its model. - The result returns the text that was replaced, so the sender can tell whether anything it still needs was dropped. - Once the target has started the message, which acknowledges it, the next message is queued as a new one. ## Related: queued cross-session messages show "Auto" in the model picker When you edit a queued message that another session sent, the model picker shows **Auto** instead of the target session's model. It should show that session's model, so if the session's picker shows Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M, the edit should show Opus 5.5 · xHigh · 1M too. This is more than a display problem. Saving the edit as Auto switches the chat's model when the message is delivered, and switching models breaks the prompt cache. Queued messages from other sessions should run on whatever model the target chat is already using, without switching it, and editing a request that has no recorded model should start on the conversation's current model. Related: #334459 (queue messages sent to a busy chat), #335540 (use steering for inter-session messages)

title: Dictation cleanup: allow any chat model available to the user/organization instead of a hard-coded model ID
text: Dictation cleanup: allow any chat model available to the user/organization instead of a hard-coded model ID. **Use case** In organizations on Copilot Business/Enterprise, admins decide which models are available, and users only get that subset. Dictation cleanup, however, can only use one hard-coded "good" model ( ). If that model is not offered to an organization, every user there silently falls back to . There is no way to choose another model that the organization *does* allow and that the same user already uses in chat every day. **What happened to us** Between 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-28, dictation cleanup stopped using Luna, although is still . is no longer offered to my account/organization (Copilot Business). Our model list now contains instead. I cannot tell whether the model was retired globally or is just not enabled for our organization. Either way, the result for the user is the same. **Why settings cannot fix it:** is hard-coded in three places: - the setting enum ( ) - in - the Copilot alias , which resolves the CAPI family Any other value is silently replaced with . **Request:** allow to take the ID of any chat model that is user-selectable for the current user, i.e. what their organization has enabled, for example . From #332969 I understand that the dedicated cleanup aliases are intentionally core-only. This request leaves them as they are. It only asks to accept models the user is already allowed to use in chat. This would also respect organization model policies by design, and model retirements would no longer need a code change. **Nice to have:** when the configured model is unavailable, show a visible hint, not only an info line in the log. **Environment:** VS Code 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1), built-in Copilot extension 0.67.0, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Copilot Business, = Nemotron (local), = .

title: MCP: Allow users to disable all workspace servers while keeping user servers enabled
text: MCP: Allow users to disable all workspace servers while keeping user servers enabled. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. --> ## Problem VS Code can discover MCP servers from workspace/repository configuration ( and ) as well as user-level configuration. I want a user-controlled way to disable every workspace-origin MCP server while keeping my user/global MCP servers available. Today, I can disable workspace servers individually or disable MCP access entirely, but I cannot exclude the workspace configuration source as a class. This is useful when I want my trusted personal MCP set without automatically adding tools declared by each repository. ## Proposed behavior Add a user-controlled setting or enablement action that: - Excludes all workspace/repository MCP servers. - Keeps user/global MCP servers enabled. - Can default workspace MCP servers off globally, with explicit opt-in for trusted workspaces. - Is stored outside repository-controlled settings, so a workspace cannot re-enable its own MCP servers. - Applies consistently to both the local harness and Agent Host-based harnesses. - Is visible and reversible in the MCP/Agent Customizations UI. For example, this could be represented as a user preference such as , or as a scoped enablement decision in the existing MCP enablement model. The exact setting shape is not important. ## Related work - #329475 requests the inverse: a workspace can exclude all user-level MCP servers and keep only workspace servers. - #329478 proposes for that inverse case. - #254931 tracks per-server enable/disable at user/workspace scope, but not bulk exclusion by configuration origin. - #330566 introduced scoped MCP enablement decisions ( ) that may provide a foundation. - #337335 requests all MCP servers default-off with per-workspace opt-in; this request is narrower because user/global MCP servers should remain enabled. - github/copilot-cli#3380 requests an analogous option for Copilot CLI.

title: Agents window: colored session groups and collections
text: Agents window: colored session groups and collections. ## Problem The Agents window sessions list is hard to scan. Custom groups, workspace sections, Pinned, and Chats all render as the same grey text, so with a lot of sessions it reads as a wall of grey and groups don't stand out. To work around this today, I create empty custom groups named , , and as visual dividers between engineering, personal, and miscellaneous work. Browsers already solve both problems: - **Colored tab groups:** a solid colored header, and a colored rail on the tabs inside. A collapsed group is a small color pill. - **Workspaces:** separate sets of groups and tabs (for example, personal vs. two work contexts) that you switch between with an icon strip. This exploration brings both ideas to the sessions list. ## Exploration | | | | --- | --- | | **Interactive mockup** | (Dark, [Light]( [High contrast]( | | **Walkthrough video** | | | **Mockup source** | (a Component Explorer fixture built from real VS Code components) | | **Implementation branch** | [ ]( ([compare]( | ![Interactive mockup: colored groups and collections in the Agents window]( ## Proposal | Area | Behavior | | --- | --- | | **Colored groups** | Every custom group has a color: a named palette color (grey, blue, red, yellow, green, pink, purple, cyan, orange) or a custom hex. New groups get the next unused color. The default **Rail** style shows a colored header pill, plus a colored rail next to the group's sessions. | | **Readable labels** | The label color on a colored header is picked automatically (light or dark, whichever has the higher WCAG contrast), and can be forced to light or dark. | | **Collapsed groups** | A collapsed group is a compact pill with a session count and its most urgent status: needs input, then in progress, then unread. | | **Workspace and built-in sections** | Workspace sections, **Pinned**, and **Chats** can optionally be colored too. Uncolored sections look the same as today. Pinned and Chats can only be recolored: they keep their names and their place in the list. | | **Collections** | User-defined sets of groups, workspaces, and sessions, like browser workspaces, for example Engineering / Personal / Misc. Each has a name, a codicon, and a color, and the list shows only the active collection. You switch collections with an icon strip or the Sessions header menu; each collection remembers its last open session. To move sessions, groups, or workspaces to another collection, drag them onto its icon or use **Move to Collection**. With a single collection, the list works as it does today. The name "Collections" avoids a clash with the existing meaning of "workspace" in VS Code. | | **Editing** | Hover actions, F2, and context menus open an editor with a name field, color swatches, an optional custom color picker, the text color (Auto / Light / Dark), and a live contrast preview. Every change can be undone. | | **Theming** | Palette colors are theme tokens with dark, light, and high contrast defaults, and only standard codicons are used. The window frame doesn't change color with the collection. | The mockup also compares other group styles (**Outline**, **Tint**, **Dot**), a compact density, and other places for the collection switcher (sidebar tabs, or the header menu only). ## Status The mockup is complete and published. The implementation branch is in progress and not ready for review yet. So far it has: - services for header colors and collections, with profile-scoped persistence; - colored groups and sections in the sessions list; - the collection switcher and navigation; - a update covering the new list state. ## Open questions - [ ] Rail as the default group style, or one of the alternatives? - [ ] Where the collection switcher lives: the title bar strip, sidebar tabs, or only the Sessions header menu? - [ ] "Collections" as the name. - [ ] Should Pinned and Chats allow more than a color change (rename, move between collections)? - [ ] Should collections ship behind a setting at first?

title: Support versionless model-family aliases that select the newest model in custom agents
text: Support versionless model-family aliases that select the newest model in custom agents. ## Feature request Support versionless model-family names in the frontmatter of custom agent files ( ) so they resolve to the newest available model in that family. For example, a setting such as: would mean "use the newest available GPT Luna model from Copilot" instead of requiring the agent author to update a version-specific name after each model release. This is illustrative syntax; the request is for documented versionless aliases, not a claim about current resolution behavior. ## Motivation Maintaining multiple custom agents requires repeated edits when newer model versions become available. A stable family alias would let agent authors opt in to new versions without changing every agent file. ## Suggested behavior - A documented model-family name without a version number resolves to the newest stable version available to the current user from the specified provider. - An explicitly versioned name continues to pin that version. - Resolution stays within the selected model family and provider, rather than switching to an unrelated model. - Preview models are excluded unless explicitly requested. - The UI shows the concrete model selected by the alias. - If no matching model is available, show a clear message instead of silently selecting an unrelated model. ## Related request #297210 requests latest-model selection for prompt files. This request proposes versionless family aliases specifically for custom agent model configuration; the same convention could serve both file types.
